lessons.t: His core frameworks (the models he repeats most)
lessons.md:
## Core Frameworks

The models Alex Hormozi comes back to most often across all sources in this doc, summarized in my own words. The numbers after each one point to example sources in the Start here tab; the topic tabs have the detailed ideas.

## Offers & Pricing

- **Value Equation:** Value goes up with the dream outcome and how likely the buyer believes they are to get it, and goes down with how long it takes and how much effort or sacrifice it costs. Make the result bigger, more certain, faster and easier, then price against that value. (see #2, #14, #25, #31, #36, #77, #119, #194)
- **Grand Slam Offer:** Define the dream outcome, list every obstacle the customer hits on the way, turn each obstacle into a named solution, brainstorm many ways to deliver it, then trim to the high-value/low-cost pieces and stack them into one package so good it feels foolish to say no. (see #65, #144)
- **Enhancers: scarcity, urgency, bonuses, guarantees, naming:** Layer real limits (spots, cohorts, deadlines), bonuses that each solve a specific obstacle, and a strong guarantee that reverses risk. A good name makes the offer memorable and specific to who it is for. (see #3, #6, #8, #11, #26, #28, #31, #33)
- **Charge more, deliver more:** Price is a signal and a source of margin; premium pricing funds better fulfillment, better staff and more ad spend. If no one pushes back on price, it is probably too low. (see #13, #14, #15, #25, #28, #30, #34, #36)
- **Starving crowd and a narrow niche:** Pick a market with massive pain, the ability to pay, that is easy to target and growing. Narrow to one avatar so the message hits harder and the offer can be tailored. (see #2, #3, #6, #9, #13, #14, #17, #27)

## Lead Generation & Content

- **Core Four:** There are only four ways to let people know about you: warm outreach (people who know you), cold outreach, content, and paid ads. Later, lead getters (referrals, employees, agencies, affiliates) do these for you. (see #2, #6, #14, #17, #34, #36, #42, #65)
- **Rule of 100:** Do 100 primary advertising actions a day for 100 days: 100 outreach messages, 100 minutes of content, or $100 a day in ads. Judge yourself on the input, not early results. (see #2, #6, #18, #34, #65, #102, #121, #127)
- **Lead magnets:** Give away a complete solution to a narrow problem that naturally reveals the next problem your paid offer solves. It should be so good people would have paid for it. (see #3, #21, #76, #79, #82, #94, #107, #108)
- **Give away the secrets, sell the implementation:** Share your best ideas for free in content; people buy help implementing them. Content works through hook, retain, reward, and volume plus iteration beats perfection. (see #3, #15, #17, #25, #36, #62, #75, #78)
- **Speed to lead and follow-up:** Contact new leads within minutes and follow up persistently; many sales are lost simply because no one called back fast or often enough. (see #1, #8, #17, #31, #35, #40, #48, #62)

## Sales

- **CLOSER:** Clarify why they are here, Label the problem, Overview past attempts and pain, Sell the vacation (the outcome, not the process), Explain away concerns, Reinforce the decision after the purchase. (see #6, #17, #34, #35, #39, #53, #58, #90)
- **Objections are just obstacles:** Most objections come down to time, money, decision maker, fit or avoidance. Treat each as a problem to solve together rather than an argument to win, and handle common ones before they come up. (see #6, #33, #35, #39, #40, #55, #58, #59)
- **Volume of sales reps:** Skill comes from repetitions: thousands of conversations, daily role-play and reviewing recordings. Close rate improves with reps, not with more theory. (see #1, #9, #35, #39, #77, #89, #106, #107)

## Money Models & Unit Economics

- **LTGP to CAC:** Compare lifetime gross profit per customer with the cost to acquire one. Aim for at least 3:1, and more if parts of the business still depend on manual work. Improve the ratio by raising lifetime value or lowering acquisition cost. (see #9, #26, #36, #62, #106, #109, #126, #144)
- **Client-financed acquisition:** Design the first 30 days of a customer relationship so the cash collected pays for that customer's acquisition and delivery plus the next customer's acquisition. Then growth is no longer limited by capital. (see #6, #14, #25, #48, #50, #62, #115, #151)
- **Money models: attraction, upsell, downsell, continuity:** Sequence offers: an attractive front-end offer to get customers in, upsells and downsells right at the point of purchase, and continuity (recurring) offers to keep value and cash coming. (see #25, #34, #35, #36, #40, #55, #62, #79)
- **Retention and referrals before more leads:** Fix the leaky bucket before pouring more leads in: onboarding, quick early wins and consistent results reduce churn, and happy customers become the cheapest lead source. (see #2, #3, #6, #8, #9, #25, #26, #28)

## Scaling & Operations

- **More, Better, New:** To grow, first do more of what already works, then make it better, and only then try something new. New has a certain cost and an uncertain payoff. (see #17, #36, #127, #132, #148, #230)
- **Find the constraint:** At any time one thing limits growth (leads, sales capacity, delivery, cash or people). Identify it, fix it, and move on to the next one instead of improving everything at once. (see #3, #6, #21, #25, #36, #48, #53, #54)
- **Leverage over hard work:** Output equals volume times leverage. Grow by getting more from each unit of effort: better skills, tools, offers, systems, capital and other people's time. (see #1, #3, #9, #21, #22, #27, #31, #34)
- **Document, demonstrate, duplicate:** Turn what works into simple written processes and checklists, show people how, then have them do it and give feedback, so results don't depend on the founder. (see #3, #7, #14, #22, #34, #35, #39, #46)

## Hiring & Leadership

- **Hire for the bottleneck, pay for outcomes:** Hire people who remove your biggest constraint, interview many more candidates than feels necessary, and give them clear outcomes, scorecards and ownership. (see #2, #3, #4, #6, #9, #18, #19, #21)
- **Feedback and standards:** Give frequent, specific feedback; set the bar clearly and hold it. Most performance problems come from unclear expectations, missing skills or weak follow-through by the leader. (see #3, #6, #14, #17, #18, #19, #21, #23)

## Mindset & Discipline

- **Volume negates luck:** The more attempts you make, the more likely success becomes; most people stop far too early. Measure effort in inputs you control. (see #1, #2, #3, #4, #6, #7, #8, #9)
- **Focus: one thing, all in:** Saying no to good opportunities is how you win at the great one. Spreading attention across many projects is the most common reason small businesses stay small. (see #1, #2, #3, #4, #6, #9, #16, #18)
- **Patience and long time horizons:** Results compound over years, not months. Patience is a behavior (not quitting, not jumping ship), even when it doesn't feel calm inside. (see #1, #2, #7, #8, #9, #10, #12, #16)
- **Identity and beliefs:** Behavior follows identity. Act the way the person you want to become would act, collect evidence through repeated action, and challenge limiting beliefs by testing them. (see #8, #9, #18, #22, #33, #37, #51, #55)
- **Embrace boring discomfort:** The work that makes money is usually repetitive and uncomfortable; your ability to tolerate it is a competitive advantage. (see #1, #2, #15, #19, #45, #83, #113, #118)
- **Learning means changed behavior:** If you face the same situation and act the same way, you haven't learned. Apply what you consume immediately and judge learning by changed actions. (see #1, #6, #8, #11, #16, #18, #19, #22)

lessons.t: NEW 2026 · The best of his lives & podcasts (1146 ideas, 33 sources)
lessons.md:
> The newest layer of how he thinks, from his 2026 live streams, his four Modern Wisdom marathons, Diary of a CEO and Ed Mylett. Paraphrased notes in my words, with his framework names; every idea on the source pages links to the exact minute. Applied to you at the bottom.

## 1 · Courage is the trait that unlocks the others
- **Courage = taking action with a big short-term cost for an uncertain, delayed benefit.** If he could pass one trait to his son, it would be this. Better a failure than a coward.
- **Your potential = how much uncertainty you can tolerate × for how long.**
- **Beat 99% of people** by mastering three things: the shame of rejection, the boredom of repetition, the pain of feedback.
- **Fear lives in the vague, not the specific.** Write the failure out step by step (whose couch, what job, what week 1 looks like). It is rarely as bad on paper as in your head. → Tool: Mindset tab › 🧰 Use it › **Fear → specific**
- **Risk is mispriced.** In the developed world the downside of trying your hardest is close to nothing; the upside you skip is everything. Your brain prices risk for a world where one mistake meant death.

## 2 · Decide = cut off
- **Options only have value when exercised.** Keeping options open is delayed gratification that never pays out: the ant with a pile of crumbs it never ate.
- **The gap between potential and realised potential is the commitments you're willing to make.**
- **"Pick your regrets or they will be chosen for you."** Time is zero-sum; you will live an imperfect life. → Tool: Mindset tab › 🧰 Use it › **Pick your regrets**
- **Hard path vs easy path: pick the hard one.** If the easy one were right, you wouldn't be debating.
- **Two hard choices?** Ask "what do I want to have happen?" and "what problem am I solving?". Emotion lowers your action threshold; wanting to act ≠ the action works.
- **Push or pivot:** pivot only when a founding assumption is disproven by real feedback. Otherwise it's execution: push.
- **Write the decision document.** When doubt returns, reread it instead of re-deciding. → Tool: Mindset tab › 🧰 Use it › **Decision document**
- **Poverty loves indecision.** Inaction is an action against your priorities.

## 3 · Hard days
- **Hard times don't last; hard people do.** Moods are weather. Never take drastic action while feeling bad.
- **Hopelessness = a perceived lack of options → build capacity** (sleep, train, save, make content). **Anxiety = many options, no priority → a quest.**
- **The story frame:** this is the story you'll tell at 80; the bigger the dragon, the better the story. No epic hero without epic monsters.
- **Judge yourself by what you do despite how you feel**, not by how you feel.
- **On a sad day find the hidden expectation** you're demanding from life, and check if it's reasonable. Deserving is the opposite of gratitude: "I deserve nothing and I'm grateful for everything."
- **Change takes days, not years.** Do the scary thing 3 days in a row. Fear is a mile wide and an inch deep.
- **Tragedy + time = comedy**, so laugh now.

## 4 · Other people
- **No one is coming to save you, and no one is coming to stop you.**
- **Listen to people closest to your goals, not closest to you.** Their opinions are built on a few minutes of your life; yours on all of it.
- **Translate all hate into "you're living your life against my preferences."** Answer: yes.
- **Judge outputs, not intentions.** Well-intended harm still harms. Look at your "stats" since someone entered your life.
- **The lonely chapter:** too big for the old group, not yet in the new one. Everyone who did anything walked through it.
- **Friend test:** do they make me better, and do they want what's best for me?

## 5 · Work
- **Volume negates luck.** Roll the dice more: you only need one 20.
- **4–6 hours of truly focused work a day** (timer on, restart when you look away) beats most people. You compete with the couch and notifications, not with humans.
- **Do so much work it would be unreasonable to fail**, then you have nothing left to be nervous about. If you're nervous, do more reps.
- **No half measures:** half effort in four areas = zero outcomes.
- **The black dot room:** you won't willpower work into being interesting; remove the other dots.
- **Change your environment** to change your loops: new place, new gym, new café, pause the friends.
- **Make the right choice the easiest choice;** add friction to the wrong ones.
- **Master the boring middle:** the marathon is won between the start and the finish.

## 6 · Respect (POWERS / HEARTED)
- **Earn it, POWERS:** Pay the cost visibly · Outcomes improve when you're involved · Word kept · Enforce standards · Restraint · Steady under pressure.
- **Give it, HEARTED:** Honor their lines · Esteem them when absent · Attend (listen) · Reliable · Truth, even unwelcome · Expectations stay high · Defer in their expertise.
- **Enforce only when** they knew the standard, could meet it, and chose not to. About the behaviour, never the person. Consistent, immediate, escalating.

## 7 · Life & death
- **What happens when you die:** your things get divided, your life is summarised in a few paragraphs, everyone eats and goes to work. What you're worried about won't be in those paragraphs. Dare greatly or not at all.
- **Design a life you want to wake up to:** work that's interesting, people you'd hate to miss, long projects that matter.
- **The third marshmallow:** delay gratification, but not forever. Optimise joy per unit of time across a lifetime.
- **Be like the alligator** when something feels urgent: it hasn't eaten in four weeks and is fine.

## 8 · When life hits (mental toughness)
- **Four dials of toughness:** fortitude (how much hits you before you change), tolerance (how low you go), resilience (how fast you're back), adaptability (better or worse afterwards). He wrote it for himself after his mother died weeks after his biggest launch. → *Diagram: Mental toughness.*
- **"My emotional discomfort is not an adequate reason to change what I'm doing."** Change as little as possible; keep doing what makes you feel better (work, training, helping).
- **Bad days are statistics:** ~3 bottom-10% days a month for no reason. Don't quit, break up or pivot on one. A bad day where you still did good work is a good day.
- **Only suffer once.** Life shoots the first arrow; you shoot the second (reliving it, judging yourself). Memory dividends, not memory liabilities.
- **Seasons:** in a bad season, win the day; in some seasons maintaining is winning (Ackman: one bite a day, look back every 30–90 days).
- **Good mood without reasons** is the single greatest skill: if you can be in a bad mood for no reason, you can be in a good one. Decree it: "the rest of the year will be good."
- **The 85-year-old frame:** wake up as your 85-year-old self back in today's body. Today's problems look cute.

## 9 · Standards & reps
- **No silver bullet, 100 golden BBs.** The first 5 reps make you better; the next 95 make a masterpiece. → *Diagram.*
- **Real perfectionists finish;** fake ones procrastinate. Pick your battles: no compromise where leverage is highest, volume everywhere else.
- **Reset your minimum standard:** his rose a hundredfold (25-slide decks → 900 slides, 100 rehearsals). Measure work in hundreds of hours and hundreds of reps.
- **Win = nothing left to do.** "But I'll know" beats "what will they think?". With high standards, the only way to not always feel like a failure is to do fewer things all the way.
- **The kitchen timer:** set it, stop it the moment you check your phone. Time on task is far lower than you think.
- **First 6 hours of every day on what moves the needle.** No calls, no meetings. Starting is the perfect condition.
- **Learning = same condition, new behaviour.** Flat revenue for 6+ months while working all hours = you haven't learned.

## 10 · Building it (from the podcasts)
- **The fastest way to $10M isn't the fastest way to $100M.** The height of the tower decides the foundation. Focus and patience are the two lasting advantages because they're anti-human. → *Diagram: the tower.*
- **Keep the customers you get.** Company A keeps its 100 a year; B churns them and must sell 600 next year. One product, one avatar, one channel to $1–3M, then fix the product until referrals flow.
- **Start unscalable and expensive:** add one or two zeros to the price and list what you'd have to do to be worth it. You only need five clients. Future you will figure out scale.
- **The $1–3M swamp:** it takes more risk to get out than in. Bet size must rise with the opportunity.
- **Lever up instead of hiring:** demand (customers make content), conversion (preload buyers so reps make six-inch putts), delivery (async, group, chat).
- **AI in the right place:** are you making more money? Don't AI-max something that isn't the constraint. Never outsource the hardest thinking.
- **Reality is the moat:** proof, track record and real stakes. Starting out? Document proof of effort.
- **"What will this change about my day?"** Most decisions change nothing, so the fear is made up. → *Tool: Will it change my day?*

## 11 · The hotline (from his 2025-26 lives)
- **Influence = SPCL:** status (you control something scarce), power (they followed your advice and it worked), credibility (proof a third party can see), likeness (they see themselves in you). Stack all four; power matters most. → *Diagram: Influence · stack SPCL.*
- **Name the real constraint.** Callers blame media buying, the economy, the season; it's almost always the hooks, the price or the set call. Volatile isn't risky if it's predictable: do more of what works instead of starting a second business.
- **Workflows, not roles. Train, don't jump in.** Time study → delegate what you already pay for → train with scripts and decision boxes → hire one for what's left. → *Diagram: Get out of the bottleneck.*
- **Define good in observable terms.** Not "be curious", but "ask three questions". Not "be a leader", but "do the activity in front of them". Every KPI gets a paired metric; rules without enforcement are suggestions.
- **Script everything that repeats.** Event pitch word for word on slides; reps record it 25-50 times before going live. A non-expert with a good script closes like the founder.
- **Price and package the front end.** A defined outcome (12 sessions, 6 weeks) beats month-to-month; pitch the back end halfway through and credit what they paid. Raise the price when the close rate is high.
- **Charge for outcomes, not hours.** Calculator close: add up what you'll save them, charge a slice of it.
- **Free first, then earn your way up.** Ten free clients → testimonials → the next ten paid. Starting out, you beat the big firm's barely trained rep: "same price, you get the owner's cell".
- **Focus is subtraction.** Make the work the only black dot on a white wall. People delay starting longer than the task takes.
- **Reps.** His first videos were awful; 30,000 ads later he's fluent. Commit to the volume first, then the pain of effort pulls you to get better.
- **Leila:** commitment is the elimination of alternatives; a system is a prompt that triggers a behaviour without relying on memory; nail it before you scale it.

## Applied to you (my application, not his words)
| His idea | What it means for Caregiver Bench this week |
|---|---|
| Fear lives in the vague | Write what actually happens if an owner says no on the phone. Answer: nothing. Then dial. |
| Decide = cut off | The HVAC alternative is filed for the 8 Dec test. Until then it's not an option, it's a distraction. |
| Volume negates luck | Tuesday's 100 dials is the roll of the dice. Logged in the dialer, so it counts. |
| Do so much work it's unreasonable to fail | Script read out loud every day this week: nerves drop when you're bored of the words. |
| Listen to people closest to your goals | Owners who hire caregivers > friends' opinions about cold calling. |
| Change the environment | Phone in another room during dial blocks; War Room shows only the dial screen. |
| Emotional discomfort isn't a reason to change | A dead dial block is a bottom-10% day, not a verdict on EgorFlow. Same plan tomorrow. |
| Keep the customers you get | First Bench Trial agency: over-deliver the first 30 days so they stay into Priority Bench; churn kills the $20k math. |
| Start unscalable and expensive | Hand-pick and personally vet caregivers for the first 5 agencies; it's the proof that sells the next 50. |
| What will this change about my day? | New idea or purchase: does it add or remove dials/BAC hours? If not, decide in a minute. If it lowers the goal's odds: no. |
| Reset your minimum standard | Today's "a lot" (45 dials) becomes the floor. Measure the month in hundreds of dials, not single days. |
| SPCL / power | On every owner call, give one specific hiring tip they can use this week. When it works, the next ask (Bench Trial) is easier. |
| Name the real constraint | You have zero paying agencies: the constraint is conversations, not the website, the offer doc or the app. |
| Script everything that repeats | Read the opener + Bench Trial pitch out loud before each block; record one run a day, keep the best. |
| Free first, then earn your way up | The 30-Day Bench Trial is your "free 10". First 3 agencies: treat them like case studies, collect the testimonial on day 30. |
| Beat the barely trained rep | Your pitch vs big staffing firms: "you get me directly, my cell, and I personally vet every caregiver". |
| Focus is subtraction | During dial blocks: only the dialer and the script are open. Everything else closed. |

lessons.t: 2026 · Modern Wisdom (Chris Williamson): 33 Brutal Truths To Stop Wasting Your Potential — Alex Hormozi (~4h, 2026) · 80 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Modern Wisdom (Chris Williamson): 33 Brutal Truths To Stop Wasting Your Potential — Alex Hormozi (~4h, 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M). 80 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **The real hard things** · "Do hard things" should mean making the decision you've avoided for 3 months, not ice baths. Hard things don't generalise: soldiers who risk their lives may not manage a vulnerable talk with a spouse; a marathon doesn't make you good at hard conversations. They only generalise if you make it an identity label ("I'm someone who does hard things"), and then you don't even need the marathon. [▶ 0:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=0s)
- **Identity = global reinforcer** · Personality = how you behave across all conditions; identity = the label you give it. Change the label ("I am honest") and it becomes a global reinforcer: in new situations you ask what fits the label, and you feel guilty when you break it. [▶ 4:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=273s)
- **Who controls you?** · "I'm not starting the business because of what they'll say" = they control your behaviour. Say it in plain words and you see how much power you've handed over. [▶ 1:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=68s)
- **Dad's gift** · Before hazing in college, his dad said: think of every hard thing you've already been through; nothing they do will be worse. Use your worst past as the yardstick (Rogan: the worst thing that's happened to you is the worst thing that's happened to you). Recency bias makes you forget your capacity. [▶ 5:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=339s)
- **Story frame** · "This is the story I will one day tell": the more bad things, the more epic the story, and the main listener of your stories is you. Stories work as motivation: they temporarily raise the value of the reward for the hard behaviour, like an ad raises the value of smelling good. [▶ 7:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=436s)
- **3 steps to win** · 1) Realise no one is coming to save you. 2) Take responsibility for your current position. 3) Be willing to sacrifice who you are for who you want to be. People stay stuck longest because of trades they won't make: they want the mountain view, the beach and the Whole Foods. "Never settle" got confused with "never make trades". [▶ 11:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=668s)
- **Options only have value when taken** · Optionality-maxing = blank cheques never cashed. Commitment = eliminating alternatives. The gap between maximised potential and realised potential is the commitments you're willing to make. Some decisions have no refunds. Inaction is a decision: doors close anyway. Unwilling to make any trade, people make the biggest trade of all: nothing. More options make people more miserable; people with one clear path just start walking. You define what you want by what you're willing to sacrifice for it. [▶ 12:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=768s)
- **Not your fault, still your problem** · Taking responsibility = seeing yourself as source. It may be untrue that it's all your fault, but it's more useful: grievance, trauma, genetics, zip code can all be real and you're still the only one who can act. "No one is coming to save you" also means no one is coming to stop you. [▶ 17:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=1026s)
- **The first friends** · The hardest part of entrepreneurship was the first set of friends he had to relinquish: known cost, unknown payoff. After the first time you know you'll survive and find new ones (crabs in a bucket). [▶ 18:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=1093s)
- **Courage** · "The world rewards you in proportion to your courage, not your intellect." "Your potential is determined by how much uncertainty you can tolerate and for how long." "Beat 99% of people by mastering the shame of rejection, the boredom of repetition and the pain of feedback." If he could pass one trait to his son: courage, because without it nothing else matters. Better a failure than a coward. Losing isn't being a loser; not playing is the permanent loss. His definition: taking action with a large short-term cost for an uncertain, delayed benefit. Two paths: the current one is guaranteed not to get you there; the other isn't guaranteed but is the only one with a shot. [▶ 19:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=1181s)
- **Feedback is fuel** · Rejection and failure hurt; in time feedback becomes fuel rather than failure. Feeling bad is a signal to change, not something to be removed. Society is trying to take the teeth out of losing; reality's bill always comes due, with interest. He wants his son to feel the pain of loss so he can learn. "You can feel bad and not feel bad about it." [▶ 23:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=1397s)
- **Push or pivot** · Pivot when a fundamental assumption you started with is proven false by feedback (100 dog owners, none want the dog skateboard). If the assumption isn't disproven and it's an execution problem, push. [▶ 26:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=1601s)
- **Learn the right lesson** · Losing always teaches; make sure it's the right lesson ("my first hire was bad, so all employees suck" is the wrong one). Unlearning is far harder than learning, so try to make early decisions well. [▶ 29:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=1746s)
- **Description vs explanation** · "Johnny stole because he's dishonest" is circular: dishonest just labels the behaviour. Real cause: he was reinforced for stealing (or saw someone who was). If you don't have what you want, your model of the world is wrong or missing variables. Looking purely at inputs and outputs has made his predictions more accurate. [▶ 30:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=1838s)
- **Unbundle words into behaviours** · "Get better at basketball" means nothing to a 5-year-old; break it into step, elbows, thumbs-down until you can act. Couples fight forever over "love" because each defines it as different behaviours; ask "what does that mean?". At Acquisition.com, "be kind and polite" was resolved by "ask more questions rather than make statements". [▶ 33:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=1980s)
- **Unspoken expectations** · Neil Strauss (quoted by Chris): unspoken expectations are premeditated resentments. A complaint is you saying reality didn't deliver what you anticipated. Reality is undefeated. [▶ 36:53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=2213s)
- **Judge outputs, not intentions** · "Malicious benefit and well-intentioned harm": haters who make videos about you promote you for free (incompetent harm, wonderful). Someone who loves you but makes your life worse is well-intentioned harm. Strip people of intentions and look at outputs. Before marrying Leila an adviser said "look at your stats": since her, more exercise, better food, less drinking, more money. Past relationships moved every stat the other way. "I'm not prepared to be collateral damage of your well-intended errors." [▶ 38:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=2286s)
- **Not transactional, just honest** · Relationships aren't binary benefit/no benefit: know the 100 ways someone helps you and tell them, which reinforces it. Exchange happens anyway. "Ride or die" = a long history of reinforcement → a long extinction curve; a new person with little history gets less patience. People change; you can be friends with who they were and not who they are. [▶ 42:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=2568s)
- **Hard wins mean more** · Everything is hard and no one cares. Dreams wouldn't be dreams if fast, easy and risk-free; easy wins are just tying your shoes. More competence → higher stakes (a billionaire playing $10 poker is wasting time). Your standards will always outrun your capacity, so you'll always feel a gap; that isn't actually sucking. [▶ 45:21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=2721s)
- **AI and the journey** · An AI could write the same book word for word, but it would prove the AI knows leads, not him. Is life's output who you became or what exists because of you? He leaves it open. [▶ 47:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=2822s)
- **Love = what you'll give up** · He measures love by what you're willing to give up to keep something. Ask anyone who says "I love you, bro": in what way have you inconvenienced yourself for this? (Chris: "Show me something I can drop on my foot"; Good Will Hunting: idea → picture → words.) [▶ 49:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=2983s)
- **You're not behind, you're early** · "You're behind because you're in a rush; you're in a rush because you feel behind; you feel behind because you're in a different season than the people you compare yourself to." You compare outputs without comparing inputs (Rogan has 10 more years). He disagrees that comparison is the thief of joy: comparison is how you measure the gap so you can close it. Compare yourself to Elon. [▶ 55:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=3356s)
- **Modelling + first principles** · Your first jump comes from modelling people who jumped first (penguins and the polar bear); after that your own reinforcement loop takes over. Listen to people closest to your goals, not closest to you. When nobody has done it: does physics prevent it? If not, it's possible. [▶ 57:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=3460s)
- **Credibility vs relatability** · Being exceptional makes you unrelatable; poor people are surrounded by poor people and think that's everyone. Look past the unrelatable success to the origin story. [▶ 59:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=3582s)
- **Document the journey** · His regret: not documenting the early days. Photos, voice notes, emails to yourself; no need to share. When he lost everything and had $1,000 he screenshotted the bank balance: "never again", and it's now part of his story. Documenting = believing you'll be the hero who overcomes. Worst case you delete it. [▶ 1:01:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=3670s)
- **Everything looks like luck to the unskilled** · You need some skill to recognise skill (jiu-jitsu to a newcomer). When people call your first wins luck, it's incompetence, not malice. "You only envy the lives of people whose sacrifices you can't see." Jimmy Carr: people want what you have but not what you did to get it. Something can be good and still not worth it to you. [▶ 1:05:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=3940s)
- **Self-care = removing people** · "Avoiding people who make it harder to achieve your goals is the highest form of self-care." "The fastest way to change your life is to get around people whose minimum standards are your life goals." Good intentions + incompetence = removable. Give people the tools (tell them exactly what helps); if they choose not to, and you value the goal more, sacrifice the relationship. [▶ 1:10:15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=4215s)
- **Everyone is rooting for you** · (a quote Chris read) Parents, partner, boss, dates all want you to win; the deck isn't stacked against you, and your failures are your own. People stay near you because you rewarded them. Tension arrives when your motives change but your environment hasn't. [▶ 1:12:36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=4356s)
- **Why we refuse trades** · We want everything, and once we get it we stop wanting it (a comedian's bit: all the joy is in the getting; having is worse; losing is worst). Losses hurt more than equal gains, so people flip-flop between paths and realise none. Bill Perkins: people endure years of misery to avoid minutes of pain. The alarm clock: you enjoy the benefit tonight, pay the cost at 6am, so you snooze. "I am" statements become a second motivating force to beat the short-term pain. [▶ 1:14:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=4454s)
- **Clouds to dirt** · Labels ("I'm a neat freak") are shorthand for bundles of behaviours; break them to the granular level and you can change who you are more fluidly. [▶ 1:20:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=4813s)
- **What you're praised for in public you pay for in private** · (Chris's line.) The constant "what could be better" that makes him good at business makes satisfaction hard at home; Leila pointed it out. A problem to be managed, not a paradox to solve. [▶ 1:15:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=4520s)
- **Monomania + no half measures** · Big swings need "complete sicko mode" for an extended period, about 10 years, with no compromises. "Half measures yield null outcomes": half effort in four domains = none realised. Say "I want this more than that, not forever, but for now." [▶ 1:21:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=4919s)
- **Poverty loves indecision** · "Money loves speed, wealth loves time, poverty loves indecision." Inaction is an action; vote with your behaviour for the outcome you want; the things worth wanting arrive with a delay. [▶ 1:24:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=5047s)
- **Ignore the average** · The average person will try to keep you average. If you want to be extraordinary, ordinary people will see what you do as extra. Many people want to see you fail because it justifies the risks they didn't take. We crave approval from people whose lives we don't want: then why weigh their opinion? As a child you had to live by others' preferences; as an adult you choose your own mould. Average American adult: obese, likely divorced, <$1k saved; following the crowd reliably gets you that life. [▶ 1:25:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=5116s)
- **The lonely chapter** · The path to exceptional is lonely, and here disagreement is a signal you're doing something different (Larry Ellison: if everyone thinks it's stupid, either they're right or you are, and if you are, you make a lot of money). Rejection comes as snide jokes and quiet exclusion. You trade those moments for the nights at home thinking "this isn't the life I want". It's no man's land, the start of the metamorphosis, and it repeats on every mountain, often hardest after your first success. [▶ 1:27:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=5255s)
- **Why are you working so hard?** · Before you win, people ask why you work so hard; after you win, they ask why you're still working so hard. Translation: your goals aren't theirs. Answer: yes. [▶ 1:32:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=5562s)
- **Crushing competitors isn't satisfying** · Beating a rival comes with no parade, no referee; by the end it's a giant beating a child, and you see the employees who lost jobs. Losers often "change their goals" mid-game, which is fine if it's a conscious decision; the problem is having it made for you unconsciously. Revenge is fuel you can use, but beating a person is far less fulfilling than you think, and it means they control you. [▶ 1:33:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=5615s)
- **Zoom out** · Ask what the wise old man would say about what you're doing now: it softens losses ("this is okay") and wins ("I'm not that important"). Time and space shrink or expand anything. [▶ 1:37:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=5824s)
- **Time/space as a coping tool** · Zoom in to enjoy, zoom out of pain. [▶ 1:38:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=5908s)
- **20 hours** · You can get competent at nearly anything in ~20 hours (2 focused 10-hour days); most people spend a decade delaying the first 20. More potential is wasted through inaction than incompetence. The first 20 hours of any skill hold the biggest concepts, and stacked skills multiply, not add (Jay-Z: rap × sell × market). [▶ 1:38:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=5917s)
- **Unsure? Build potential** · Don't know what to do? Sleep well, get in shape, build an audience: prepare the launch pad, but be ready to cash it in; optionality without decisiveness is a trap. [▶ 1:41:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=6072s)
- **Deserve it by volume** · "You only need to get rich once, so work as hard as you can to get it done as fast as you can." "Do so much work it would be unreasonable for you to fail." "Work with such relentless obsession that people are grateful they don't compete with you." "The fastest shortcut is to stop looking for shortcuts." [▶ 1:42:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=6159s)
- **Volume negates luck; violence is the answer** · The two credos in Acquisition.com's internal sales handbook. Nothing is more satisfying than leaving it all on the field for something you deem meaningful. [▶ 1:43:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=6202s)
- **A man must have a quest** · (his and Leila's saying) Best father, best musician, best tire replacer, anything. Hopelessness = a perceived lack of options; anxiety = many options and no priority; a quest fixes both: one clear path, then destroy the doubts and fake risks on it. A partner who believes in the better you is rare ("come back with your shield or on it": they reward the good fight). [▶ 1:44:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=6278s)
- **Questless people mocking the questing** · One of his least favourite groups. Turn down the volume on people who don't understand your goals; it's not your job to explain yourself to them. His live translation of all hate: "you're living your life against my preferences" — "you're right". Your new standards highlight where they aren't living by theirs (Chris quitting drinking as a club promoter got mocked even though he profited from their drinking). [▶ 1:47:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=6428s)
- **Nobody hates you** · They hate a projection built from a few 30-second clips. Weight opinions by how much of your life they've shared: someone who spent one day with you has 1/13,000th of your context. [▶ 1:51:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=6677s)
- **Buy nothing challenge** · If you're broke: 30 days buying only food, rent, gas, insurance; leave the wallet at home, pack lunch. You learn how little you can live on, which shows how much more risk you can take. "Being good with money = spend less than you make and put the extra in things that go up, not down." Not spending is hard because there are a hundred things to buy and only one "nothing". [▶ 1:53:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=6829s)
- **Nostalgia** · Across species, bad consequences fade and good ones stick (the ex, the hangover), which is why every season looks like the good old days later. His gratitude operation: imagine something good, imagine losing it, realise you haven't. [▶ 1:56:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=6960s)
- **Simpler, not easier** · Your system handles intensity but not complexity (Adam Lane Smith via Chris). You always find the maximum number of problems your brain can perceive at any age. Focus multiplies: his best work came from many "coats of paint" over time in different moods; split thinking across five projects and you only go an inch deep. Believing you can serve several masters is arrogant: it assumes fully focused competitors can't beat you. [▶ 2:00:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=7200s)
- **Every position has an advantage** · Young = cutting edge; old = experience; small = personal; big = track record; rich = resources; broke = nothing to lose. "You aren't limited by your resources, only your resourcefulness." There's always a way to win, just not always enough desire. [▶ 2:04:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=7479s)
- **Inversion** · We're wired to spot threats, so list everything that would guarantee failure, then flip it (Munger). Design the day your worst enemy would want you to live. George's version: you vs you-with-a-moustache who knows all your weaknesses: do what he'd do. Investor version: if someone bought 100% of your company today, what would they do in the first 30 days? (cut the catering, let go of Todd who stopped growing). Keeping Todd = you care more about not feeling guilty than about the business: "show me your priorities". [▶ 2:06:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=7564s)
- **Want to want** · Many people want to want; they don't actually give things up to get stuff. [▶ 2:10:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=7813s)
- **Fear lives in the vague** · "Above intelligence and work ethic, you're compensated in proportion to your risk." Write down in excruciating detail what happens step by step if you fail; it's rarely that bad. "Fear exists in the vague, not the specific." Ask a friend in advance: "if this blows up, can I crash on your couch?" Real friends say yes, and that lets you jump. [▶ 2:10:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=7825s)
- **Risk is mispriced** · Peter Thiel on Elon: he must understand risk differently. In the developed world the downside of trying your hardest is almost nothing (you won't starve, there's shelter, unskilled work exists); the upside you miss is everything. Our brains price risk for a world where one mistake meant death. Recalibrate your risk appetite as you grow (a $12M-profit company should make $2–4M bets). Bezos: a 10% chance of 100× is worth taking every time. Even the 90% "losses" build skill, network and perspective: you win or you learn. Better high-conviction and wrong than low-conviction and wrong. Inaction = action against your priorities. Indecision practised = you become indecisive. [▶ 2:11:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=7860s)
- **If not now, when?** · What got him to quit: future-him would have a wife and kids, so it'd never be easier than now. You want perfect information for a perfect decision; when information is perfect the opportunity is gone. Have a worldview, make bets, check upside vs downside. Jocko: "all loss is just psychological until death". [▶ 2:17:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=8263s)
- **Reminded more than taught** · Important lessons sound like clichés. If you're bored of hearing it, why haven't you mastered it? The gap is usually execution, not information. [▶ 2:19:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=8395s)
- **How he actually quit** · Fired as a mediocre employee who read self-help all day; a book's flippant word "wantrepreneur" disgusted him; Arnold's "you can't climb the ladder of success with your hands in your pockets" every morning; Relentless (Tim Grover) gave permission to use his dark side; nightly calls with his friend Victor pacing a groove into an IKEA cowhide rug; repeated lunches where his dad talked him down. He re-derived the same decision a hundred times with friends for six months (it's fine to be "boring" when you need support). Then he looked around and saw his life hadn't changed at all from reading, and Googled how to start a gym. A gym owner told him to make a serious commitment; when he came back without even a lease the guy said "lose my number". It took all of it, not one book, to cross his threshold of action. [▶ 2:24:34](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=8674s)
- **An exploding offer from life** · He even studied 4 hours of GMAT a day and applied to Harvard/Booth. One essay question ("how will an MBA help your goals?") made him do the maths: $120k and 2 years for a $120k salary vs betting the same 2 years on owning a business making $10k/month. It was the realisation that it would never get easier, and the fear of never starting, that made him move. He packed, drove halfway across the country, and only then told people, so they couldn't talk him out of it: his conviction was that fragile. [▶ 2:30:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=9044s)
- **Change your environment** · Your environment (where you live, friends, routines, places) runs your behaviour loops. Vietnam vets: ~20% used heroin; only ~5% relapsed at home vs huge relapse rates after rehab, because every cue changed. Move cities, or at least across town; train at another gym; work from another coffee shop; pause the friends. Real friends welcome you back. "If nothing changes, nothing changes." A crisis (breakup, accident) scrambles your loops: a short window to change things cheaply, so be grateful for the chaos. [▶ 2:33:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=9205s)
- **Quantum leaps** · After every prolonged period of hardship there tends to be a period of leaps across several areas, if you don't give up on yourself (a quote Chris read). "Failure and success are on the same road; failure is just an earlier exit." Don't be the one who quits at the moment you should fight hardest. [▶ 2:36:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=9380s)
- **From coward to courage** · At Vanderbilt he was VP of powerlifting, fraternity president, 3.8 GPA, graduated in 3 years, then took the first job offered out of fear. "You can change your stars." He was afraid of everything; he flipped it by being more afraid of looking back on a life where he never tried than of failing. Use whatever fuel you have (anger, shame, fear): put it behind you so you run away from the future your current path leads to. The enemy ahead or the whip behind: you face the one you fear least, so raise the pain of the one you want least. [▶ 2:37:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=9424s)
- **Someone's dreams will die** · The boy he was in his father's eyes "died"; living up to his dad's expectations was all he'd wanted, and he had to sacrifice it (they're great now). "Someone's dreams will die: yours or theirs." Make sure whoever dreams for you dreams bigger than you; well-meaning practical people often dream smaller. [▶ 2:43:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=9820s)
- **His son** · Will care endlessly about effort and very little about outcomes (if he controlled the controllables); high standards because he respects and believes in him. Purpose over happiness (happiness is fleeting). Above all: brave and tries his ass off. [▶ 2:45:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=9922s)
- **He'll change when conditions change** · Fatherhood won't block business goals (the most successful people mostly have kids). He chose this life and traded "the young boy and that life" for it, and would make that trade 100 times. Possible surprise: he works much less because he'd rather be with the kid. He'll model men on their "second family" who all say they should have spent more time with the first kids. [▶ 2:48:27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=10107s)
- **No half measures** · "If you're going to chase a dream, go all in; if you love, love fiercely; if you walk away, never look back." Most solutions never get a fighting chance: not enough volume for long enough. The cost is unknown, like a race without a visible finish line. Irreversible decisions make people happier than reversible ones (no-returns jeans). [▶ 2:55:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=10523s)
- **No one was watching** · Everyone is thinking about themselves; you should have done what you wanted all along. His dad's father-figure: "I've got 10 years, I don't have time for this", near-zero worry. Old people are less competitive: they've seen the best and worst status die the same and the world move on fast. Classic wisdom ("money won't make you happy", "see your parents more", "your worries were a waste") is hard to absorb because the short-term reward pulls harder. Don't be the 60-year-old still playing a game you already beat. [▶ 3:01:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=10916s)
- **Reps kill nerves** · "If you're nervous, do more." Do something enough times you're bored of it and you're ready. He rehearsed the book launch 100+ times: on stage he was the calmest person the organiser had seen: "I've done this before." You can do the hard work of not caring what people think, or do so much work there's nothing left to control. Do your job (Belichick). Think now about what you'd say after failing, and do that before you fail. Rehearse failures (dead clicker, fallen props) so they've already happened. [▶ 3:10:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=11412s)
- **Never waste a crisis** · A restraining order to stop his $10M book launch was filed the day before; his reaction when it was dismissed: "darn, that would have been a better story". Some problems (a toddler breaking something precious) you just suffer through; there's peace in having done what you could. [▶ 3:14:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=11670s)
- **Know what you want, refuse anything else** · What you want = what you're willing to sacrifice for. Pick the one thing you'll put everything on the altar for, and every decision gets a single lens (Kobe: "does this make me a better basketball player?"). Decision-making becomes easy and you get your mental bandwidth back. [▶ 3:19:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=11995s)
- **Write the decision document** · The hard part is deciding, not sticking. The hidden cost is switching DESIRES: yearning for the price of a decision you already said was worth it. For big decisions he writes a document with all the reasoning; when doubt returns he rereads it and the loop closes. Especially after a breakup: punishment fades and reward sticks, so write the warning letter to your future self. (Chris: "borrowed authority" from your past self.) [▶ 3:21:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=12085s)
- **Tragedy + time = comedy** · So laugh now (a friend's mum laughing when he was 11: "you'll laugh about this in a few years"). Make the fear look silly, like the boggart in Harry Potter. Comedians are modern philosophers: comedy is punishment avoided. Every story he remembers from that trip is the funny disaster. [▶ 3:23:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=12212s)
- **Make a company worth working hard for** · Humans haven't changed; lazy and driven people exist in every generation. A big noble goal people will suffer for (Elon: saving humanity) + a micro-environment leaders keep good. If people keep being demotivated, you're the common denominator. Culture = the rules of reinforcement: what's rewarded, what's punished, what's tolerated that shouldn't be. Define in observable terms: not "Susie is lazy" but "slow Slack replies, late to two meetings". The leader's main job: hold the standard, define what good looks like observably. [▶ 3:30:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=12619s)
- **No success legitimises you to the ignorant** · Ray Dalio got roasted as a "fake guru" on TikTok. Some people aren't worth being loved by; it's good to be hated by a bad person. Being disliked by the wrong people is a fixed cost. The internet is huge and opinions differ, so a big share will hate you. But ask "what if they're right?": haters called him a steroid user and Leila said "you have taken steroids". The pain is in fighting it; accept it and it stops affecting you. [▶ 3:34:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=12864s)
- **Routine must be additive** · "The stress of trying to be perfect will kill you faster than your imperfections." If you can't function without your routine, your routine owns you. Additive is great; dependent is fragile. He fears getting soft, so he still does Q&A with small owners to stay connected to the ground. Nobody is ever at 100% (Invictus). Nobody remembers the bad ref call in 20 years: just win. Mayweather: win with your Z game. [▶ 3:42:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=13368s)
- **Master the boring middle** · The hard part isn't starting; it's continuing when the excitement's gone. A marathon's crowds are at the start and finish; it's won in the 26 miles between. Motivation is ephemeral, so arrange conditions that make successful actions the most likely ones. Don't stack the deck against yourself (relying on perfect willpower to not drink and perfect sleep to be ready). Antifragile plans: the Money Models launch had 3–4 independent ways to break the record, each 80–90% likely. People attack problems with too little volume and intensity: "I applied to 3 jobs" (45 minutes) vs 1,000 a month. [▶ 3:48:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=13680s)
- **The black dot room** · More dreams are destroyed by distraction than incompetence. In a white room, the one black dot is the most interesting thing. You won't willpower the work into being interesting; put yourself where the work is the most interesting thing available. [▶ 3:51:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=13893s)
- **Respect = POWERS** · Respect = letting someone's words change what you do when they can't make you. Earn it with POWERS: Pay the cost (sacrifice for the group where they can see it — he volunteered to go with a pledge to the feared hazer), Outcomes (things improve when you're involved, traceably, repeatedly), Word (what you say happens, happens), Enforce (don't let people cross you consistently), Restraint (punish less than you could, give more credit than needed), Steady (act the same in high stakes as normal). Enforcement alone = tyrant (compliance ends when your power does); competence without enforcement = admired doormat. [▶ 3:52:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=13937s)
- **Enforcing a standard** · Only enforce when: 1) they knew the standard, 2) they could meet it, 3) they chose not to. Unspoken standards are premeditated disrespect. Make it about the behaviour, not the person (the chef: "you cost us that table; we're comping it; you're still with us; 6am tomorrow, do better"). Consequences must be consistent (or you teach people to gamble with you), immediate and escalating; repeated, it becomes the person, and you let them go even if they're a high performer. [▶ 3:56:36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=14196s)
- **Give respect = HEARTED** · Honor (respect their preferences and lines, don't test limits), Esteem (praise them when they're not there), Attend (listen without interrupting), Reliable (keep your word to them), Truth (tell them straight, including what they won't like), Expectations (hold them to the same standard; don't lower the bar), Defer (in their area of expertise, defer to their decisions). Defining respect as behaviours lets him give leaders real feedback (one over-enforces, one under-enforces). [▶ 3:59:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=14392s)
- **Sacrifice mediocrity** · "You can't get rich without risking losing money, loved without risking rejection, strong without risking injury. You have to risk looking broke, weak, desperate. Egos hold back more dreams than failure and rejection ever will." Risk = trading a known inferior thing for an unknown superior one. Most lost gains come from being unwilling to sacrifice mediocrity: you sacrifice one either way, the ordinary for a chance at extraordinary, or the extraordinary to stay ordinary. [▶ 4:05:11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-AdkwqkE20M&t=14711s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Modern Wisdom · 41 Harsh Truths Nobody Wants To Admit (4h, 2025) · 93 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Modern Wisdom · 41 Harsh Truths Nobody Wants To Admit (4h, 2025)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8). 93 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Nobody remembers the Queen** · She ruled a nation and was richer than 99.9% of humans, yet you hadn't thought of her today. No matter how big your dreams, you'll die and everyone moves on: do what you want. "It sucks to not be liked, but it sucks more to not be yourself." To a busy salesman skipping the gym: "You'll never have more time and less responsibility than now. If you can't make it work now, accept you'll never be in shape, and stop wanting it." [▶ 3:21:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8&t=12117s)
- **Non-negotiables on date one** · He stated his up front (I work a lot; I train; I won't give those up). Minimise the gap between how you perform and who you are; they'll find out anyway. Like Bezos ("what won't change?"): look for the few big rocks that won't change in 50 years (behaviour under duress), not 100 pebbles. Have ~3 musts and ignore the rest. [▶ 3:26:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8&t=12400s)
- **Work-life balance** · "People who obsess about work-life balance are typically mediocre at both. Obsessed people apply their obsession to everything and just call it life." [▶ 3:30:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8&t=12620s)
- **Divorce course first** · Inversion: right after marrying, they studied why couples divorce (money, kids, tactical preferences) and handled each. "Rounding up": if something can be taken two ways, assume the good one. Space when he gets home. Preferences are behaviours: "What would you prefer I do instead?" [▶ 3:30:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8&t=12645s)
- **Appreciation camel** · "I'm proud of you" means little to him; "Thank you for working so hard" landed hugely, because it framed his work as serving them. Leila's superpower: he never has to repeat feedback; she changes immediately ("Okay, what does warm look like?"). When a request costs her something, they talk trade-offs (she stopped cooking his meals to run the company). [▶ 3:32:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8&t=12768s)
- **You are your behaviours** · Identity = the sum of what you do ("who is John?" → what John does). See yourself as 1,000 behaviours and ask: is keeping this one worth more than the relationship? Changes that cost you little and mean a lot to them are easy trades. [▶ 3:38:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8&t=13137s)
- **Learning to try generalises** · Lazy people can't start, weak people can't finish, successful people can't stop. Once you've truly tried at one thing, all resources, daily, for a long time, you learn how few things you can do well, how easy it is to beat people who don't, and that the skill transfers (500 forehands = 500 tweets with feedback). [▶ 3:40:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8&t=13251s)
- **Depth beats a second 9/10** · The better he gets at one thing, the less he wants others: the effort to be 9/10 at a second skill could instead take him from top-100 to #1 in the first. Returns per unit of effort are highest at the top, even though it feels like less progress. [▶ 3:42:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8&t=13363s)
- **Meditation as the next maximise** · He's seriously weighing ~4 hours a day of meditation: long-term practitioners report subjective wellbeing several standard deviations above normal. He runs it like the house: if I spent all available time, would it be worth it? The troubling answer is yes. "The single greatest skill is being in a great mood without reasons." At 19–20 he chose "be useful" over chasing happiness; now he's open to being both. [▶ 3:45:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8&t=13537s)
- **Spend to buy time** · ~$1,500/month buys back ~90 hours/month (housekeeper who cooks + rideshare/driver). If your free hour is worth more than ~$50, it's a good trade. The highest-ROI money he spends as an investor: getting founders 100 hours a month back. Most people stop at house, car, clothes, food, travel. [▶ 3:53:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8&t=14025s)
- **His two biggest updates this year** · 1) Useful and happy isn't a trade-off. 2) Get specific about moments: spread one good thing as wide as possible, shrink one bad thing into the smallest box, and never shoot the second arrow. [▶ 3:58:21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ky1oHHJ5Ne8&t=14301s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Modern Wisdom · Be Ruthless About the Life You Want (3h) · 62 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Modern Wisdom · Be Ruthless About the Life You Want (3h)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ). 62 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Three generations** · In three generations everyone who knew you, including the people whose opinions stopped you, will be dead. Death is the thing he thinks about most; it lets him act despite judgement, so there's only one voice to listen to: his. The catch: you must work things out from first principles; independent thinking is a muscle. [▶ 0:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=0s)
- **"Okay" is terrifying** · Living at home when you want to move, dating the safe girl, the okay job: the freedom to fail repeatedly feels more real than autopilot. "Why can't you physically quit? Could you move in with parents, split rent?" If you zoom out far enough you can't see the Earth. [▶ 2:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=121s)
- **Don't copy most people** · (Sean Kelly via Chris) The average person is obese, likely divorced and has under $1k saved; doing what everyone does guarantees their results. [▶ 3:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=210s)
- **One booming voice** · He had essentially one voice: his father. The moment his father was most proud (consultant, graduated in 3 years) was when Alex was saddest, so maybe that approval wasn't the way to feel good. Six months from decision to change. He was so afraid that he didn't tell his dad until he was five states away. [▶ 5:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=307s)
- **Decision-to-action compresses** · The higher your agency, the shorter the gap between deciding and doing. The first big wall is the hardest; after it you use it as evidence for every next one: "I told my dad no; how hard can selling strangers be?" The bigger the dragon, the more proof you can slay the next. [▶ 6:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=362s)
- **A few hard conversations** · The life you want is on the other side of a few hard conversations. When anxious, insecure, angry or sad, ask "what conversation am I not having?" After you have one, you want to have five more. [▶ 8:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=484s)
- **The crash** · He was splitting everything with partners in several gyms and an agency, all relying on him. A DUI and a 60 mph head-on collision he walked away from was the wake-up call, not to stop drinking but to have the conversations he was drinking to avoid. Next day he called every partner: "I'd rather be alive." [▶ 9:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=547s)
- **Nothing to lose** · "I hope I don't wake up" meant he had nothing to lose, which made him dangerous. If you feel you have nothing going for you, you also have nothing to lose. [▶ 10:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=605s)
- **Region-beta paradox** · (Chris) Walk under a mile, drive over: you'd get 2 miles faster than 1. Comfortable complacency (okay job, okay relationship, cheap mouldy flat) traps you because it's not bad enough to act. Alex: every most painful event (leaving his dad, the crash, losing everything) created a disproportionate gain (first business, ending partnerships, switching to licensing). Expand the time horizon and most bad events become net wins. [▶ 11:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=690s)
- **Unmade decisions are the heaviest thing** · Commitment = eliminating alternatives; until you remove the exits you haven't decided. Unmade decisions run a hamster wheel; usually it's fear of one specific person's judgement. Name them: "Looks like Tom controls my life more than I do." At 19, blaming his parents gave them control; disgust at that is what made him take control. [▶ 15:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=900s)
- **Anxiety cost** · (Chris) Every second thinking about an unmade decision is time you'd get back by just making it: eat the frog early. Alex: decide by end of day instead of end of week and you move ~7× faster; 4 decisions take a normal person a month and him 4 days. [▶ 18:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=1120s)
- **Fear of insufficiency drives achievers** · Pre-Baltimore Alex had more insecurity than most; it's why he did well. Most high performers run on "I might be a piece of crap" more than a love of greatness. Regress any fear far enough and it's death, the greatest motivator: people go ten times harder with a gun to their head than for a reward. [▶ 21:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=1267s)
- **Fear of others' opinions** · You're not afraid of failing, you're afraid of what people think if you fail; imagine what they think when you don't try. His tweets are notes to self. If you fail in public, they think nothing; they don't think about you at all. [▶ 24:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=1480s)
- **Use what you've got** · The perfect condition is the one you're in; play the hand. Every position has an advantage: the newcomer can say "you're a number to Gym Launch; with me you get personal attention." [▶ 25:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=1550s)
- **Cynicism = safety blanket** · (Chris) Never trying means never feeling public failure; you guarantee failing long and privately rather than short and publicly. Like never investing: the only investment guaranteed not to work. [▶ 27:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=1630s)
- **Grandpa's lunches** · Three lunches a week at a nursing home with his 90-year-old grandfather (who fled the Nazis): "You have two hands and one brain; use them." Seeing someone with no options left and only regrets. His regrets about how he raised Alex's mother helped Alex understand and forgive her; "to understand is to forgive"; it's hard to hate up close. When she pushed his usual button, he said "I get it, I'm sorry, you had a tough life" and she broke down. [▶ 29:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=1745s)
- **Choose your regrets** · (Hitchens via Douglas Murray via Chris) Opportunity cost makes regret unavoidable, so ask "which regret can I live with?": one awful conversation with your boss vs a wasted decade. Alex: this uses your run-away-from engine. [▶ 33:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=1983s)
- **Cat and cheese** · (Peterson via Chris) A starving rat pulls harder for cheese when a cat smell comes from behind. Three traits of successful people: superiority complex (cheese), crippling insufficiency (cat), impulse control (only one direction). Loss aversion is ~3×: frame it as what you'll lose (a wasted decade), not what you'll gain. [▶ 36:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=2161s)
- **Proof, not affirmations** · "My biggest fear is getting to the end and thinking I wasn't good enough" = could have tried harder. Confidence comes from a stack of undeniable proof, not mirror affirmations. [▶ 38:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=2300s)
- **Win = nothing left to do** · He used to measure outcomes; now he wins when there's nothing else he could have done. $100M Leads: 19 drafts, 4 full rewrites, 6am–noon daily for two years. For a 500k-person launch he justified 50× the prep he'd give a 10k audience: 900 slides, daily run-throughs in his head, then out loud recorded, then rewatch and fix every stumble, until it's "glass". "I'm the judge, jury and executioner of my own self-esteem"; with very high standards, the only way to not always feel like a failure is doing work until nothing's left, which means doing fewer things. [▶ 39:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=2341s)
- **Turn pro** · (Chris, after Pressfield) Treat your pursuit like an athlete: game tape, sleep, food, coaches, environment. He podcasted from a boot two weeks after rupturing his Achilles; 3 episodes a week for 3 years without missing. Nervous vs excited = your level of preparation. [▶ 42:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=2521s)
- **Reset the minimum standard** · A public-company CEO friend posts once a day; Alex's team posts ~300 a week. "Thank you for resetting my minimum standard." His biggest reason for bigger results later: his minimum for how much work he can put into something rose a hundredfold (first decks: 25 slides). Measure in hundreds of hours. The more you do, the more you realise you can do; next year's "pro" is this year's minimum. [▶ 46:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=2767s)
- **The woman in the red dress** · (Matrix) Every distracting opportunity is a woman in the red dress, and the more successful you get, the more attractive she is. A mentor after the Gym Launch sale: "If it's not a billion, it's not worth your time." Acquisition.com gets ~3,000 deal inquiries a month and did 13 deals in two years. Your no-muscle is really a yes-muscle for the one thing that matters most. [▶ 49:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=2943s)
- **Heroes use pain, villains are used by it** · (riff on Donald Miller) Same backstory, pain; the villain says "the world hurt me, I'll hurt it back", the hero "I won't let it hurt anyone else". People hunt for passion (cheese) while the cat is already behind them: use the pain you have. [▶ 54:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=3243s)
- **Twist the knife** · Operationalise pain: not "I hate my life" but "I hate how Andrew made me feel when he said I'd amount to nothing, because he's right." What hurts is what's partly true: look in the mirror and ask "what if they're right?" Then act. Insufficiency and resentment fuel most high performers; Chris thinks it turns toxic over a lifetime but fuels a decade well. [▶ 55:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=3330s)
- **Success is the only revenge** · At 15 a school admin, Mr Given, started training him. When Alex fantasised about showing up a bully at the 10-year reunion, he said: you'd look like the loser; they'd say "you did all that to prove me wrong? I feel sorry for you." Win so big they compare themselves to you and you forget they exist. It's not the best revenge, it's the only one; everything else proves you thought about them all day. [▶ 58:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=3510s)
- **Don't let them pick your game** · (Chris) Changing your direction just to beat someone at the game they care about means they've already won: they ventriloquised you. [▶ 1:01:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=3664s)
- **Whose game are you winning?** · He spent years trying to out-earn his father; when his dad called to apologise, Alex replied coldly. Having beaten his father's game (money = status), he realised he'd never asked which game he wanted to win. He likes who he is, and his father raised him, so maybe he was the right father. [▶ 1:04:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=3846s)
- **Your shame's bright side** · (Chris) Being an outcast at school is why he can outwork anyone in solitude, and obsessing over why others had friends made him a top club promoter. Alex: bad micro events, doubled down on, become big macro wins. [▶ 1:07:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=4022s)
- **You've already hit goals you said would make you happy** · Wins bring little joy; his joy is the Rocky cut-scene of the work itself. He'll feel let down when the launch is over. So set something very big and far away to stay in pursuit as long as possible. (Chris: set the destination so you'll take the journey; these are the golden years.) [▶ 1:11:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=4262s)
- **Make the man** · Picture the bulletproof man you want to become (marriage, business), then ask what you'd put him through to build him: not easy or quick wins, but reaching just past your threshold, over and over. In hard times: "I'm making you." [▶ 1:15:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=4506s)
- **85-year-old gratitude** · Imagine you're 85 waking up in your 30-year-old body: no pain, clear head, young wife, no flying cars yet. You'd give anything to have this mundane day back. It lasts minutes, but those minutes are what he remembers. [▶ 1:16:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=4590s)
- **Five present moments a day** · (Sam Harris via Chris) Aim for small moments of presence (the first sip of coffee); string two together, five times a day. Peripheral vision is a cue: see the edges and you're present. Alex: zoom into a detail, like the bird on the branch before the battle in Gladiator. (Chris: you have one megabyte of RAM; think one thought.) [▶ 1:17:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=4670s)
- **Fame's seesaw** · People root for you on the way up because you remind them of their dreams, and tear you down at the top because you remind them they gave up (Chris). "Fame doesn't change you, it changes everybody around you" (Lewis Capaldi via Chris). Alex's gym clients cheered when he slept on the gym floor, then sneered "boss man" 9 months later; people want you to do well, but not better than them. The tipping point depends on where they stand. [▶ 1:24:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=5043s)
- **Hate is a requirement** · A performance coach: "Hatred isn't something you avoid; it's a requisite for success. No hate, no success." So hate is a leading indicator. When friends say "too cool for us now?", you've reached the top of their mountain. The lonely chapter: you don't fit your old friends and don't yet have results for new ones. Don't bend the knee back into conformity. [▶ 1:29:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=5346s)
- **Ignorance was bliss** · Once you know sleep matters, every bad night is on you. The difficulty of a goal is what makes it worth it; don't resent the price tag, decide whether to pay it. [▶ 1:34:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=5640s)
- **Self-love = higher standards** · Self-love is holding yourself to a higher standard than anyone else does: believe in your 85-year-old ideal self, ruthlessly look at the gap, break it down and pull the first thread. His early foothold: "I don't need to deserve success; I can still have it if I do what creates it." [▶ 1:36:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=5761s)
- **Reject self-acceptance** · Accept circumstances (your age, race, sex, hand dealt) but never "I'm satisfied and can't be better." Good enough for the work you've put in ≠ good. Hard times are a requisite for big goals. [▶ 1:39:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=5940s)
- **Learn what each stage tastes like** · A portfolio CEO stuck on how many locations to open was actually missing a finance leader. First time, you can't recognise the signs; others' descriptions of what each stage feels like let you say "this sounds like X". [▶ 1:40:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=6030s)
- **Personal brand = what you'd do if nobody watched** · Everyone has a unique brand; most look boring because they conform. He asked "what would 85-year-old me wear?" (most functional, comfiest, works in every room). Ask the same for work, clothes, who you'd date. Stick-to-it-ness is a skill: each attempt lasting longer is progress. Half the US has negative net worth; the bar is low. [▶ 1:42:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=6125s)
- **The bar is just not overweight** · To be top 10% you need to not be overweight and be employed. (Chris) The "alpha history fantasy": men think they'd have been Genghis Khan rather than peasant #1,373,000. [▶ 1:46:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=6361s)
- **Good sticks** · (Ferriss via Chris) Don't build a perfect note system. Take the one thing from a podcast you can't stop thinking about and work on it for a month. Chris remembers things through caring and massive exposure (670 podcasts). [▶ 1:48:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=6510s)
- **Operational emotions** · Sadness = a lack of perceived options = ignorance, which is solvable: "what do I not know, what option don't I see?" Anxiety = many options, few priorities: list them, pick the most important, ignore the rest. Patience = knowing what to do in the meantime; most goals are reachable if you extend the time horizon. [▶ 1:52:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=6725s)
- **Sticking to the plan** · Choosing the plan isn't hard, doing it isn't hard, sticking to it is (Munger: the money is made in the wait). Your first plan was usually fine. [▶ 1:54:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=6890s)
- **The stick-to-it muscle** · A mediocre plan you stick to beats a perfect plan you don't. Start-stop is normal until you get your first cookie; then more of the same gets more cookies and you get addicted to working. The scary part: the new bar becomes every time. [▶ 1:55:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=6930s)
- **What does "must be nice" get you?** · (Chris) Sympathy is available, but ask what that mindset buys you; someone has had it worse and done better. "Tell me you don't have kids" → so you blame your child for the life you didn't live? [▶ 1:56:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=7000s)
- **The work works on you** · People misread Alex: his work is his fun. Whatever you amount to won't matter; who you become in the process is what lasts. "There is profit in all labour." He spent 5 years building 6 gyms, sold 5, put the money into a partner who disappeared with it into bankruptcy; in the next 12 months he made about 5× the previous five years' profit, because the output was him. No work is wasted: "I am the output of the work, not the outcome." [▶ 1:59:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=7141s)
- **Work capacity is trainable** · "Once you look like you work out, you can worry about overtraining." Recovery capacity grows with volume; you either die, get injured or adapt. Experts become experts because they learn to be rewarded by the work itself (Dr Kashy). [▶ 2:03:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4PzOjM5BJQ&t=7387s)
- **Judge actions, not thoughts** · He was far less disappointed in himself once he judged only his actions. Traits aren't binary; patience is a continuum you build with pennies on the scale each time you act patiently while not feeling it.
