- **Don't restart on a winning model** · Landscaper wanting to switch to consulting other landscapers: every path (own more locations, franchise, education) helps many people at scale; starting over puts you at zero in a new game (B2C → B2B, national ads). A one-location owner he told to just keep opening $40–50k locations that made $300–400k became a nine-figure company four years later. "When it gets boring is when you need to go harder; boring is where you get rich." Hard-to-scale = a moat others must also cross; info products give a high-paying job, not an enterprise. [▶ 8:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=486s)
- **Don't know what you want? Eliminate** · (Munger) Know where you'd die and never go there. Cross out what you don't want until what's left is good. He looked at his good and bad days: avoid the common bad things, string together the good ones. He lived by "forget happiness, be useful", and one day noticed he liked his life. [▶ 15:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=902s)
- **Directional, not perfect** · The perfect pick is a lottery fantasy: you lack the context to judge until you've done things. Words or numbers? Numbers → which numbers careers? → finance? → jump in. Two years in the "wrong" thing isn't wasted: Jobs' calligraphy class became Mac fonts; Alex brought a space/intelligence consulting lens to gyms. You're not in a rush; everyone ends up in the same place. [▶ 18:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=1083s)
- **You can help people in any business** · Shutting an agency to "help people" missed that he could change his employees' lives. Get hyper-specific on what you were great at; sell done-with-you/done-for-you; give away all the secrets (Neil Patel: tutorials for everything, people still hire us). Where you weren't good, don't fake it: he found the 20 of 1,000 Gym Launch gyms with low churn, extracted the 5 things they all did, tested on 10 + 10 gyms, then "state the facts and tell the truth". [▶ 22:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=1324s)
- **Death as permission** · Everyone whose opinion you fear also dies; if people outlive you, they don't think about you. Spending your life catering to them is a shame. Remembering he'll die and be forgotten makes him go after bigger things. [▶ 26:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=1567s)
- **Burnout = rushing** · You burn out because you set an arbitrary deadline (a billionaire by tomorrow). Commit to activities that make progress reasonable; if you did $100k → $200k aiming for $1M, you can choose to call it failure or success. "The work is the goal" — not "and the score takes care of itself", which still makes the score king. He's not high-energy; he endures because he keeps his commitments. Missed a workout? Have a slice, train tomorrow; 13 workouts this month → 16 next. His 15-year-old neighbour would sign a contract for "no money for 10 years, then a guaranteed million", but nobody lives that way. Who you become can't be taken. [▶ 28:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=1686s)
- **The one move that makes the rest irrelevant** · He barely writes goals down; he spends his time finding the one chess move that makes other problems vanish (e.g. building a personal brand), then ruthlessly does those activities. On AI: humans + tools vs humans + tools is fine; if it's humans vs machines, nothing he does changes it, so he does today's work. [▶ 36:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=2165s)
- **Big goals without big work = entitlement** · "Work + big goals = ambition. Lazy + big goals = entitlement." Desire changes nothing; translate everything into behaviour. "I want to help 10 million people get fit" from a one-gym owner: no you don't, you say it because people nod. He rejects manifestation and worthiness talk; the comforting truth is you can be undeserving and still get it by doing what gets it. More people find out → more buy; better offer → more buy. [▶ 40:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=2405s)
- **People who say slow down** · They have their dream of who you should be; as you level up people come with you or fall off. Anxiety = many plans, few priorities → force-rank. Strategy is a fancy word for priorities. For each goal define input → output; for books, take one action before reading the next ("learning = same condition, new behaviour"). Most owners make money by accident; find the channel that drives 90% and 10× it. [▶ 45:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=2705s)
- **Service businesses = training and culture** · Gyms, salons, massage are hard to scale because profit depends on the people; a 70-member gym is probably breaking even with the owner working 80 hours: promote more, fix pricing, add services, check in with every member every two weeks. [▶ 51:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=3064s)
- **Stop planning, get on the ice** · An ex-athlete employee: athletes already know years of work without reward; generalise it. Realistic vs big goal doesn't matter; rational design is a farce ("everyone has a plan till they get punched"). He's never written a business plan. LLC, processor, bank account, ask strangers for money; warm outreach to 100 people from your phone; Rule of 100. A 10-year-old who can't skate shouldn't debate going pro. [▶ 53:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=3210s)
- **Accountability = your biggest fear** · Afraid of losing your house? That's your accountability. His was "I can't go home a failure." Use the 6,800 non-work hours; once side income matches your salary for 6 months and you've saved it, quit. To the spouse: give him this season, or he'll resent it later. [▶ 59:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=3570s)
- **Write what you'll give up** · The bigger the goal, the bigger the sacrifice; you can't add to a full plate. Going from 6 to 10 gyms he gave up the Ravens (and all the football chatter and the friendships built on it) and Netflix, announced on a Facebook Live nobody watched. "If I can't talk to my friends about anything besides the Ravens, are they my friends?" [▶ 1:03:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=3787s)
- **No skills yet? Get paid to learn** · Work for a small business (under 10 people) where you touch marketing, sales and delivery. He left consulting to mop gym floors at minimum wage as an "apprentice" (emailed 40 gym owners, 1 replied), 16-hour days learning every role. Paid a media buyer $75/hour he couldn't afford, recorded everything, could run ads in six weeks. You're worth what the market pays this season. Learn acquisition above all. His dad told nobody he worked at a gym until he owned several; have a longer time horizon than your parents and don't resent them. [▶ 1:08:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=4080s)
- **Early outbound: get better, give more** · A coach doing ~75 reach-outs/day + 2–4 posts/day had 4 clients in ~6 weeks: "you're on shot 300 of 50,000." Make one good post a day instead of several mediocre ones; split-test the opening message and the offer (the biggest outbound levers); give away more up front (free kitchen walkthrough, grocery FaceTime), then "how can I get more of this?" sells itself. Doubling response rate turns a client every 10 days into one every 3–5. [▶ 1:15:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=4505s)
- **Scars from slain monsters** · The bigger the goals, the bigger the failures and the louder the audience wanting you to fall. People root for the underdog until you pass them. You didn't lose friends; you exposed they never were. "You become a success the moment you decide to do the activities." [▶ 1:26:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9OsUfwTTslc&t=5190s)

lessons.t: 2026 · 14 Years of Actually Good Advice — live, ~Oct 2026 (idea from Chris Williamson / Adam Mastroianni's "actually good advice") · 28 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [14 Years of Actually Good Advice — live, ~Oct 2026 (idea from Chris Williamson / Adam Mastroianni's "actually good advice")](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU). 28 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Filter for advice** · Good advice is: applicable to everybody, likely to help, unlikely to harm, useful without lots of context. Most advice is obvious, situational or wrong. [▶ 0:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=0s)
- **Overheard compliments** · Compliment people when they don't think you know they can hear (the waiter after they walk away). It lands far harder. [▶ 0:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=52s)
- **Food mechanics** · Cutting a weight: foods you cut and chew. Gaining weight: foods you drink or eat with a spoon. [▶ 1:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=98s)
- **No-based questions** · "Would it be crazy if…?", "Would you be against…?": people feel safe saying no, so you get yes (Chris Voss). Best for asks right on the edge. [▶ 3:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=192s)
- **Nervous = excited** · Before a talk or hard conversation: "I'm not nervous, I'm excited." You are the source, not the thing being happened to. [▶ 4:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=243s)
- **Social proof for compliance** · "Most of you already did it, a few haven't, you know who you are." Make not-doing it the odd-one-out position. [▶ 4:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=279s)
- **Inbound = bids for time** · You can't answer every DM, text, call or email; feel zero guilt. Messages are bids for your time; you have a fixed budget. [▶ 5:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=326s)
- **Forced fizzle** · End a friendship without confrontation by slowing your response time. [▶ 6:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=366s)
- **Handshake** · Firm without crushing: sink your webbing deep, then squeeze. [▶ 6:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=401s)
- **Pack of gum** · Meeting 10–15 new people: offer each a piece. Cheapest reciprocity there is. [▶ 7:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=439s)
- **Who–what–when** · No meeting ends without who does what by when. [▶ 7:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=475s)
- **Say your flaws first** · To be believed about a strength, list real weaknesses first (relatable + credible). Works in copy. [▶ 8:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=497s)
- **"What would it take?"** · Don't ask "can you?"; ask "what would it take to…?". You get the price of the thing and decide if it's worth it, instead of them deciding your priorities for you. [▶ 9:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=545s)
- **Stage** · First time on stage: headset > lapel > handheld. [▶ 10:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=613s)
- **Letters > gifts** · A one-page heartfelt letter beats a gift that sparkles. Leila kept every letter; gifts got thrown away. People want your time and attention. [▶ 11:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=663s)
- **Clean to calm** · Emotionally stressed? Clean your environment: room, car, desk, desktop, inboxes. Shower: grooming lowers stress across species. [▶ 11:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=717s)
- **Desk** · Shoulder pain at a desk: desk at lap height, sideways (vertical) mouse, screen at eye level. Solved what $20k of PT didn't. [▶ 12:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=775s)
- **Earplugs** · Learn to sleep with earplugs (3–5 days to adapt) → sleep anywhere for life. Highest-ROI sleep habit. [▶ 13:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=823s)
- **Best human as leader** · Promote the best human, not the best performer: you lose the production and maybe gain a bad leader. [▶ 15:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=919s)
- **Hard path rule** · Choosing between a hard and an easy path: pick the hard one. If the easy path were right, you wouldn't be debating. You're only hesitating because the right one will hurt. [▶ 16:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=962s)
- **First chapter test** · Read chapter 1 to decide if a book is worth finishing; it's the most edited part. Abandon guilt-free. [▶ 16:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=984s)
- **Read + listen** · Read and listen to a book at the same time: faster, more focus, more retained. [▶ 17:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=1022s)
- **Decide by elimination** · Big decision (career, spouse, business)? List what you DON'T want first. Filters shrink the ocean. [▶ 17:34](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=1054s)
- **Bad news: brace them** · "This isn't going to be a fun conversation." It lowers their pain and calms your nerves. Doctors are trained to do it. [▶ 18:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=1124s)
- **Spouse** · Pick someone who pushes you to the best version of you, not the most comfortable version. [▶ 19:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=1189s)
- **Sales: digging for pain** · Alternate "Can you give me an example?" and "Tell me more about that." until you hit the kernel your product solves. People love talking about themselves; "tell me more" is a soft command. [▶ 20:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=1258s)
- **Fast cash, 3 sources** · (1) Prepayments from current clients for a small discount; (2) past clients: "I owe you money", credit their past spend toward a bigger package; (3) whole list: giveaway / buy-X-get-Y / ultra-limited prepaid 1:1 offer (5 spots). If you just need money: drive Uber hours, or ask your employer what extra project would be worth it. [▶ 23:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPHn-nW30QU&t=1381s)
- (Rest of the stream: cash-flow Q&A.)

lessons.t: 2026 · Advice for Hard Days (1/0 LIVE, episode 1, call-in format) · 22 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Advice for Hard Days (1/0 LIVE, episode 1, call-in format)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc). 22 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Believe** · Despite everything hard, you have to believe with all your heart that you'll make it. [▶ 0:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=0s)
- **One path** · Pursuing several business paths at once virtually guarantees none succeeds. The hard part is choosing one and committing despite uncertainty; wishing entrepreneurship were certain is what causes the suffering. [▶ 1:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=119s)
- **Stack knowledge in one vertical** · The richest people he knows stayed in one space for decades: compounding comes from depth. Scaling what you already know (location 2) is as challenging as a new model but you keep your learnings. Test whether success was you or your system: replicate it with hired people. [▶ 4:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=275s)
- **Breathe first** · Grand vision with no capital? The giants (Bezos, Gates, Zuckerberg) started well capitalised. Get your head above water with a simple income business first, so you can breathe long enough to build something big. You might also just like it. [▶ 8:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=486s)
- **Strategy = prioritisation** · Allocating limited resources against unlimited options: narrow the problem until you can solve it completely (Amazon → books, Facebook → colleges), then go adjacent. Being #1 = all the skills plus luck. [▶ 11:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=693s)
- **What hard feels like** · Losing sleep, doubting, stressing about bills, an unfinished to-do list, wondering for years if you made the right call. That's what hard feels like, and it's okay. Entrepreneurship = a known cost paid daily for an unknown payoff, sometimes years away, and the payoff isn't always money. [▶ 13:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=805s)
- **Looking back = progress** · When last year's work looks dumb, that IS the progress: you are the work. [▶ 15:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=905s)
- **The universe stays silent** · Waiting for a guarantee before acting = talking to the dead. Talk to the marketplace: it always answers. [▶ 17:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=1063s)
- **Controllable goals** · Make big goals about actions you control, not outcomes you don't. "Sell 10,000 or die in 12 months: what would you do?" Then commit to the actions (e.g. 4 hours of promotion a day) and judge success by adherence. Doing it all and selling 999 isn't failure; you learn the 1–2 things that work, then do 100× more. "Don't do your best. Do what is required." The market recognises anyone putting 4 hours a day into one thing. [▶ 19:21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=1161s)
- **How to keep going after loss** · A caller lost a grandfather and a relationship and still spoke to thousands with a smile: "You're asking how to do something you've already done." You keep living by keeping living. Getting over someone takes exactly as long as you decide. No epic hero without epic monsters (Shoe Dog = 30 years of being kicked). When you die only the story remains: make it epic. Either you keep going or you die; if you don't die, you succeeded. "Don't judge yourself by how you feel. Judge yourself by what you do despite how you feel." The first audience is the person in the mirror. [▶ 23:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=1408s)
- **Give in public, sell in private** · Keep giving value publicly; light calls to action in DMs, stories and comments. [▶ 29:34](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=1774s)
- **Nothing to lose = dangerous** · With your back against the wall you have nothing to lose, which makes you the most dangerous competitor: people with something to lose stop taking gambles. Every call, door, cold email is a free scratch-off ticket. The price of yes is a hundred nos; pay it and you get as many yeses as you want. [▶ 31:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=1883s)
- **Loneliness as you grow** · Join a community. [▶ 35:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=2124s)
- **Friends as you grow** · Get physically and online around people doing what you do; go on "friend dates" and be willing to be rejected. His friend test: do they make me better, and do they have my best interests at heart? Real friends want you to take the hill more than they want a reply; at his level there are zero social obligations and a 3-day silence is no drama. [▶ 35:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=2132s)
- **The lonely middle** · Too big for the old group, not big enough for the next. Everyone who accomplished anything walked through it. Find the givers in communities (givers spot givers) and give first, even if 9 of 10 give nothing back. Fewer in-person friends is a price tag: pay it or don't. [▶ 39:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=2357s)
- **Back on the horse** · A caller went back to a 9-to-5 after 3 years of business debt with 4 kids: wise, not failure. Get back on the horse before fear sets in; Rocky: it's how hard you can get hit and keep moving forward. Hormozi lost everything twice. [▶ 42:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=2530s)
- **The real gap: promotion** · The caller had a skill in demand but never promoted 4 hours a day. Nights: timer on, 4 hours of content + outreach. Solo service = all promotion at the start. Reach out to 10,000 people and you'll have the business you want, even if you're bad at it; most providers are bean-counters, not promoters. Partner with adjacent businesses for referrals. Content early = lead nurture for your outreach, not lead gen. [▶ 46:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=2767s)
- **Life is hard** · "Life is hard. Believing it should be easy makes it harder." Naval: desire is a contract to be unhappy until you get what you want. [▶ 51:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=3076s)
- **Find the hidden expectation** · On a sad day he asks: what spoken or unspoken expectation of the universe is unfulfilled, and is it reasonable? Usually it isn't. [▶ 52:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=3121s)
- **Deserve nothing** · "Deserving is the opposite of gratitude." Believing you deserve something turns a gift into an expectation, like spitting on a gift. "I deserve nothing and I'm grateful for everything." [▶ 52:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=3157s)
- **Pain is the price** · It isn't pain tolerance; it's reframing pain as reality, expected, the price you chose for what you want (the $500 Nikes). The founder's job is what's left over: the terrible conversations and the never-seen-before problems. Scars accumulate into pattern recognition. It doesn't suck less higher up; you get used to it. A legal threat means you finally have something worth taking. "Nothing says stagnation like a comfortable entrepreneur." Growing pains = breaking the old self and feeling every crack. [▶ 53:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=3222s)
- **Not alone** · Despite how lonely it feels, you're not alone. [▶ 58:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cw_BR6utgc&t=3489s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Answering Your Sales Question Live (Aug 2026) · 15 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Answering Your Sales Question Live (Aug 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4). 15 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Too small to plan an exit** · "I don't want to work in this forever" is irrelevant when you're this small; you're the only thing making it work [▶ 0:01:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=70s)
- **Turn up the dial** · If traffic (ads), conversion (webinar) and delivery (digital) all scale and LTV:CAC is ~6:1, just 4× the spend and make more angles of creative [▶ 0:02:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=160s)
- **Annual first** · Pitch the annual plan on the webinar, then downsell to monthly with a bonus after cart close [▶ 0:04:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=250s)
- **Reviews as constraint** · Staff "ethics" objections to asking for reviews are often fear of rejection; reframe ("help other kids find help and feel less ashamed") [▶ 0:06:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=370s)
- **Cone in the road** · To get low-skilled staff to follow a process, block the flow: you can't close the file without asking [▶ 0:06:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=410s)
- **Daily huddle number** · Make the constraint the first number in every daily huddle and report; review recordings and role-play. Importance = speed and number of communication cycles [▶ 0:09:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=540s)
- **Red-yellow-green churn** · One portfolio company halved churn by making it the daily huddle number plus an emergency Slack channel for at-risk clients [▶ 0:11:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=680s)
- **Never email quotes** · Deliver quotes live, ask for the sale on the spot, and book the next meeting before hanging up (BAMFAM) [▶ 0:16:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=970s)
- **Cut the fat** · When revenue drops and opex rises, cut the weaker people; the stars stay and the culture lifts [▶ 0:17:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=1020s)
- **Pick the better business** · One operator, two businesses: put everyone's effort into the one with 40%+ margins and a working acquisition channel; same effort could add $800k more [▶ 0:20:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=1230s)
- **Price objections** · If you're overcoming "too expensive" after the price, the sales motion is wrong; frame local vs global cost beforehand with a VSL [▶ 0:25:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=1540s)
- **Cancer star** · For a top seller who demeans others: isolate what she does that works, teach it, warn the team changes are coming, recruit; when he's removed such stars, the team average rose [▶ 0:27:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=1670s)
- **Sell the outcome** · Farmers don't care about drones, they care about faster, cheaper, better spraying; take the risk off them (do it at cost or free) [▶ 0:30:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=1800s)
- **No case studies** · Work for free to get them: you learn more than you earn, get a customer, referrals and reviews [▶ 0:32:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=1930s)
- **Not pushy** · What you dislike is bad selling. Sell better, not harder: add to their logic, don't disprove them; objection handling is what happens when the intro and discovery went wrong [▶ 0:33:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLgSkSQUql4&t=2020s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Answers Your Questions (Ask Me Anything hotline, Apr 2026) · 22 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Answers Your Questions (Ask Me Anything hotline, Apr 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw). 22 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Identity** · People skip what they "should" do because a short-term reward wins; act first, then label the pattern ("I am organized") and stay consistent with the label [▶ 0:03:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=200s)
- **Warm vs cold motion** · Cold traffic put through a warm funnel (short VSL → call) fails; microwave cold traffic with a paid $49-99, ~3-hour workshop with a stacked offer, then book calls from it [▶ 0:06:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=360s)
- **Qualified conversion** · Add the top buyer signal (e.g. average buy-in) to the opt-in; judge the webinar on qualified-lead conversion, not total leads [▶ 0:10:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=620s)
- **Volume of creative** · Low daily spend relative to CAC feels lumpy (volatility = insufficient volume); spend at least ~1 CAC per day and go from 5 ads/week to ~100 (they launch ~250/day) [▶ 0:16:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=1000s)
- **Easy ad volume** · Walk-and-talk iPhone videos reading hooks from a teleprompter app, then turn winners into statics; reuse winning hooks [▶ 0:20:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=1240s)
- **Pixel on qualified** · Optimize the pixel on a step you get ~1,000 of (qualified application thank-you page), not on closes [▶ 0:21:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=1300s)
- **Small market, big rewards** · Slovenia agency at $3k MRR doing ads + content: aim at the US, add a zero to the price, make content about doing their content (translated with AI), a lead magnet like "100 days of content in 100 minutes", pick one avatar [▶ 0:26:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=1600s)
- **Teach everything** · Show the world everything you do; people see the work and hire you to do it [▶ 0:29:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=1770s)
- **Hands-on onboarding** · SaaS churn: do live group onboarding twice a day, watch friction, push activation steps; segment churn by channel and avatar; bill quarterly or annually to match the value cycle; keep monthly for the signal [▶ 0:37:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=2220s)
- **Bow tie** · Service businesses need demand funnels and supply (talent) funnels; recruiting is lead gen. Referral bonus should be ~10% of a hire's gross profit (e.g. $10k, mostly after 90 days); 10 contingency recruiters for a role [▶ 0:49:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=2970s)
- **Hiring at scale** · They took a sales team from 0 to 80 in 90 days with all ads plus 15 recruiters at a negotiated $5k a head; kept 50, +$5M/month in sales [▶ 0:52:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=3120s)
- **Thrive not survive** · Mobile IV drips: emergency inbound gets price-shopped; flip to memberships ("want to make today free?") and run interruption ads to people who want to feel better, prepaid in quarters [▶ 0:57:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=3420s)
- **Business as experiment** · Until the model is nailed, the only point of marketing is reps to practise the offer [▶ 1:03:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=3820s)
- **Up-market avatar** · For 17% monthly churn: define the ICP (e.g. $750k+ earners, a training system, 10+ reps), price minnows quarterly and whales monthly at 5k, segment churn; scale once ICP churn is ~5% or less [▶ 1:07:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=4020s)
- **Shiny object loop** · Uninformed optimism → informed pessimism → valley of despair → new shiny object; push through to informed optimism. "The grass is greener because it's fertilized with manure" (his CFO) [▶ 1:16:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=4600s)
- **Panda Express** · Same thing for 45 years; switching resets years of compounding [▶ 1:19:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=4780s)
- **Same flesh** · If someone else did it, model exactly what they did, then do 2-3× more [▶ 1:20:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=4840s)
- **Learn by problems** · Start with the customer's problem and learn the tools as you need them (Elon's wrench example) [▶ 1:21:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=4890s)
- **Kudos** · He took from Leila: give far more praise, or you extinguish good behaviour [▶ 1:23:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=5020s)
- **Enterprise** · Go where the fish are: trade shows, conferences, centres of influence (law firms, architects) [▶ 1:24:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=5040s)
- **Consistency** · The last remaining alpha is consistency: doing the same thing over and over without immediate reward [▶ 1:26:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=5200s)
- **No support** · Having no team or support is just what starting is; commit to make it work or die and drop invented standards [▶ 1:28:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ooj0V4hpgw&t=5280s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Answers Your Questions (hotline, Apr 2026) · 17 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Answers Your Questions (hotline, Apr 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E). 17 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Train people** · Can't find technicians? You can often train someone to do an OK job in a weekend [▶ 0:03:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=190s)
- **Fastest leads** · Go to whoever already has your customers one or two decisions before you, and make a referral deal that pays them [▶ 0:04:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=290s)
- **Freemium** · Done well, freemium means acquisition costs ~zero and all effort goes into ascension; only 3 calls from 300 free users is silly; add a booked onboarding call and outbound-call new sign-ups [▶ 0:07:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=460s)
- **Channel demand** · Carve a piece off an existing river of desire; serve the flow you have (maybe a cheap automated tier or selling the leads) [▶ 0:10:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=600s)
- **Next problem** · Solving a customer's problem always creates the next one: leads → sales → delivery → retention → leadership → more demand [▶ 0:11:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=690s)
- **Create flow** · Create flow, monetize flow, add friction [▶ 0:13:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=790s)
- **Marketplace hard side** · Start with the hard side of a marketplace (brands with money, not creators who want it); measure LTV:CAC per brand; options: partner with platforms, hire their top deal-getters, run an AI outbound agent [▶ 0:16:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=1010s)
- **Talent agency model** · The grown-up version is a talent agency on a percentage (CAA/WME digital) vs a flat-fee volume play; both work, pick one on day one [▶ 0:18:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=1120s)
- **Tech disguised as services** · "The next trillion-dollar company is a tech business disguised as a services company": map every manual action into workflows and automate them one by one [▶ 0:24:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=1480s)
- **Scale zero** · Get your time on the current unit to zero before scaling it; go slow to go fast [▶ 0:27:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=1650s)
- **Second-place prize** · Giveaway offers must sell the second-place prize: everyone applies for the big prize; the runner-ups get the same thing at a discount, shown publicly [▶ 0:39:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=2390s)
- **Spouse + VSL** · In-home sales: confirm in reminders that they watched the video and the spouse will be there; show a second VSL on an iPad while you "calculate" [▶ 0:37:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=2220s)
- **Pick better margins** · For database reactivation, pick industries with margins and big lists (med spas), not restaurants [▶ 0:44:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=2640s)
- **Stakes in content** · Content isn't boring because tax is boring; it's hypothetical. Record real client sessions with real stakes ("$500k tax bill, no cash"), 1-3 tactics, 10 minutes; study 10 people doing better and borrow hooks, not content [▶ 0:49:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=2940s)
- **Hook, retain, reward** · That's how content works; Dave Ramsey says "spend less than you make" for 40 years, the stories make it interesting [▶ 0:53:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=3220s)
- **Facebook** · Facebook has the most users and older buyers with money; under-used [▶ 0:51:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=3080s)
- **Affiliate army** · Andromeda rewards 100% unique creative and burns ads out fast; build a "self-licking ice cream cone" where clients make 2-5 pieces a week (e.g. instead of paying the membership) using your best hooks; target 500 pieces a week; keep a winners sheet that feeds the AI [▶ 1:05:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A8p2HCI_23E&t=3940s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Answers Your Questions (hotline, Feb 2026, Leila joins) · 24 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Answers Your Questions (hotline, Feb 2026, Leila joins)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk). 24 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **CLOSER on the phone** · Swim school: close the other doors (home, public pool, cousin) until there's no reasonable alternative; three things everyone needs (environment, expertise, process); move the anchor in time ("should have started last month"); send a payment link and stay on the line [▶ 0:00:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=30s)
- **Defined front end** · Swap $100/mo + fee for a 12-session $600 outcome with a keep-working guarantee; pitch phase 2-6 halfway through and credit the $600 toward a ~$2,500 back end; add a branded physical item as an upsell [▶ 0:04:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=280s)
- **Referrals aren't selling** · If every lead was a warm referral, you've never really sold [▶ 0:07:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=440s)
- **Volatile ≠ risky** · Seasonality that's predictable is a feature: plan for it; double what works (PPC, crack Meta) instead of starting a second business [▶ 0:11:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=710s)
- **Friction maths** · Adding qualifying questions raises the percentage qualified and lowers the absolute number: mission accomplished; now increase front-end volume [▶ 0:21:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=1300s)
- **Find the content that buys** · Ask customers/calls which video brought them; run the most saved shorts (saves > shares) as ads [▶ 0:24:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=1440s)
- **Describe, don't explain** · Data consultancy: talk about the vacation not the flight; lead magnet = five free 1:1 calls for qualified companies; describe what will happen, not how [▶ 0:32:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=1920s)
- **Calculator close** · Total the savings found, charge up to ~30% of the measured outcome, not hours [▶ 0:35:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=2100s)
- **Fix 30-day cash** · $27 membership: sell only the annual with exclusive bonuses during the launch; afterwards run a scoop-up campaign to the monthly with bonuses removed; consumer impulse window $300-600 [▶ 0:41:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=2460s)
- **Reason + excuse** · Physical kits give buyers a legitimate excuse; can push price toward $1,000 [▶ 0:43:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=2620s)
- **Fractal pricing** · Tiers must be ~5× apart; +20% tiers are undifferentiated. Rich buyers want flexibility, not 10-year commitments; use a tiny annual "stewardship" retainer as an excuse to visit; small jobs get the big jobs [▶ 0:49:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=2980s)
- **Workflows not roles** · Agency owner bottleneck: build an intake that spins up assets automatically; then script sales so a non-expert closes; mine sales calls for "why people buy" into the VSL [▶ 0:58:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=3520s)
- **Avatar sets the ceiling** · Keep the bar for who can be a customer rising; desperate clients make a churn factory [▶ 1:04:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=3840s)
- **Content = ads** · Make more content, run the best as ads; the ad and content algorithms have merged [▶ 1:07:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=4040s)
- **Pick one** · Owner of two unrelated businesses: you can only maintain both, not grow them; pick one and commit [▶ 1:22:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=4920s)
- **Price the front end** · PT gym: €97 + fee can't cover a €200-250 CAC; sell a 6-week €600 onboarding (meal plan, weigh-ins, money back if you show up), pitch the year halfway, credit the €600, sell supplements at intake [▶ 1:30:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=5400s)
- **Statics first** · Statics beat video for most people because most people are bad on camera [▶ 1:35:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=5720s)
- **Stone cutter** · Same work, three outlooks; following your passion still means 90% chores; reframe the work you're doing for people you care about [▶ 1:38:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=5880s)
- **Script the pitch** · Every word of the event pitch on slides, one sentence per slide; trainees record it 25-50 times before going live [▶ 1:44:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=6280s)
- **Leila: commitment** · Commitment is the elimination of alternatives; maximizing options means never getting the reward [▶ 2:05:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=7500s)
- **Leila: nail before scale** · Get revenue and profit per location right before adding locations (rowboat vs Titanic) [▶ 2:08:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=7680s)
- **Leila: ask better questions** · Current state, desired state, blockage [▶ 2:11:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=7860s)
- **Leila: what a system is** · A prompt that triggers a behaviour without relying on memory; a leader must be present to show what good looks like [▶ 2:12:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=7960s)
- **Focus = subtraction** · Remove stimuli so work is the black dot on the white wall; people delay starting longer than the task takes [▶ 2:16:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IG9IWQVmxqk&t=8160s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Answers Your Questions (hotline, Mar 2026) · 28 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Answers Your Questions (hotline, Mar 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8). 28 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Diagnose by elimination** · Dental implants: if the offer and process are roughly right, look at the set call (BANT wasn't asked) and creative; Meta leads are colder than PPC and need heavy screening [▶ 0:10:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=600s)
- **BANT on the set** · Budget ("this is four figures plus, no shock?"), need (1-10, "why not a 10? why not a 1?"), timing (today vs later = tire kickers), authority [▶ 0:16:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=960s)
- **Ad looks like avatar** · Meta finds people who look like those in the ad; show your ideal customer (and a lab coat) [▶ 0:18:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=1120s)
- **Pay the button-clicker** · Find someone a level or two down at a specialist agency on LinkedIn and pay ~$500/hour to walk you through keywords [▶ 0:20:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=1200s)
- **Own the stage** · Speaker capped by event calendar: run webinars with callout ads ("OTs, PTs, SLPs with 5+ locations"), show 10 use cases, then FAQs; pitch a free savings assessment. Or partner with B2B vendors and get integrated into their sales motion [▶ 0:23:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=1430s)
- **Better and cheaper** · Nobody wants to be sold "same for less"; sell better for less [▶ 0:25:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=1520s)
- **Price vs alternative** · A $35k one-year career program is fine when a year of college costs ~$38k; sell it at week 2-3, before the first program ends, so it feels like completing what they started; credit the first payment; half now, half when the job offer lands [▶ 0:32:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=1930s)
- **Kiss the toads** · Early on, meet everyone, see who buys, then reverse-engineer qualifications [▶ 0:35:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=2100s)
- **Supply-constrained service** · Lawn care is a cleaning-type business: always constrained by talent; nail recruiting/onboarding before scaling; at 70% close, raise price [▶ 0:44:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=2660s)
- **Paired metrics** · Every KPI needs a paired metric (speed and quality); if a tech cuts a corner they redo it on their own time and lose that day's bonus; three strikes. Rules without enforcement are suggestions [▶ 0:48:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=2920s)
- **How culture forms** · Define in observable terms, demonstrate, have them do it, correct immediately, praise publicly, repeat; culture exists when they praise each other publicly and correct each other privately [▶ 0:52:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=3160s)
- **Lead by example** · Gandhi needed a month to stop eating sugar himself before telling the boy to [▶ 0:54:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=3270s)
- **Subscription churn** · Make reorders automatic with a default box editable by text; offer skip/half portions; test quarterly billing; if the +50% price cohort churns less, lean premium ("we're not the cheapest, we're the best") [▶ 0:57:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=3460s)
- **Missed opportunity** · Leila's frame: "this isn't a problem to solve, it's an opportunity you made up". Don't risk the main sale with a second offer; once the goal is hit, offer a credit-rollover (ticket price credited toward the annual community) [▶ 1:10:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=4220s)
- **Market penetration** · Count the real eligible pool before setting goals; selling 2,500 to ~15,000 is heavy penetration; add a back end or go adjacent [▶ 1:27:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=5260s)
- **Feed Andromeda** · It runs only the top ~10% of creatives, so you must feed it constantly; build a creative machine from client lifecycle ads and in-person events [▶ 1:21:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=4870s)
- **2026 opportunity** · Take people-heavy businesses with limitless demand (legal, accounting, agencies) and run them as workflows of agents, not role-based org charts [▶ 1:31:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=5460s)
- **Train, don't jump in** · Jumping in to solve your staff's problems is lazy short-term relief; time study, delegate jobs you already pay for, train with decision boxes and spending limits [▶ 1:39:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=5980s)
- **Don't sell "AI"** · Nobody cares that it's AI, and saying so anchors your price lower; sell the outcome [▶ 1:50:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=6600s)
- **Built for war** · Some seasons are war time; judge work-life balance over a decade, not a week [▶ 1:52:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=6750s)
- **One skill** · Get a stranger to pay you to do something they don't want to do; then solve bigger problems for better people [▶ 1:55:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=6920s)
- **Ethics** · If you believe making money is wrong you'll never make it; state the facts, tell the truth, voluntary exchange [▶ 1:58:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=7120s)
- **Demonstrate** · The most slept-on marketing is demonstration: do it, record it, post it [▶ 2:00:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=7240s)
- **Focus = environment** · Arrange your environment so work is the most interesting thing available; it's not willpower [▶ 2:04:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=7440s)
- **Beat the employee** · Starting out, compete with the big firm's barely-trained rep, not the firm: "same price, you get the owner's cell phone" [▶ 2:06:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=7560s)
- **Reps** · His early gym video was awkward; 30,000 ads later he's fluent. 90% of podcasts die before episode 20 [▶ 2:08:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=7680s)
- **Buy dad's business** · Credit your salary toward equity plus seller financing and an SBA loan [▶ 2:12:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=7950s)
- **Career path** · For repeated roles, zigzag title bumps (junior setter → setter → senior → closer → manager...) with pay and perks; drop-off points at day 14, month 3, month 6 [▶ 2:15:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnDC4ZJ0oy8&t=8100s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Answers Your Questions on Reddit (AMA live, Jul 2026) · 30 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Answers Your Questions on Reddit (AMA live, Jul 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM). 30 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Start with leverage** · Start with whatever existing skills give you the most leverage (lawn/snow is just the lowest bar). At zero, every business starts the same way: LLC, a way to take money, a dollar from a stranger [▶ 0:00:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=30s)
- **Close to the money** · In B2B, pick work as close to revenue or savings as possible so you don't sell from your own wallet [▶ 0:02:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=120s)
- **NDA proof** · When wins are under NDA: tell the specific story as "Acme Corp"; play the actual lead calls you generate; ideally, a free trial pulls proof forward [▶ 0:04:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=240s)
- **Employees** · Pay follows the risk you take on; ask for variable pay or stock, and get closer to the money you directly make [▶ 0:07:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=420s)
- **Agents** · He expects people to arrive at companies as an entire AI-run department and be paid a share of what the department cost [▶ 0:08:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=510s)
- **Scale ad spend** · Making ~6:1 on ad spend? Spend more. If you can't, fix the offer, find cheaper channels, or (his preference) expand the money model [▶ 0:09:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=580s)
- **LTV arms race** · Long term, businesses compete on lifetime gross profit per customer (a Starbucks customer is worth ~$14k); short-term disruptors win on cheaper distribution (Gymshark, First Form) [▶ 0:10:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=640s)
- **Rate limiter** · Effort not aimed at the constraint raises the system's potential, not its throughput (Elon: focus only on the rate limiter) [▶ 0:13:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=780s)
- **AI is one lever** · AI didn't erase other leverage (brand, capital, people). If your AI use isn't making more money, you still aren't on the constraint; AI agrees with you too readily for strategic decisions [▶ 0:14:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=850s)
- **Other leverage** · One-on-one → one-to-many (~10×), templated delivery (3-5×), one-to-many selling [▶ 0:18:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=1080s)
- **100,000 outreaches** · Reaching 100,000 people with real iteration and a free offer and staying broke "doesn't add up"; more likely you went straight for the sale on something people didn't want. Start free, get reps and proof [▶ 0:19:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=1180s)
- **Accent** · For a Filipino engineer aiming at $20k/month: get access to US markets; the better you are, the less the accent matters; your licence is like the $1,000 in the suitcase, irrelevant to what you start [▶ 0:23:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=1420s)
- **AI coaching fears** · People hire coaches for accountability and approval, not information (Coco Fit failed betting on info); more businesses are killed by fear of AI than by AI [▶ 0:29:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=1740s)
- **Death** · If a thought doesn't serve you, stop thinking it; he was "dead" for all time before birth and expects the same after [▶ 0:32:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=1960s)
- **Optimizer paralysis** · You're already in failure by not acting, so you're only choosing whether to roll the dice; at 85 a guaranteed regret beats nothing [▶ 0:35:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=2100s)
- **Ops-only founder** · Easy way: partner with a promoter; hard way: do the work you suck at; the hard part is emotional [▶ 0:38:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=2330s)
- **Lead-gen speed** · Ads fastest, outbound next, content slowest; door four: partner with adjacent businesses that already have your leads; lumpy direct mail ("saved you the step" letter in a tiny trash can) [▶ 0:41:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=2470s)
- **Scam test** · A scam promises what it doesn't deliver; state the facts and tell the truth, and if they're not compelling, change reality [▶ 0:44:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=2640s)
- **Haters** · Decide whether you serve those you help or those who hate; haters are reminded of the risk they didn't take [▶ 0:45:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=2700s)
- **Pricing wrong ways** · Wrong: average of competitors, a bit more for less, cost-plus [▶ 0:48:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=2920s)
- **Price changes within a customer** · The first beer after skiing is worth more than the third; charge more up front when deprivation is highest (his gyms flipped free trials into $500-5,000 starts) [▶ 0:49:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=2960s)
- **Between customers** · Same service, different value to rich and poor; maximize units × gross margin; for human services be the premium leader [▶ 0:52:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=3150s)
- **5:1 rule / tiers** · Bottom 50% hold ~3% of wealth; top 1% hold ~30%. Tiers should jump ~5× in price; if ~20% take it, revenue doubles [▶ 0:54:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=3280s)
- **Selling "nothing happened"** · Prevention (IT security) isn't selling nothing: sell the plane that lands on time, guarantee responsibly (month free on outage with conditions), and win on speed, ease, service [▶ 0:58:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=3520s)
- **Passion isn't the problem** · "Too passionate" is cope: you were mispriced and couldn't sell; both are learnable [▶ 1:02:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=3770s)
- **Uncertainty** · Action alleviates anxiety; fear only exists in the vague. Play out the worst case: a job, not death [▶ 1:05:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=3940s)
- **Capture, don't manufacture** · Film yourself delivering; find the key moments (sign-up, onboarding, milestone, halfway, end) and compress six weeks into 60 seconds [▶ 1:08:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=4100s)
- **Fear** · Leila: fear is a mile wide and an inch deep. Elon gave each company ~10% odds and still went; the downside barely exists [▶ 1:10:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=4220s)
- **AI and kids** · Equip children with as many skills as possible; adaptability wins; AI progress feels like it's hitting diminishing returns [▶ 1:13:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=4380s)
- **Define words** · "Running from trauma by working": define terms (trauma = lasting learning from a bad event; ask "what do I do instead?"). People thrust "shoulds" on you; you can change your mind when the season changes. His grandfather: you have two hands and one brain, use them [▶ 1:16:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32fVmwvLmTM&t=4600s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Get Rich While You're Young (live Q&A, Jul 2026) · 52 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Get Rich While You're Young (live Q&A, Jul 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o). 52 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Max/min** · To money-max for a season you have to min everything else for that period [▶ 0:00:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=10s)
- **Compounding** · Money saved early compounds roughly 3× more per decade than money saved later ($1 at 25 vs the same at 35 and 45) [▶ 0:00:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=30s)
- **Skills compound** · Reps you get young compound longest (Gates coding early) [▶ 0:01:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=80s)
- **Youth multiplier** · Until ~30, youth multiplies every win: press, mentors, capital, access ($500k cheque to an 18-year-old with a $30M brand) [▶ 0:02:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=130s)
- **Stepping stones** · Each success is a step to the next: in shape → trainer → gym → gyms → Gym Launch → Acquisition.com [▶ 0:03:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=230s)
- **Young advantages** · More energy, fewer obligations, live for less, move where the reps are (DC, NYC, LA), most adaptable player wins [▶ 0:04:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=270s)
- **Model the rule** · Model the rule, not the exception (Colonel Sanders). Goals are the same for winners and losers; actions, risk and pain tolerance differ [▶ 0:07:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=460s)
- **Goal creep** · By the time you hit a goal (his 315 bench) it already feels obvious because the work made it reasonable [▶ 0:08:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=510s)
- **Churn ceiling** · Ian's SMB lead-gen agency: 10% monthly churn means you resell ~70% of revenue every year; SMB lead gen is "the restaurant of digital marketing" [▶ 0:15:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=900s)
- **Month six** · Across services, if a client reaches month six, churn often falls under ~2%; make the goal "get them to month six" [▶ 0:18:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=1080s)
- **LTV:CAC over CPL** · His highest-ROI Gym Launch campaign had his highest CPL ever; watch LTV:CAC, not cost per lead [▶ 0:18:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=1120s)
- **Fast cash** · Win-back past customers, presell future service at a deal, attraction offer to the lead list; then re-aim the avatar at your 2-year clients ("one year later" campaign) [▶ 0:20:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=1240s)
- **Bird** · A bird trusts its wings, not the branch: don't let fear of AI stop you solving today's problems [▶ 0:23:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=1400s)
- **Revenue retention** · A business's ceiling tracks revenue retention: 0% (resell everything yearly), ~100% (stacks), >100% net revenue retention (grows by default). Sticky businesses are slow to start; patience is part of vehicle choice [▶ 0:24:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=1470s)
- **Motivation** · Create the conditions: lock the doors and turn up the heat. Remove distractions so the work is the only thing left (Seinfeld's empty room, the black dot) [▶ 0:28:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=1680s)
- **Time study** · Key-man founder: do a time study, eliminate problems not worth solving (Napoleon waited three weeks on letters), delegate the rest; keyman risk below $10M is normal [▶ 0:31:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=1860s)
- **Future you's bets** · A $10M version of you would make today's hiring bets without blinking [▶ 0:34:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=2040s)
- **Step value** · If a $30k assessment converts to a $180k project 90% of the time, the assessment is worth ~$210k; don't remove the step [▶ 0:35:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=2140s)
- **Passion** · Things suck while you suck; you come to like what you're good at. Failure and success are on the same road, failure is an earlier exit [▶ 0:37:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=2220s)
- **Workspan goals** · Set goals in units of work: 100 workouts each adding a little weight, 1,000 pieces of content with feedback, 2,000 hours on a book [▶ 0:38:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=2310s)
- **First-time applicants** · Greatness rejects all first-time applicants [▶ 0:40:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=2400s)
- **Right vehicle** · You only see a few steps ahead; feedback comes from action. Almost every model taken far enough can hit $100k/month profit [▶ 0:40:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=2440s)
- **Simple ads** · Home-mods nurse: before/after creative, "did your parent recently fall?" hook, lead form, call fast; do nothing else [▶ 0:44:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=2640s)
- **Analysis paralysis** · Add constraints to the question: remote or in person, B2B or B2C, capital or none, ads or door knocking [▶ 0:49:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=2980s)
- **Learn sales** · Get paid reps on a call floor/door team, or sell your first five customers for free [▶ 0:51:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=3080s)
- **Value is set by market** · Your time isn't valuable until demand exceeds supply; lower price to get demand, raise it as you improve [▶ 0:52:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=3140s)
- **Price-capped** · Price-capped service: sell "plus" add-ons out of pocket and cut cost from zero-based budgeting; small businesses sell on SDE at ~1-3× [▶ 0:55:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=3340s)
- **Too many businesses** · Six failing businesses: concentrate, you have very little leverage; spend your day letting strangers know [▶ 1:04:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=3840s)
- **Spouse** · Before a risky jump, ask your spouse "what would have to be true for you to feel OK?" and make that the checklist [▶ 1:08:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=4080s)
- **Free first** · At 13 with no clients: work free, get testimonials, then price off demonstrated value [▶ 1:09:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=4180s)
- **First hire** · Gym couple: hire for the afternoon sessions so you can sell; trade money for time only if the time makes the money back [▶ 1:13:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=4380s)
- **Look young** · At 22 he said he was the manager and "checked with the owner" [▶ 1:19:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=4780s)
- **Push or pivot** · Pivot only if a core assumption is false (nobody wants it); if the industry exists, it's your skill [▶ 1:20:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=4830s)
- **Learn from vendors** · Pay an agency serving your avatar double to be in the room when they work; learn from competitors outside your market [▶ 1:26:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=5190s)
- **Someone else's dream** · Reframe your situation as someone else's dream; Leila: half your life is good, half bad, which half you focus on decides [▶ 1:29:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=5340s)
- **Fear** · Leila: fear goes after you do it, not before; picture what will realistically happen instead of catastrophizing [▶ 1:36:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=5800s)
- **Never too late** · Saying "too late" means accepting you'll do nothing until you die; older brings judgment, emotional control, leverage [▶ 1:38:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=5920s)
- **Better envied than pitied** · His dad ignored every complaint; sob stories don't change your condition. The victim prize is one you lose by winning [▶ 1:42:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=6150s)
- **Precise words** · Leila: dramatic words make it worse; say "I'm frustrated", not "I'm at my breaking point" [▶ 1:45:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=6300s)
- **What's good about it?** · Leila on illness: ask what's good about this; don't drop the work that gives you confidence [▶ 1:47:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=6420s)
- **Choose** · Filmmaking vs robotics: pick by your goals; not deciding guarantees zero; bet on the jockey, skills carry over [▶ 1:52:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=6720s)
- **Procrastination** · Leila: anxiety, boredom or rebellion, all solved by frustration tolerance; build it with small incremental goals; action changes feelings [▶ 1:56:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=6990s)
- **Girlfriend** · 69% of relationship problems are perpetual (Gottman); make an agreement (Sam Ovens: home by 6, Sundays off, trip every 12 weeks) [▶ 2:00:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=7240s)
- **Quit job?** · Block 2 hours a day to generate revenue; if you can't in 10 h/week, you won't in 40. Prove a dollar crosses the bridge first [▶ 2:05:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=7540s)
- **Fully booked** · Booked solid = raise prices, then build a career path to keep great techs [▶ 2:07:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=7650s)
- **Coward/shame** · Say "I acted cowardly", not "I am a coward"; arrange conditions so the easy path is the right one [▶ 2:11:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=7860s)
- **Alignment** · Both take 51% accountability, never "I told you so", support = keep the other from quitting, judge the partnership over years [▶ 2:14:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=8040s)
- **Chapter 1 vs 10** · Don't compare your chapter 1 to someone's chapter 10; date potential, not just actual [▶ 2:18:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=8310s)
- **Andromeda** · It didn't ruin you; it favors creative volume, change strategy [▶ 2:26:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=8790s)
- **Apathy** · Once needs are met, run toward a mission, the team, the community, or make a bigger bet [▶ 2:27:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=8850s)
- **Memberships** · Digital memberships: better and fewer, consumable value, more ads and launches [▶ 2:30:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=9030s)
- **Commodity** · Screws/fasteners: differentiate on service, speed, quality and brand; locally pricier, globally cheaper [▶ 2:33:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfXy_PzlC0o&t=9210s)

lessons.t: 2026 · He Makes $1.5M a Year and Keeps 1.3% (live Q&A, Jul 2026) · 29 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [He Makes $1.5M a Year and Keeps 1.3% (live Q&A, Jul 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o). 29 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Price cliff** · His $29 vs $12 three-book bundle: a 4× conversion difference. Find the line where an offer starts to feel unreasonable (e.g. a speed promise) and test right at it [▶ 0:00:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=10s)
- **Speed promise** · Local junk removal: a 24-hour promise ("out of your house in 24 hours") is the lever; do the refund maths like an unconditional guarantee [▶ 0:00:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=50s)
- **Price-capped** · Insurance-paid businesses are priced so a normal operator barely survives; either run like Walmart on cost or add cash-pay [▶ 0:04:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=240s)
- **Sorting question** · Ask up front: "Are you here for the best result or just what insurance covers?" Sell a simple add-on ($300-600 personalised plan); at 1.3% net, +10% revenue ≈ ~7-10× profit [▶ 0:07:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=420s)
- **Simplify the pitch** · If your explanation needs a paragraph, it's too complex; state the outcome (e.g. less medication in 6 months) [▶ 0:14:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=840s)
- **Events** · Retreats only profit if you sell them out; offer "pick 2-3 of 4", sell renewal at the second event while they feel great [▶ 0:18:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=1120s)
- **Two levers** · When a price stalls closes, lower the front and add points on the back; two levers let you experiment [▶ 0:23:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=1380s)
- **Avatar** · Changing avatar is one of the biggest changes in business; use sandpaper, not a chisel [▶ 0:26:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=1560s)
- **Lead magnet name** · The lead magnet's name and packaging is the biggest lever because that's all they've seen when they decide; test 10-30 titles with ad CTR [▶ 0:28:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=1720s)
- **Content is the lead magnet** · Content is the best lead magnet: free distribution, warms people up; cut the big lead magnet into hundreds of pieces [▶ 0:29:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=1780s)
- **Webinar maths** · Fix the biggest gap first: 5% opt-in vs 30% show (fine for cold, KPI ~25%) vs 10% book (target ~20%); obsess over the opt-in page [▶ 0:34:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=2040s)
- **Lease, don't own** · Photo booths: depreciating assets with a 17-month payback; lease them so cash isn't the constraint [▶ 0:42:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=2520s)
- **Eat your dog food** · If you sell YouTube growth but your YouTube doesn't sell, your influence is the problem; views only matter once the content fits the buyer [▶ 0:48:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=2880s)
- **Education churn** · Education is transactional: high margin, no recurring revenue, so acquisition is everything [▶ 0:50:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=3040s)
- **Weight loss churn** · You'll never solve churn in weight loss coaching; it's a pure distribution game. Sell renewal at week 4, a milestone, halfway and last chance ("all roads lead to Rome") and offer buy-6-get-6 [▶ 0:56:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=3360s)
- **Tiny CAC** · $135 CAC on a ~$1,500+ customer: just spend more on ads [▶ 1:03:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=3780s)
- **Referrals only** · Selling only by referral means you've never really sold; expect churn to rise with colder traffic [▶ 1:09:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=4140s)
- **Ad copy** · State the avatar's exact situation as the ad: "$1M+ owner, tried ads and hiring, don't want to manage people" [▶ 1:09:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=4180s)
- **Short minimum** · A 3-month minimum sets expectations better than 12 months (contracts aren't really enforceable) [▶ 1:10:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=4220s)
- **QA at scale** · Review random samples against a checklist and keep growing the checklist [▶ 1:12:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=4330s)
- **Local hybrid** · When you must make money, go local: in-person close in a rented office at a gym, set → video → close; local ROAS is often 10-30× [▶ 1:15:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=4540s)
- **Don't break what works** · If your current funnel already returns 4×, don't switch: double the spend and add DM setters [▶ 1:20:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=4850s)
- **Get them to month six** · Churn after month six is ~2%/month across memberships; drag clients past day 30, 90 and 180 [▶ 1:26:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=5160s)
- **Expectations** · People leave when expectations don't match reality; balance big promises with honest ones [▶ 1:31:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=5490s)
- **Remote local** · Transaction coordination: run city-by-city ads or outbound to top MLS producers; start with outbound when cash is thin [▶ 1:35:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=5700s)
- **Restaurants to a billion** · Radical simplicity (Raising Cane's, Chick-fil-A), payback per location, career paths for managers, a banger grand opening [▶ 1:43:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=6180s)
- **First hire** · Hire when the time you get back makes several times what the person costs; trade your lowest-value hours for your highest [▶ 1:52:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=6750s)
- **Consumable value** · Prefer businesses whose value is consumed again (trash, cleaning, editing) and differentiate on proven results, speed, ease [▶ 1:54:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=6880s)
- **Sandpaper or change** · Decide if you need sandpaper (refine) or a fundamental change; wisdom is knowing which [▶ 1:57:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lidFtb1Ga0o&t=7060s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Hotline · Brutally Honest Advice For Mental Toughness (live, Oct 2025) · 50 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Hotline · Brutally Honest Advice For Mental Toughness (live, Oct 2025)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac). 50 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Definition** · Mental toughness = the chance that a bad thing changes how you act in a way that works against your goals. It's a percentage, not a yes/no, so you can measure and train it [▶ 0:03:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=180s)
- **Model** · When bad stuff happens: normal baseline → a trigger changes behaviour → how far you drop → how long you stay down → you recover → new baseline is higher, same or lower [▶ 0:04:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=240s)
- **Bad** · "Bad" just means against your preferences, something you wish hadn't happened [▶ 0:05:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=320s)
- **4 parts** · Mental toughness has four separate parts: tolerance, fortitude, resilience, adaptability. Rate yourself low/medium/high on each [▶ 0:05:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=340s)
- **Tolerance** · Tolerance = how much or how long you endure before your behaviour changes; the length of your fuse. It's not ignoring pain, it's how long you keep acting normally [▶ 0:06:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=380s)
- **Fortitude** · Fortitude = how big the behaviour change is once you snap. Five minutes outside then back = high; quit job, divorce, drugs = low [▶ 0:08:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=520s)
- **Resilience** · Resilience = how long until you're back to a baseline after the change. Bounce back in five minutes vs five years. His pick (with tolerance) as the most workable one to train [▶ 0:11:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=670s)
- **Adaptability** · Adaptability = is the new baseline higher, same or lower? Let hard times beat strength into you, not out of you [▶ 0:13:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=780s)
- **Trauma** · His working definition: trauma = a lasting change in behaviour caused by a bad event. It can go either way; going worse is low adaptability [▶ 0:14:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=870s)
- **Profiles** · Max stats: almost nothing bothers them, tiny change, instant recovery, they get better. Zero stats: Wi-Fi ruins the day, huge spiral, stuck for months, end up worse. Most people are a mix, e.g. long fuse but big blow-ups [▶ 0:17:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=1020s)
- **Skill** · Naming the four parts turns "toughen up" into instructions. Toughness is a skill, not a trait [▶ 0:24:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=1490s)
- **Fix tolerance** · Short fuse: be more upset about letting the thing control you than about the thing itself. "I won't give them control of my behaviour" [▶ 0:25:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=1510s)
- **Fix fortitude** · Catch the moment you've diverted. Ask "what would I say if I weren't in a bad mood?" and say that. Remember what happened last time you went down this road, to stop the negative snowball [▶ 0:26:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=1570s)
- **Fix resilience** · Once you've messed up, full 180 back to normal: act as if you weren't upset. It doesn't invalidate the feeling, it cuts the link between feeling and acting [▶ 0:29:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=1740s)
- **Fix adaptability** · Ask "how can this serve me?" and use the movie frame: what would the main character do now to move toward the happy ending? [▶ 0:30:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=1840s)
- **Guilt/shame** · Guilt = broke your own rules, shame = broke others'. Only useful if they change behaviour; feeling bad for its own sake serves no one [▶ 0:32:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=1950s)
- **Feelings** · Not about numbing feelings: you don't have to act them out. Separating feeling from behaviour is maturity, and maturity is a skill, not an age [▶ 0:33:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=1980s)
- **Mourning** · How long you mourn has nothing to do with how much you loved; the person you lost would want you better, not permanently worse. Written after his mom's death [▶ 0:33:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=2030s)
- **Biology** · Sleep and food raise all four stats (measured), but you still have to play the hand you're dealt [▶ 0:35:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=2120s)
- **Eulogy** · At a funeral, achievements get a sentence or two; people talk about service and character (how you treated others) [▶ 0:36:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=2210s)
- **Write to understand** · Writing exposes the gaps in your thinking; there's no hiding from words on a page [▶ 0:38:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=2280s)
- **One W at a time** · Get through this conversation without them knowing you were off = a win. Over time you build a reputation as unshakeable, people label you, and you live up to it [▶ 0:40:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=2430s)
- **Language** · Words are behaviour reinforced by how people react; his vicious cycle with Leila (he got angry when she cried because it stopped the crying) until he learned behaviour. Define your words: what does it mean, how do you know, why does it matter [▶ 0:44:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=2640s)
- **TAM** · "My market is saturated" is usually ego: your ads/skill are the limit. One channel, one format = a sliver of the pie; add more platforms, ads, outreach [▶ 0:47:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=2820s)
- **Red ocean** · Bloody water = lots of fish. Start as the biggest fish in a puddle, then pond → lake → ocean as skill grows [▶ 0:55:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=3300s)
- **5 moves** · From your spot in the market: go up-market, down-market, adjacent, broader or narrower [▶ 0:57:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=3460s)
- **Cost of switching** · Year 1 of a new thing vs year 4 of the current one: switching resets the head start. Most goals fit inside your current vehicle if you'd do it for 40 years [▶ 1:04:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=3850s)
- **Features not bugs** · Every model has a hard part: info fast then hard to scale, SaaS slow then fast, ecom cash/supply pain, service slow but steady (people). The hard part is why you get paid [▶ 1:06:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=3960s)
- **Source** · Rephrase "no good salespeople in my market" as "I don't have the skill to hire good salespeople" so you own the outcome. Some prizes (the pity award) aren't worth winning [▶ 1:12:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=4350s)
- **Cooler story** · At 85, pick the cooler story. If the easy thing were right you'd already have done it; hesitation means it's the hard one [▶ 1:14:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=4490s)
- **Five years** · He hasn't seen anyone really get business in under ~5 years all-in. Growth pain = the gap between current and required you [▶ 1:18:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=4710s)
- **Compare** · Comparing is fine to find gaps ("what's he doing that I'm not?"); labeling yourself worthless from it is the poison. Business is an infinite game; the players get swapped every 100 years [▶ 1:24:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=5040s)
- **Many-sided die** · Story from his Leads book: everyone rolls a die with unknown sides; greens grow the more you roll. The only guarantees: more rolls = better; quit = lose. Infinite games have players and quitters, not winners [▶ 1:29:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=5380s)
- **Artist vs businessman** · Chiropractor call: choose technician (raise price as demand grows) or businessman (systems, people). Learning business took as long as learning the craft [▶ 1:38:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=5910s)
- **Commodity** · Fishing guide call: sell a commodity and the market prices you at burnout. Decommoditize with a Grand Slam Offer (bundle, chef, experience), charge more, then teach others from that proof [▶ 1:51:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=6660s)
- **Up-market** · Agency call: serve businesses that already know their metrics; volatile tiny clients make you volatile. Don't drift into selling for them [▶ 2:02:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=7320s)
- **Predictable bills** · Pay-per-show clients churn on surprise invoices; tell them their tab regularly (Leila) [▶ 2:04:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=7450s)
- **Prices later** · Don't raise price until delivery has been stretched and holds [▶ 2:07:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=7660s)
- **SLO** · Newsletter call: sell a cheap guide pack on the thank-you page to liquidate ad cost; don't start a lights business, do more of this [▶ 2:14:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=8040s)
- **Paid tier** · Free placement model: add a premium screened tier (Leila on coaches: full-time learners vs part-time alumni) [▶ 2:22:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=8560s)
- **Bottom of funnel** · Bootcamp call: "go apply" only catches the ready; give the first module free as a lead magnet and make video content [▶ 2:32:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=9150s)
- **Retention first** · Martial-arts agency: level-8 skill on a level-3 opportunity; find a product people don't churn out of. "It's just as hard to build small as big", pick one worth the pain (Leila) [▶ 2:44:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=9840s)
- **Commitment** · Leila: commitment = elimination of alternatives; consistency → competence → confidence; broken promises to yourself erode self-trust. 12 weeks: 1 long + 7 shorts a week [▶ 2:57:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=10660s)
- **Small dog** · Compete with the big firm by comparing you to their employee #86, not company to company [▶ 3:04:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=11040s)
- **EPC** · Subscription vs one-time: compare earnings per click, then check the cash cycle [▶ 3:05:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=11130s)
