- **Affiliates** · Referral partners: launch then integrate into their existing flow [▶ 3:13:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=11620s)
- **Day split** · Starting out: 4h promote, 4h build, 4h deliver; you're fighting irrelevance [▶ 3:16:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=11800s)
- **Pivot rule** · Only pivot when a core assumption proved false; volatility is a symptom of too little volume [▶ 3:19:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=11960s)
- **Sale** · Selling a business: don't tell staff, keep operating as if it won't close, and grow hard in the 12 weeks after LOI for leverage [▶ 3:55:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=14100s)
- **Double price** · Accounting call: 80% close + supply constrained = double/triple price; worst case they say no [▶ 4:05:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0nCuqu7Cac&t=14700s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Hotline · How to Actually Achieve Anything (Sep 2025, 2h20) · 25 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Hotline · How to Actually Achieve Anything (Sep 2025, 2h20)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs). 25 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Do what you like, at volume** · His media strategy for the year: live and interactive, because he enjoys talking to people most, and you can only do huge volume of what you enjoy. You drift toward novelty, then calibrate back to centre. [▶ 1:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=63s)
- **More is the answer** · Of more, better, new, "more" made him. The question every owner must answer: why can't I do more? The big volume unlocks come right after "there's no way I can do more." "Quantity has a quality of its own." [▶ 2:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=126s)
- **Sharran's 260 events** · His president grew Real from ~$200M to ~$1.2B in under three years; at dinner he said "I did 260 events in the last 365 days." Most owners wildly underestimate both the volume required and the volume they're capable of. [▶ 4:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=240s)
- **Lifting as a job** · Stuck on muscle for years (pre-testosterone, he notes), he set a timer to do one set of three exercises every 45 minutes: 9–10 sets a day; ~15 lb in four weeks, breaking years of plateaus. [▶ 5:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=330s)
- **Top 0.01% = win the stadium** · From his sales handbook: top 1% = leave a room of 100 as number one; 0.1% = a high school of 1,000; 0.01% = a 10,000-seat arena, beating everyone. Can you keep the same friends, hobbies, lazy weekends? No, and people won't think it's healthy. "You can't make yourself exceptional and live a normal life." The secret: get better, never stop. "The work begins when your motivation ends." [▶ 8:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=485s)
- **More has the best risk-adjusted return** · Getting something to work took many tries; the odds the next change works are low. Pour more into what already works. Maximisers beat optimisers: gold vs silver is a tenth of a second and everything. Diminishing returns are still returns. [▶ 12:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=724s)
- **Kemp got into Duke** · In high school he prided himself on getting 91s without studying and mocked Kemp, who worked hard. Kemp got into Duke; Alex didn't. Colleges didn't care who worked less. At Vanderbilt he studied 12 hours a day. [▶ 13:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=810s)
- **The 20% rule** · Changing something that works typically costs ~20% of output at first (retraining, knock-on effects) for maybe +5% later; don't take that bet unless the upside clearly beats it. Constant tweaking keeps you below your potential; left alone, people get 1–3% better a month. He picks about one big change a year. Strategy isn't "what's in the fridge?" but "what do I want to eat?" Many founders use the business to feed their own need for novelty; his best-earning periods were the most boring. "Repetition is the father of skill." [▶ 16:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=964s)
- **Outbound scales** · A trainer wanted "a more scalable method" than DMs. Outbound scales; her real problem was hiring and training another setter. Score bets by ICE: impact, confidence, ease. If one move could double the business, why do three? [▶ 22:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=1326s)
- **Absolute beats relative returns** · $100 → $1,000 (10:1) vs $200 → $1,200 (6:1): the maximiser takes the second, it's more net. A 30% opt-in page will never reach 300%, but you can 10× inputs. He'd take $1M in → $2M out over $10k → $100k every day. [▶ 25:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=1500s)
- **What would it take in 6 months?** · (Elon) Set a 10-year goal, ask what it would take in six months, then what resources that needs: usually far fewer than you expect. [▶ 28:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=1685s)
- **The recruiter math** · A $10M supply-constrained healthcare business hired ~14 providers a year via recruiters at $5k each; a provider = ~$100k gross profit/year. Pay $25k each with a 6-month replacement guarantee across 10 recruiters: $1M (half a year's profit) buys ~40 providers, doubling the business; at ~8× profit that's $16M → $32M of enterprise value, and the reinvestment cuts the tax bill. (Not an earnings claim.) [▶ 29:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=1740s)
- **More, by channel** · Paid: in order of risk, more creative → more spend → more platforms. The launch banked 2,000+ ads beforehand (~2,800 total; 15 editors instead of 5) and spent ~$500k a day at the end. The pain of doing more forces efficiency (best call times, pickup rates). One sale a week = a level of advertising producing four a month; one a day needs ~7–14× it. [▶ 33:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=2010s)
- **Pull up your LinkedIn** · A bigger creator he paid simply compared their feeds that day: 10 LinkedIn posts vs Alex's 1, 3 Instagram posts vs 0. If someone's 3× ahead, do 10–30×, because they do volume you can't see. Don't throw rocks at people ahead; learn from them. "Nobody understands the volume: it's 100×." [▶ 40:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=2400s)
- **Consistency** · Rare because you can only observe it by being consistent yourself. Sales teams reset to zero every Sunday. You'll never get credit for the work, only the outcome. If 100× more would hit your goal: what resources, is it worth it, what's stopping you? [▶ 44:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=2646s)
- **Pool company: playing not to be poor** · $1.2M pool service, $4.5k/yr clients, 93% retention, techs leave after a year. His read: fix sales → raise prices → pay techs more. Ads were ~$500/month: $150 CAC for $2,250/yr gross profit and ~$500 GP in 30 days. "You'll make money for the landlord and the bank but not for you." 10× ads; call leads within 5 minutes (could take close rate from 30% to ~60%); pay overtime; bonus trainers for faster training, but they must certify the trainee's work for a month. [▶ 48:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=2886s)
- **Before-and-afters as content** · Dental tourism: build photo capture into the customer journey (day 1/30/60); post winners, then run the best as ads with a CTA. [▶ 1:00:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=3600s)
- **SaaS churn = activation** · A fence-visualisation app at $199/month churned 8%/month; clients who sell a fence in the first 10 days stay. Don't scale ads until churn is fixed; measure churn only after conversion. Fix: charge up front, second month free if they use it on 3 yards in 10 days (free trial with penalty). Target <1–2%/month. [▶ 1:04:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=3840s)
- **Quick hits** · Sales identity: sell → train one seller → lead a team; "you're a level-one salesman". Don't copy him: be the most of you; do epic stuff then talk about it, or let effort be the proof. Start free to get 10 clients and testimonials ($100M Leads p.51, p.61). [▶ 1:12:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=4320s)
- **Niche lead gen** · Mortgage broker for pilots: generic realtor referrals brought the wrong clients (1 in 14 closes a pilot). Instead: pilot content (incl. humour), a free course as lead magnet into a pilots-only community with an onboarding call, then run the best organic as ads. "It's interest media now; the algorithm knows who the pilots are." [▶ 1:18:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=4710s)
- **Selling supplements: menu upsell** · Staff do a 30-day challenge first so they believe in it; then a free 28-day transformation. In the nutrition orientation: seed ("everyone wants to know which supplements; food first"), unsell (no booster, no gainer; send them elsewhere for cheap fish oil), prescribe (number each product; place it in the car, by the toothbrush, by the coffee), A/B (chocolate or vanilla?), card on file: ~90% close. [▶ 1:27:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=5220s)
- **Don't solve the same problem twice** · (Leila) If a fix takes 90 days, don't pile on fixes at day 30. When leads flow, build a talent machine: hire for personality, Indeed/FB ads in a 50-mile radius, ~300 leads/week → twice-weekly group interviews (expect ~30% to show) → one-on-ones. [▶ 1:33:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=5581s)
- **10 testimonials, and you suck at training** · Get 10 free or discounted clients for testimonials. Reframe "X holds my business back" as "my inability to do X". Can't hire? Break your work into parts and delegate pieces (his team preps hooks so he records ads in 45 minutes). Hiring funnel = customer funnel: applications → nurture → interview → onboarding → retention → ascension. [▶ 1:44:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=6270s)
- **Door-to-door reps quitting in week one** · $4M window company: profile who makes it (demographics, experience, behaviours). Train like you play: freestanding doors in the office, knock every time, run between doors, role-play the customer who slams the door. Door-per-hour targets; reward early wins (most knocked, most opened, best cuss-out). Recruit with truthful hard copy (Shackleton's "men wanted for hazardous journey"): you're selling a lifelong skill. Career path: sell → teach one friend → build a team. [▶ 1:51:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=6690s)
- **Concentrated industries** · Deals in small industries: base content + outreach + every conference ("it's not who you meet, it's who they introduce you to"); build a broker network over years. No capital? Wholesale. Janitorial: Google PPC, door-knock small buildings, LinkedIn to building managers; quarterly in advance. Athlete with 150k followers: you're in media; sponsorships, education (training programs, merch) or equity as spokesperson. [▶ 2:07:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HbwUdqUcEs&t=7620s)

lessons.t: 2026 · How To Learn Anything Faster Than Everyone Else (live, Nov 2025) · 45 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [How To Learn Anything Faster Than Everyone Else (live, Nov 2025)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas). 45 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Close rate → price** · His rule-of-thumb ladder for sales-led offers: close 80%+ = underpriced ~3-4×; 60-80% = 2-3×; 50-60% = 1.5-2×; 40-50% = 1.25-1.5×; 30-40% = right (if pre-call education exists); under 30% = fix avatar or sales motion before touching price [▶ 0:04:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=270s)
- **Services go up** · In services, price only goes one way: up. The faster you spin that loop, the better the talent, margins and reputation [▶ 0:07:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=460s)
- **LTV:CAC by humans** · Required LTV:CAC rises with humans in the loop across attraction, conversion, delivery: 0 humans 3:1, 1 human 6:1, 2 humans 9:1, 3 humans 12:1; cushion for hiring and new people being worse [▶ 0:09:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=580s)
- **Gym Launch 100:1** · Year one of Gym Launch: ~$100k ad spend, ~$10M made; most of his money came in four windows of 30:1+ arbitrage [▶ 0:15:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=900s)
- **Zero or infinity** · Big winners push CAC toward zero (brand, viral: Facebook) or LTV toward infinity (enterprise: Salesforce) [▶ 0:16:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=1000s)
- **Rule of 100** · 100 primary actions a day for 100 days; most get a first customer by week three. Feast-or-famine is a symptom of too little volume; companies doing 30× your sales usually do ~30× your advertising [▶ 0:19:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=1140s)
- **Diminishing returns** · Diminishing returns are still returns; optimizers get the most per action, not the most [▶ 0:24:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=1440s)
- **Speed to lead** · Call leads within 5 minutes; slow follow-up can roughly 4× your effective CAC and lowers close rates and margins [▶ 0:24:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=1480s)
- **Calendar** · Keep reps around 70% booked (never over ~85%, not under ~60%): full calendars push appointments out, show rates drop and no one works the pipeline; empty ones kill momentum. He's never made less money by hiring more salespeople [▶ 0:27:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=1660s)
- **Payback 30 days** · Recover CAC within 30 days so a credit card's interest-free month funds growth without your own cash [▶ 0:33:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=2020s)
- **Pull cash forward** · Setup fees, onboarding packages, bundles, longer terms, buy-one-get-two, last month upfront [▶ 0:37:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=2270s)
- **80% gross margin** · His minimum for services. 70% vs 80% vs 90% looks close but means ~$233 vs $400 vs $900 profit per $100 cost. Net margin can never exceed gross margin [▶ 0:38:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=2320s)
- **Selling from your wallet** · Owners undercharge because they're broke or because the work feels easy to them; price off the customer's problem [▶ 0:40:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=2430s)
- **30-day cash** · Cash collected in 30 days should exceed CAC + cost of delivery; then each customer funds the next [▶ 0:47:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=2870s)
- **Retention** · Be in the reselling business, not the selling business (John Paul DeJoria). B2B target: 80%+ annual retention of the same cohort; 50% retention ≈ 2 years of value, 80% ≈ 5 [▶ 0:50:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=3030s)
- **CAC is a commodity** · In an industry, CAC is similar for everyone; the winner is whoever's customer is worth more and can outspend [▶ 0:53:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=3180s)
- **Prepay** · At least 10% off for paying in full; buy-10-get-2 ≈ 15-20% take; discount plus faster/safer/easier bonuses ≈ 30-40%. Good financing can lift sales [▶ 0:55:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=3300s)
- **Payment ladder** · Full prepay with bonuses → half now, half in 30 days → thirds; align payment dates with payday. Layaway: they pay first, start when paid (his $25k onboarding story) [▶ 0:58:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=3510s)
- **Conversion rules** · Meta leads, in-person service: ~10% close; cold webinar opt-ins 2-5%; in-person rep 35%; landing pages 1-2% [▶ 1:03:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=3780s)
- **Industry averages** · Industry averages are dumb: the average person is in debt and overweight. Only physics limits you; his friend makes 70% net on machines [▶ 1:05:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=3940s)
- **Business = transformation** · A business turns raw inputs into outputs worth more than the inputs [▶ 1:08:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=4120s)
- **Trade-offs** · You can't have the beach-and-ski house; people stay in decision purgatory and trade time for nothing. A 1% outcome needs a 1% trade-off [▶ 1:12:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=4320s)
- **Unknown upside** · People know what they'll lose but not what they'll gain; the worst case is usually a friend's couch. All upside lives in uncertainty and delay [▶ 1:17:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=4620s)
- **Critics** · He's never been criticized by someone ahead of him; judge yourself by the quality of your enemies (Ray Dalio getting roasted on TikTok) [▶ 1:23:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=4980s)
- **Germs story** · Eighth-grade camping cured his germaphobia: he didn't die. Other people's opinions are the same [▶ 1:24:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=5080s)
- **Death** · All failure besides death is psychological; if it fails it changes nothing, if it works it changes everything [▶ 1:34:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=5640s)
- **Learning** · Learning = same condition, new behaviour. Intelligence = speed of learning, so you can compensate by doing iterations faster (his Vanderbilt 7am-9pm days) [▶ 1:35:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=5740s)
- **Skill** · A skill is a chain of adapted behaviours; chunk "business" down into marketing → sales → ... until it's behaviours you can change [▶ 1:38:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=5920s)
- **Define success** · Define what mastery looks like for each sub-skill and track it; if you don't track, you don't care [▶ 1:42:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=6150s)
- **Black box** · Ignore the "why"; manage observable inputs. A tennis pro fixes your grip, not your childhood. If they can't tell you what to do with your mouth or body, it isn't instruction [▶ 1:44:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=6280s)
- **Observe the top** · Watch what the top 1-10% do, not what they say; experts often can't explain their own skill [▶ 1:49:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=6590s)
- **Coats of paint** · Do volume, compare your top 10% to the rest, find one difference, repeat; each pass adds a layer [▶ 1:52:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=6760s)
- **Repetition** · Repetition is the father of skill; hire experts to start at their iteration nine, then out-iterate them. Over a long horizon, rate of improvement beats starting point [▶ 1:57:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=7020s)
- **Fail and know why** · Better to fail and know why than succeed and not know [▶ 2:01:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=7280s)
- **Luck** · Remove luck from your vocabulary; he feared winning the Powerball because he'd never prove he could do it [▶ 2:02:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=7330s)
- **Impostor** · State the facts and tell the truth; impostor feelings come from overstating. Honesty about weaknesses sells more [▶ 2:06:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=7580s)
- **Skill stacks** · Exceptional = good at 3-4 things at once [▶ 2:09:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=7780s)
- **Local services** · Great to start: no inventory, easiest acquisition, built-in local trust; harder to scale [▶ 2:11:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=7880s)
- **SaaS isn't magic** · Software isn't valuable per se; high gross margin, retention and growth are [▶ 2:13:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=7980s)
- **Sell outcomes** · Nobody buys software; they buy their problem gone [▶ 2:17:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=8270s)
- **Landscaper** · Add a VSL before each appointment, then price up; spend on the constraint (a crew lead); add maintenance continuity anchored by the big project [▶ 2:24:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=8640s)
- **Honesty in a sale** · Caught an employee skimming during a sale: tell the buyer the whole truth and let them go. "It's not the first time she stole, it's the first time you caught her" [▶ 2:36:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=9360s)
- **Pods** · Stop staff walking off with clients: pay better and serve clients with small pods, not single owners [▶ 2:46:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=9960s)
- **Bigger ocean** · If you're genuinely good, move to where the competition and money are; niches are for when you're not yet [▶ 2:53:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=10410s)
- **Bricks** · A course that taught you 3 bricks of the bridge wasn't a waste; keep adding bricks [▶ 2:55:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nTkffKVnas&t=10520s)

lessons.t: 2026 · How To Play To Win | Alex & Leila Q&A (live, Aug 2026) · 34 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [How To Play To Win | Alex & Leila Q&A (live, Aug 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M). 34 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Play to win** · Many founders play so they can tell people they tried; nobody remembers the weather or the referee, only who won [▶ 0:00:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=10s)
- **Touchdown plays** · A legendary coach's every play had a path to a touchdown: check every business move can actually reach the goal, not just gain yards [▶ 0:00:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=30s)
- **What have you done?** · "Can't find technicians" usually means 1-2 attempts. List 7+: headhunters, forums, relocation bonus, poach, ads, trade shows, trade-school internships [▶ 0:01:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=100s)
- **One constraint, 10 ways** · Reconciles "do less" with "do more": one constraint, attacked ten ways, all the volume on that point, like a magnifying glass burning paper [▶ 0:03:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=180s)
- **Turbo-bomb** · Internal term for overwhelming the constraint. Under $1M: one channel, huge volume [▶ 0:05:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=300s)
- **Bet size** · Effort that took you 0→$1M won't take you 10→30M; reset your bet size (e.g. $1k/day ads → $10k/day) [▶ 0:06:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=400s)
- **Highest return spot** · The constraint is where effort returns most, and it's rarely the part of the business you enjoy [▶ 0:08:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=510s)
- **Weak link** · Early on you can be subpar at some things; later the weakest link caps everything [▶ 0:09:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=570s)
- **Attribution** · When growing, try everything and don't wait to know which lever worked; prune later to find out [▶ 0:10:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=640s)
- **"Let me think about it"** · Not a reason to hang up. Ask "awesome, what's your main concern?" or "what are you afraid of having happen?" Decisions need information, and you're the source [▶ 0:18:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=1110s)
- **Pain** · Sales locally raises the importance of one problem: carrots and sticks. Future-pace the pain: "change nothing, what does a year from now look like?" [▶ 0:16:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=1000s)
- **BANT** · Qualify on budget, authority, need, timing; if they qualify and still stall, it's an education problem; add pre-call content [▶ 0:16:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=960s)
- **Commodity** · Selling only on price is a race to the bottom; differentiate on speed, risk reversal, service, brand around the commodity [▶ 0:23:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=1410s)
- **Price rise** · His gym: $99 → $299, lost 30% of members, doubled revenue with lower delivery cost. The most profit isn't where you get the most yeses [▶ 0:25:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=1500s)
- **Low-cost leader** · Only one company can be cheapest and it must be designed for it; in developed-country services, don't be [▶ 0:26:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=1560s)
- **Cheap comparison close** · "If we were the same price as them, which would you pick? Why?" They list the reasons; "right, that's why we're more" (said with a laugh) (0:27:40, Leila)
- **Cheap = crutch** · Selling something cheap needs little sales skill; once you raise price you're learning to sell for the first time (0:28:30, Leila)
- **Define good** · Leadership tip #1: define what good looks like, in observable terms, or you can't coach, model or give feedback [▶ 0:29:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=1740s)
- **Observable** · Not "stop being lazy" but "answer Slack within 15 minutes"; if you can see it you can measure it [▶ 0:30:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=1800s)
- **Sacrifice** · In their 20s they gave up friends, fun, drinking, fitting in; disproportionate input for a long time. But they can't know what they'd have got without it [▶ 0:32:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=1930s)
- **Liked ≠ bought** · People saying they love the brand means nothing if they don't buy; people vote with dollars (0:35:40, Leila)
- **Sell the problem** · Don't sell ingredients/jargon; describe their problem in their words, then "I've solved that, try it". Good copy makes people feel understood [▶ 0:38:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=2300s)
- **Extreme niche** · Products often start with the hardcore niche and spread (if it works for climbers it works for me) [▶ 0:39:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=2380s)
- **Busy on cold calls** · "I'm busy" = ask too big, reason too small. Big reason, tiny ask (a short window), like the mentalist's "want to see the best trick in the world? 60 seconds" [▶ 0:44:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=2640s)
- **No-shows** · Four levels of friction: integrity tie-down → card on file with no-show fee → paid consult credited to purchase → paid consult. 25% no-shows on thin margins = huge profit leak [▶ 0:46:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=2760s)
- **Feuding reps** · Leila: put both in a room, each says how they felt, each compliments the other, each says what could be true in the other's view, each commits to one give; never again in my office [▶ 0:47:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=2860s)
- **Aggressive seller** · People believe what they say, not what you say. Ask questions, make few statements; pitch = statement + analogy [▶ 0:51:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=3060s)
- **Price tracks tenure** · In services, your price should rise with your years in business, reviews and case studies [▶ 0:54:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=3240s)
- **Cost of sales** · In-house he wants total cost of sales ≤ ~12% [▶ 0:55:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=3330s)
- **Personal crisis** · Leila: grace in proportion to the goodwill banked; but if a blip becomes a new pattern hurting the team, have the conversation and set a time frame [▶ 0:57:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=3460s)
- **Rain** · Some people get rained on and put on a coat; others let it cascade into job, marriage, health. Is it a blip or a new pattern? [▶ 1:01:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=3666s)
- **Scammed** · Lawsuits rarely make you whole; take your licks, learn, and grow so big the loss feels small. It's a legal system, not a justice system [▶ 1:03:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=3780s)
- **Size** · For a commoditized retailer: make the item a one-of-one ("this one fits you, don't gamble on another") and make shopping an experience [▶ 1:11:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=4260s)
- **Grief & panic** · Leila (on a rep whose wife died): don't expect instant performance; fear of the panic is what feeds it; act even before you feel it, your feelings catch up. Alex: distraction through work is OK, get back on the horse, dial to make her proud [▶ 1:15:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgmRlzh0Y7M&t=4500s)

lessons.t: 2026 · How To Progress Way Faster Than Anyone Else (live, Aug 2026) · 49 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [How To Progress Way Faster Than Anyone Else (live, Aug 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA). 49 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Focus** · A focused fool beats a distracted genius; lack of focus is a form of cowardice: you don't believe in yourself enough to go all in [▶ 0:01:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=90s)
- **Early days** · When the work was too big to count, he stopped thinking about the pile and just took the next thing off the stack: blinders like a racehorse [▶ 0:02:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=120s)
- **Losing** · Losing doesn't make you a loser, quitting does; determination looks like a long string of failures before it works [▶ 0:02:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=150s)
- **Subtraction** · Hardest lesson: grow through subtraction. Adding feels easy today and hurts tomorrow; when you're stuck you're almost always doing too much [▶ 0:02:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=170s)
- **Senra** · David Senra's one-word summary of hundreds of founder biographies: focus. You aren't violent enough in what you say no to [▶ 0:03:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=220s)
- **Cull** · Your job as the boss is to regularly prune: decent-not-good talent, unright-sized teams after automation, unused seats, bloated meetings and threads, extra revenue streams. If you don't, the market will [▶ 0:04:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=270s)
- **7 streams** · "Seven streams of income" is backwards: people get rich, then diversify [▶ 0:06:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=390s)
- **Vector** · Growth comes from direction, not activity. Pruning the tree is how you grow it [▶ 0:07:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=450s)
- **Why cutting hurts** · You must admit a mistake, hurt someone to fix it, and beat sunk-cost thinking. That emotional work is exactly what entrepreneurs get paid for [▶ 0:08:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=490s)
- **30 people** · A 30-person team should do ~$10M badly run, $30M+ well run; his fitness founder with 5 offers does far less [▶ 0:10:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=630s)
- **Power** · Power = how small the gap is between information and action [▶ 0:11:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=690s)
- **Hard part** · The hard parts of business aren't intellectual, they're emotional: the vines strangling the trunk [▶ 0:13:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=780s)
- **Owner vs CEO** · You can own many companies but you can't be CEO of several; don't conflate the two hats [▶ 0:16:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=960s)
- **Obvious truth** · The restaurant doesn't grow because the food sucks; ego hides the obvious truth and distracts you with new projects [▶ 0:17:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=1020s)
- **Peanut butter** · Too little peanut butter on too much bread: spread thin, nothing tastes good [▶ 0:17:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=1070s)
- **Symptom** · Constant fires, whack-a-mole, 3-4 initiatives, spinning plates = a big obvious problem you refuse to confront [▶ 0:20:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=1240s)
- **Make it** · You already know the decision; put it on the calendar and make it. Proof you're more powerful than you think [▶ 0:22:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=1340s)
- **Keys** · Employees stealing the business is mostly a one-on-one service risk; don't give all the keys; learn to generate demand yourself [▶ 0:23:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=1380s)
- **Cycle** · Business cycles like biology: growth → bloat → cutting → efficiency → growth [▶ 0:25:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=1550s)
- **Next business** · It's normal to start new businesses, just not concurrently: shut one down and go all in on the next [▶ 0:27:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=1620s)
- **A players** · A players cost ~1.5× B players but are worth 3-5×; track IQ per square foot, revenue per head and profit per head [▶ 0:28:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=1680s)
- **Third marshmallow** · Top performers can delay gratification forever and never eat the marshmallow; know when to cash some chips [▶ 0:30:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=1830s)
- **Better vehicle** · If your clients grow bigger than you, their vehicle beats yours; go for unique, expensive, sticky, scalable [▶ 0:31:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=1910s)
- **Streams vs workflows** · He's not against more revenue streams, he's against more workflows. If daily behaviour barely changes, fine; a whole new talent/workflow, no [▶ 0:33:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=2020s)
- **Stay poor** · How to stay poor: treat others' wins as your loss, start many and finish none, keep starting instead of getting good, take advice from people behind you, blame everything else, look smart over being smart, tolerate mediocre people, quit [▶ 0:34:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=2080s)
- **Energy** · He's not super energetic; works ~12h, does heavy thinking 5am-noon, decisions in the morning, rests when output per hour drops [▶ 0:35:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=2140s)
- **Five years** · Bootstrapped founders take ~5 years to understand what's going on; the Rocky montage can last six years [▶ 0:37:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=2250s)
- **One source** · Pick a high-signal source who's achieved what you want and helped others do it; copy them fully before you iterate [▶ 0:39:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=2340s)
- **Test vs model** · Test prices instead of guessing, but don't test everything: an accurate model of reality lets you decide faster than data [▶ 0:40:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=2400s)
- **Lists** · List quality: buy several lists, measure connect rate and % ideal customers, buy more of the winner [▶ 0:41:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=2510s)
- **Same spot** · Be more afraid of being in the same position a year from now than of the scary decision now [▶ 0:42:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=2560s)
- **Urgency** · Urgency comes from the top; the speed of the boss = speed of decisions = data × accurate models. If you won't get more info, decide now (wait out anger first) [▶ 0:43:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=2620s)
- **Replay** · Replaying a video game level is 6× faster because the decisions are pre-made; that's what experience is [▶ 0:46:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=2800s)
- **Overexpansion** · Overexpansion usually means under-talented team or training; rebuild by making the food good again [▶ 0:49:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=2970s)
- **Commodity service** · Outbid market: own deal flow plus a Grand Slam Offer on everything around the core service [▶ 0:50:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=3030s)
- **Content** · Nobody cares about the hair and makeup; good educational content is a bargain: it saves more time than it costs [▶ 0:52:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=3130s)
- **Standards** · Get rich by having higher standards than your customers and charging a lot for it [▶ 0:53:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=3220s)
- **Capital** · If the opportunity is good enough, money appears; if it doesn't, the opportunity isn't good enough [▶ 0:55:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=3300s)
- **Models** · Mental models come from volume: talk to 1,000 owners and you know it's one of five things [▶ 0:55:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=3350s)
- **Violence** · Be unreasonable; many people are 6 inches from gold. In the pursuit of everything you get nothing [▶ 0:56:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=3410s)
- **Family** · Do business with family like strangers; the deal must make sense even if you weren't related (he made Leila's offer stand on its own) [▶ 0:57:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=3460s)
- **Ads ELI5** · New service ads: attraction offer (free/giveaway) → do it free for 5-10 people and film it → use as creative → Meta instant forms → sheet + phone ping → call within 5 minutes [▶ 1:00:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=3600s)
- **Goals filter** · Too many opportunities look good because your goals are too small; raise the goal and fewer pass the bar [▶ 1:04:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=3890s)
- **Dumb hires** · Signs you hire too low: stupid rules, doing their work, team slowing, revenue per head falling, liking them less [▶ 1:07:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=4020s)
- **Consumption test** · While consuming, ask: what will this change about what I do? If nothing, stop [▶ 1:08:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=4120s)
- **Teach** · One point, many examples (stat, story, analogy, personal); communication's only point is to change behaviour; define it in observable terms and if-then rules [▶ 1:09:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=4180s)
- **Soft** · Compared with people centuries ago, most of us are soft; don't use their standard for hard work [▶ 1:13:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=4420s)
- **Updates** · Long lead times: airline-delay method, update often even when there's no change [▶ 1:14:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=4490s)
- **Certain first** · Exhaust the certain growth path before cracking a new channel; the first pill costs billions, the second cents [▶ 1:16:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ehmBlLNGgsA&t=4560s)

lessons.t: 2026 · How To Think Like The Top 1% | Sales Masterclass (live, Aug 2026) · 37 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [How To Think Like The Top 1% | Sales Masterclass (live, Aug 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc). 37 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Counterintuitive** · Big sticking points have counterintuitive solutions; you start with the intuitive one, and sometimes that's exactly the trap (the motion-activated sprinkler for the neighbour's dog) [▶ 0:00:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=10s)
- **Pay more** · If labour costs too much, you're probably paying too little: A players cost 25-50% more but are worth 3-5 B players (Henry Ford) [▶ 0:02:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=120s)
- **Fewer products** · Sell fewer products to make more money: better product, clearer avatar, clearer message [▶ 0:03:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=190s)
- **Narrower** · Go narrower, not broader: time management for everyone ~$19, for outbound reps selling power tools ~$10k (Dan Kennedy). Earn the right to go broad [▶ 0:04:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=250s)
- **Hear more no** · To make more profit, hear no more often: at 80% close, raise price; double price with 25% fewer closes = more revenue and lower delivery cost [▶ 0:07:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=420s)
- **Test price often** · Profitability tracks how often a company tests price (never < annually < quarterly < real time) [▶ 0:08:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=520s)
- **More before new** · Doing more of what works is the highest risk-adjusted move. Think in zeros, not doubles: 10× volume forces a different solution [▶ 0:09:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=540s)
- **The crumb** · A second plumber on Google PPC didn't halve your pie; you own a quarter of one crumb out of hundreds of channels. Your biggest competitor is irrelevance [▶ 0:11:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=690s)
- **Add friction** · More friction usually makes more money. Money Models launch: lead campaign leads cost ~$4 worth ~$20; pre-order campaign leads cost ~$17 worth ~$189 [▶ 0:13:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=780s)
- **One year later** · His best Gym Launch campaign (one-year-later results) had the highest cost per call and the best customers; unify marketing and sales as "acquisition" [▶ 0:15:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=940s)
- **Hire slower** · Grow faster by taking longer to hire; replacing a bad leader often means replacing half their team [▶ 0:17:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=1070s)
- **Fire the toxic star** · Remove a high producer who breaks the culture; everyone else steps up [▶ 0:19:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=1170s)
- **Cut supply** · To raise demand, cut supply: cohorts, waitlists, rotating start dates, limited drops [▶ 0:20:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=1230s)
- **Give the best free** · Give away good stuff others charge for before asking for money [▶ 0:21:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=1310s)
- **Logic trap** · Where you get stuck is where the logical solution is wrong (Rory Sutherland's elevator mirrors) [▶ 0:22:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=1360s)
- **Unscalable first** · Do it manually first: question, delete, simplify, accelerate, then automate; humans are a cost/return question, not "unscalable" [▶ 0:24:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=1460s)
- **High risk, high return** · Absurd LTV:CAC in regulated niches comes with volatility; follow platform rules or expect whack-a-mole, bank good months [▶ 0:32:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=1960s)
- **One change at a time** · New baby plus remote management: don't add a second location; prove the remote model first [▶ 0:35:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=2110s)
- **Demos** · Demos are fine if tight: use discovery to find the one reason they buy (most buyers are single-issue voters) and demo only that [▶ 0:37:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=2220s)
- **Proof hierarchy** · Live > recorded, in person > digital, similar to the prospect > different, big > small, many > few, recent > old; show mostly proof matching your typical customer's goal [▶ 0:40:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=2450s)
- **Qualification vs education** · Two sides of sales friction. Cold-feeling but right people = more education; wrong people who feel hot = more qualification. Put education where it's cheapest (after opt-in, before appointments); present quotes in person and close on the spot [▶ 0:44:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=2660s)
- **Hiring reps** · 30-second video → practise a script → group tryout call (tests prep, coachability, team play) → only then one-on-ones [▶ 0:48:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=2910s)
- **Pull teeth** · Discovery's two magic prompts: "Can you give me an example of that?" and "Tell me more about that", alternated; commands position you as authority. Discovery should be much longer than the pitch [▶ 0:50:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=3000s)
- **Sell the prospect** · Learn to sell the prospect, not the product; the conversation is the same whatever you sell [▶ 0:52:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=3170s)
- **B2C vs B2B premium** · B2C premium is ~80% qualification and selling experience/time; B2B buyers are buying a deal (ROI) [▶ 0:54:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=3260s)
- **Comp** · Self-gen hunters: mostly performance. Reps fed leads: reverse from market value, ~50/50 base and variable [▶ 0:57:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=3470s)
- **Six-inch putts** · A great sales motion drops the ball 6 inches from the hole so average reps can tap in; very high sales cost usually means an underdeveloped motion [▶ 1:00:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=3600s)
- **Commodity service** · If you do better work for less, just charge more; sell local vs global cost, then speed, ease and every annoyance you remove [▶ 1:02:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=3750s)
- **Opportunity cost pitch** · Show the extra bookings × booking value and charge a fraction of it [▶ 1:06:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=3960s)
- **False constraints** · "One-on-one doesn't work, no content, no ads" = distorted premises, not reality [▶ 1:07:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=4040s)
- **Is the door closing?** · Leila's question: will closing this door lose the opportunity, or will it be bigger later? [▶ 1:09:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=4160s)
- **Against big firms** · Pull back the curtain: with a big firm you get a partner's 5% and analysts; with you, you get you [▶ 1:10:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=4240s)
- **Learn acquisition** · If you run an agency, learn to get customers yourself; outsourcing that is not smart business [▶ 1:12:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=4360s)
- **Outbound offer** · If they answer and don't move, fix the offer with big fast free value (his example: top 5 on Google Maps in 7 days, then bill) [▶ 1:16:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=4560s)
- **Free first five** · Solo agency: give service away free to your first clients, card on file with conditions; nobody values your time yet [▶ 1:18:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=4720s)
- **Annual vs monthly** · Keep monthly plans until you've driven churn down; annuals hide the signal [▶ 1:22:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=4960s)
- **Sign maintenance** · Sell a maintenance plan whose payments credit toward the next sign [▶ 1:23:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=noE1MQPMvAc&t=5030s)

lessons.t: 2026 · How to Build a Business That Runs Without You (live, Oct 2025) · 28 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [How to Build a Business That Runs Without You (live, Oct 2025)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU). 28 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Not a business** · A business that requires you is a job you can't quit; the goal is something valuable to anyone, which is what makes it sellable [▶ 0:03:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=200s)
- **Fred vs William** · Same $10M revenue, $2M profit: the owner-operator saves ~$500k/yr after tax; the hands-off owner holds a ~$12M asset. +$500k profit adds ~$250k to one and ~$3M (6× multiple) to the other [▶ 0:05:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=300s)
- **Step 1: self-inventory** · Run a time study (note every 15 minutes for a week), list everything you do, slot a person, process or project against each; tackle green (give it away now) → yellow (build a process) → red (missing person/skill) [▶ 0:08:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=520s)
- **If-then** · Write decision trees for common cases ("change my card → do this") and spending limits staff can approve alone (his $250k/month surprise-dinner lesson) [▶ 0:11:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=660s)
- **How do you make us money?** · Ask every role how they make the company money; reverse the costly mistakes of a role into its KPIs (camera person: footage saved, named, on time) [▶ 0:14:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=860s)
- **80% test** · Graduate a hand-off when someone does it 80% as well; if you do it right with part of your time, someone with all their time should beat you [▶ 0:16:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=1000s)
- **Can't outwork everyone** · You can outwork anyone in your business, not everyone [▶ 0:18:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=1090s)
- **Step 2: managing** · Trade 50h of doing for 5h of managing, then hire a manager and trade again; shadow → supervise → support → own [▶ 0:18:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=1120s)
- **Rate of improvement** · He now judges hires on how fast they improve, not where they start; intelligence = rate of learning [▶ 0:21:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=1260s)
- **3-month test** · Can you leave for three months and come back to a bigger business? Brick-and-mortar shouldn't open location #2 before passing it [▶ 0:22:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=1320s)
- **A players talk metrics** · Judge skill by the quality and quantity of metrics someone tracks (his first great HR hire asked his cost to acquire talent, time to fill, two-way fit) [▶ 0:23:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=1380s)
- **Interview volume** · Interview far more people than feels reasonable, use group interviews; Sam interviewed ~600 developers to find School's CTO. Volume tunes your pattern recognition [▶ 0:25:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=1500s)
- **Learn from leaders** · If a leadership candidate can't teach you something, don't hire them [▶ 0:28:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=1680s)
- **Step 3: leave marketing** · If your face brings the customers, you're the key man. Systems: screenshot community praise weekly, reward testimonials (e.g. trial of a higher tier), stitch sales/onboarding recordings into "lifecycle ads", film key moments, pay support $5 per chat testimonial, turn reviews (even funny 1-stars) into ads, affiliates/TikTok Shop [▶ 0:28:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=1720s)
- **Step 4: stress test** · Take the 90 days off, fix what breaks, repeat until nothing breaks [▶ 0:34:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=2040s)
- **You're not good enough yet** · The real reason: the best people want to work for someone great (Jony Ive for Jobs). Build track record or the ability to sell the future; Gym Launch let him hire at Acquisition.com's level [▶ 0:35:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=2140s)
- **Enterprise value** · Cash flow covers your life first; after that, enterprise value is the tax-efficient way to build wealth, borrowable and sellable. If you don't know where rent is coming from, ignore it [▶ 0:39:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=2380s)
- **Value equation** · Fitness coaching vs a GLP-1-style drug illustrates the value equation: speed, effort and certainty change everything [▶ 0:43:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=2620s)
- **One-time fees** · Customers are sensitive to monthly price, much less to one-time fees; bundle move-in needs (like the storage example: lock, boxes, insurance) to pull cash forward [▶ 0:47:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=2860s)
- **Next book poll** · Options he floated: profit/pricing, sales, or operationalizing life (trust, loyalty, guilt, trauma defined) [▶ 0:50:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=3040s)
- **Qualify harder** · Adding qualification friction has almost never made him less money; find the avatar from best customers (demographics, quantifiables, geography, sales-process behaviour) and weave it into ads, pages, VSLs [▶ 0:56:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=3400s)
- **Chunk up for retention** · If end customers churn, find the node that retains (Allan: agencies, not SMBs; architects: referral partners) [▶ 1:02:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=3750s)
- **Predictive data** · Volatility shrinks with more tracked launches; build an ambassador/creator program [▶ 1:08:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=4110s)
- **Platforms** · B2B SaaS is a safer bet than a marketplace; platforms command multiples because they're so hard [▶ 1:15:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=4530s)
- **Patents** · A patent means nothing without a budget to defend it (he has a 5-person takedown team) [▶ 1:16:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=4600s)
- **Membership** · 12% monthly churn: find who stays, push annual prepay (LTV is 8 months, so give 4 free), add an SLO on the thank-you page [▶ 1:24:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=5080s)
- **AI leverage** · Use AI to 100× your scale rather than fear it; adoption still follows a curve [▶ 1:28:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=5320s)
- **Scale what works** · Robotic cotton candy: 100 emails → ~1 close worth ~$7,500; go from 100 to 5,000 emails a day before anything else. "Meta didn't work" means your ads and conversion didn't [▶ 1:30:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLpLmhWqKEU&t=5440s)

lessons.t: 2026 · I Live Streamed For 30 Days. Here's What I Learned. (end of his 30-for-30 run, ~Oct 2026) · 11 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [I Live Streamed For 30 Days. Here's What I Learned. (end of his 30-for-30 run, ~Oct 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw). 11 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Volume forces efficiency** · 30 lives in ~30 days pushed so much footage through the team that they cut idea → slides → filming → editing → posting to under 12 hours. Low-production content still performed: 1.6M long-form views, 21.5M short-form views, 20M impressions; each stream raised the baseline. Production doesn't matter; audio does. [▶ 0:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw&t=0s)
- **Consistency of time** · Streams that started at the promised time had far more viewers. [▶ 2:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw&t=179s)
- **Engineer the moments** · Think about the clip while answering: land the plane with clear next steps. Open with proven hooks. A guest (Leila) beat solo. [▶ 3:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw&t=221s)
- **Two hard choices → goal optimisation** · When both options are hard, ask: "What do I want to have happen?" and "What problem am I solving?" A hard conversation isn't about telling him he sucks; it's about getting him to improve. Emotion lowers your action threshold: you want to act to stop feeling bad, but wanting to act has no correlation with whether the action gets the result. Pause: is the thing I want to do the thing that gets what I want? Almost always not. [▶ 10:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw&t=642s)
- **Family first family** · Optimise for the whole family, not kid-first or marriage-first. Model the behaviour you fear someone won't. [▶ 12:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw&t=762s)
- **Become who you need to be** · The fastest way to become the person you want to be is to put yourself where you have no choice but to become them. Listen to the people closest to your goals, not closest to you. [▶ 15:27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw&t=927s)
- **Partner disagreements** · With Leila: if they don't agree, they don't move forward. Not compromise: get 100% of the same information; when they disagree the first question is "what info do you have that I don't?". Frame hard talks: "we're talking about the issue, not each other. I love you, we're a team." [▶ 16:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw&t=976s)
- **Terms are terms** · Offered 50/50 if fully committed and he isn't? The terms weren't met; the split is gone. [▶ 19:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw&t=1141s)
- **Working ON the business** · After delegating your old job, your job is growth. Ask: if we got 50% more customers tomorrow, could we handle them? Yes → demand-constrained → promote, advertise, sell (learn how first). No → supply-constrained → build capacity. [▶ 19:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw&t=1170s)
- **Firing** · It never gets easy if you have a heart; you get faster. Beginners keep laggards far longer than experienced owners. Keeping 2 bad people sacrifices the other 8. Fire when you don't have to rather than when you must. Test: if the business were losing money, would you let them go? Then the action is the same now, only your story differs. Tell people when they're messing up and what continuing costs them. [▶ 21:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw&t=1293s)
- **Do what you don't wince at** · If you cringe at the idea of more customers, you'll never push to grow; choose a business you don't wince at doing more of. [▶ 25:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7McLmx73Xw&t=1503s)

lessons.t: 2026 · I'm 37. If You're In Your 20s or 30s, Watch This (birthday stream, part of his 30-day live run) — Oct 2026 · 30 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [I'm 37. If You're In Your 20s or 30s, Watch This (birthday stream, part of his 30-day live run) — Oct 2026](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M). 30 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Birthdays** · Your maturity is inversely related to how much you want others to celebrate your birthday. Celebrate others; don't demand it for yourself. [▶ 0:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=29s)
- **Finish** · "There is no good in anything until it is finished." (Genghis Khan quote a teammate sent.) Stand tall, endure, finish what you started no matter what it costs, how long it takes or how much it hurts, because you said you would. [▶ 1:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=74s)
- **Cringe tax** · Being cringe is the tax you pay to prove you care more about what you want than how you look. [▶ 2:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=120s)
- **Hard to distract** · Goals get easier when you become harder to distract. [▶ 2:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=136s)
- **Room at the top** · Most people are distracted and out of shape, so you'll pass them fast; they're standing still. If you don't have courage, nothing else matters. [▶ 2:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=142s)
- **Youth = optionality, adulthood = commitment** · Society overvalues keeping options open. Options only have value when exercised; dying with your options unexercised is an ant with a pile of crumbs it never ate. The best things in life sit behind one-way doors (marriage, kids, a business). Maturity = the number of commitments you've made and people who rely on you. [▶ 2:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=171s)
- **Priority is singular** · "Priority" was singular in English until ~1950: only one thing can come first. [▶ 4:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=256s)
- **The 10 life areas** · Community · Romance/partner · Parenting · Family · Recreation · Friends · Career · Physical health · Spiritual · Personal growth. Everyone ranks them differently, and people call your ranking wrong because it isn't theirs. Ignore them; follow the law, then live by your own order. [▶ 4:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=268s)
- **Pick your regrets** · "You get to pick your regrets or they will be chosen for you." Time is zero-sum: every hour added to one area comes from another. You will live an imperfect life: you can't have the isolated mountain house and walk to restaurants and ski out. [▶ 5:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=344s)
- **Decide = cut off** · "Decide" comes from the Latin for "to cut off". What future am I cutting off today? People attack your choices because they're too afraid to make their own. [▶ 7:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=430s)
- **Check multiple boxes** · His one tactical tip: pick activities that tick several areas at once. Lifting with friends he works with = recreation + friends + career + health. [▶ 8:46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=526s)
- **You are the constant** · Single people want marriage, married want single, employees want to start a business, owners envy employees who clock out. You already have things you once said would make you happy. The constant source of dissatisfaction is you, because you want it all. [▶ 10:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=622s)
- **If you like your priorities, you won** · Trouble comes when you let life set your priorities and options expire passively. [▶ 12:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=724s)
- **Annual audit** · Rank the 10 areas 1–10, then check which one gets less effort than its rank. His own: he hasn't been as good a husband as he should be, and wants more friendship, so he'll trade a bit of career time for them. [▶ 12:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=758s)
- **Most dominant game** · (from a founder on David Senra's podcast) Pick the game whose metric beats the others: MySpace optimised total users, Facebook optimised monthly active users, and won. The superset game is winning at life, with the 10 areas as parts. [▶ 14:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=849s)
- **Let people change** · People hate when you change priorities in front of them. They have two sentences of context on your life; you have all of it. Separate breaking laws from breaking unspoken rules; the consequences of the second are far smaller than they feel. "There are no rules": what invisible box am I choosing to live in? [▶ 15:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=957s)
- **Getting what others don't want to give** · Ask "what would it take?" and let them name the price. People assume you won't pay a price they never named, because they're pricing it from their own wallet of time, money, embarrassment or guilt. Then ask what THEY want: nobody sells a company because they want to sell; find another way to give them the benefit. [▶ 19:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=1163s)
- **Average = equal attention** · People who feel average usually give all 10 areas equal attention when they aren't equal in value to them. [▶ 23:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=1406s)
- **Leaving friends** · Most people want you to do well, just not better than them. Keep the few who cheer when you win. Leila: friends add value in many ways (support, fun, decompressing), not just ambition. Cutting off people who don't root for you isn't hard, just heartbreaking. [▶ 24:34](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=1474s)
- **Luck = roll the dice more** · Luck is the probability of a good outcome. Beat it by rolling a lot: you only need one 20, the world doesn't care it took 100 rolls, and each roll costs only air, water and food. [▶ 26:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=1612s)
- **Control is partly an illusion** · Health issues and an unplanned pregnancy changed their life; Leila leans on the Serenity Prayer: change what you can, accept what you can't, know the difference. [▶ 27:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=1668s)
- **Marriage** · Their marriage has been "one long walk": walks and drives are where the best conversations happen. Relationship quality with your partner correlates about 0.71 with subjective wellbeing; most people barely try at it. Be findable: you need inbound. [▶ 30:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=1837s)
- **Dating = volume** · Leila went on one first date a week, militantly, until the right one. Most people "interview" five candidates for a lifetime partner. Get in shape, be employed, don't smell, take many shots. You can hate the rules; the game won't change for you. [▶ 32:36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=1956s)
- **Many paths up the mountain** · There's no single "true goal"; several paths reach the top. Delaying the first step does more damage than picking a slightly worse path. Too much introspection: you learn by attempting, not watching or reading. "Never analyse your pleasures" (a boat name): you want what you want. [▶ 34:15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=2055s)
- **Past trade-offs** · Priorities change; a trade-off that fit then may not fit now: just start fixing it. Beating yourself up hurts you twice: it steals the energy you need to move. [▶ 36:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=2188s)
- **Change takes days, not years** · Anticipatory fear creates the illusion that change is long and hard; your brain is built to survive, not succeed. Do the scary thing three days in a row and it stops mattering. "Fear is a mile wide and an inch deep." [▶ 37:36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=2256s)
- **Retire? Farm** · Both would farm: work with visible proof of progress. His gym remodel: no shortcut, the floor only changed if he did it. [▶ 38:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=2329s)
- **Partner who kills your ambition** · Communicate, ask for support, keep your own discipline. If your day-to-day goals truly conflict, decide which you'd regret more at 85. Leila "breathed belief" into him: "this is not the last chapter". [▶ 41:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=2460s)
- **Every position has an advantage** · "Would you succeed in the UK?" is a request for an excuse. Every position on the board has an advantage (5'5" people live longer than 7-footers). If it's hard for you, it's hard for competitors too. Born in a developed country you already rolled about 1 in 25. The question protects your ego; the blame finger has to point at yourself because that's the only thing you control. [▶ 43:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=2609s)
- **You compete with the couch** · Your real competitors are distraction, notifications, conflicting priorities. Truly focused work, timer on, restart when you look away, 4–6 hours a day, puts you ahead of most people. Showing up is half; the other half is working while you're there. [▶ 45:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IPgbO7-O2M&t=2713s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Live · Brutally Honest Advice To Achieve Your Goals (Nov 2025, 1h55) · 23 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Live · Brutally Honest Advice To Achieve Your Goals (Nov 2025, 1h55)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU). 23 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Right words, right way** · You're not making the money you want because you're saying the wrong words (script) or saying them the wrong way (tone). "I didn't say he hit his wife" means four things depending on which word you stress. [▶ 0:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=0s)
- **Sales tone: 3 constants** · Loud enough to hear; slow enough to understand (~135–185 words per minute; he knows he speaks at 185, so he timed when the buy link would drop); articulate every word. Natural tone comes from knowing the script so well you're not reading it. [▶ 2:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=121s)
- **Black-out memorisation** · Print the script; read it aloud; black out one word; read it again; repeat until the page is black and you "breathe" the script. Then your attention goes to the prospect's words: the person who speaks most in a sale loses. Script is gold; no one is above it. If everyone says different words, you don't have a team (95% of sales teams). [▶ 4:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=246s)
- **Two variables: pauses and pitch** · Mark the script with three symbols: ".." short pause (attention), "." full stop, "?" voice rising (asks for a response). The close combines both: ask, raise the voice, then a long pause, and shut up. Research cited: waiting up to ~8 seconds after the ask closed ~30% more. Coach in observables: "speak louder", not "have more confidence"; "slower", not "stop sounding nervous". [▶ 7:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=424s)
- **Ask more times, don't argue** · Reps who ask the most close the most; objection overcomes mostly exist to give you a reasonable reason to ask again. Universal close example: "the reason you don't want to is the reason you should" (no time → that's why you need it). You never sell anyone by being right. Only ~20–30% of sales come after the first no; most selling happens before the ask, and most sales are lost in discovery. [▶ 14:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=845s)
- **Pull teeth in discovery** · One-word answers? "Can you give me an example?" / "Can you be more specific?" alternately until you hit meat ("same leads as last year"), then chunk up: "so it sounds like a marketing problem, fair?" Get 2–3 chunked problems that match what you sell, confirm "if we solved these, would it grow the business?" — they've accepted the sale before you pitch. Match each problem to a solution (expert who's done it), then ask and shut up. [▶ 18:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=1110s)
- **Sell the man, not the product** · The front half of every pitch is identical; only once you match their problems do you present the product. Like poker: play the person. "Sell me this pen": you never sell a pen. [▶ 24:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=1445s)
- **Very expensive to few or very cheap to all** · The middle dies. Either near-zero CAC (sell to everyone) or near-infinite LTV (sell to a select few). Starting out, selling expensive to few is far easier (Tesla Roadster → S → Y → 3). [▶ 28:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=1710s)
- **Sell your time one-on-one first** · At his first gym, one client trained 5×90 minutes a week, ~$4.5k/month cash, which funded the business. Why: you learn more from fewer high-value clients; rich clients reset your sense of who has money (a $15k sale vs selling $50 memberships); everyone earns hourly anyway (annual income ÷ 2,000; even Buffett's research is hours); flexible delivery for fast iteration; cap the hours; 100% margin; it anchors your scalable offer. A second, absurd lever gets pulled by more than zero people. "Not worth my time?" Then fix the price until it is. [▶ 31:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=1860s)
- **The math of the expensive tier** · 90 buyers of a $100 thing at 40% margin = $3,600 profit; 10 buyers of a $1,000 one-on-one = $10,000 at ~100% margin. Revenue doubles and three-quarters of profit comes from the premium tier. List the price everywhere and confront it out loud ("working with me one-on-one is $10k"), then be silent; if they balk, offer the version with 90% of the elements. [▶ 39:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=2340s)
- **Three frames to design it** · 1) What would I do for 10–100× the price? List it, cross out hard costs, keep the rest. 2) If you could only grow by word of mouth from this one customer, what would the experience have to be? 3) Strip everything unscalable but still make it worth 10× more. Bonus: case studies, authority ("my private clients") and wealthier friends who shift your worldview. [▶ 43:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=2580s)
- **Value equation for premium** · Right avatar (not your $100 buyer upgraded); describe their pain better than they can (mine reviews of books in the niche; persuasion lives in the specific). Perceived likelihood rises one-on-one. Speed beats magnitude: sell the wealthy on time saved, not money ("go after their calendar"); priority, first in line, same-day SLA. Effort: map every action the customer must take and delete them one by one; pay vendors more to prioritise your clients. Service businesses only progress one way: more expensive and up-market. [▶ 47:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=2820s)
- **The fallacy of the perfect pick** · (to a 17-year-old) Join free communities, then take a bet. Most paths with enough work lead to success; all paths have parts that suck. "I don't like my business" usually means you lack the skills for the next stage; every business ends the same way: you own a thing that makes money. Most people start several businesses. [▶ 57:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=3420s)
- **Suffering is a fixed cost** · Rich, poor, single, married, entrepreneur, employee: everyone suffers; growing, shrinking and plateauing all hurt. So pick a goal big enough to be worth suffering for (Frankl's "why"). The cost (uncertainty, criticism, cringe, failure) is fixed; what you get for it is your choice. Most people trade their life savings of suffering for a bag of chips and Netflix. "Embrace the cringe" (Alex Becker). [▶ 1:01:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=3660s)
- **Beat 99%** · Master the shame of rejection, the boredom of repetition and the pain of feedback. ~20 hours gets basic competence in any skill; your first 20 hours of selling teach more than every book. Learning = same condition, new behaviour; otherwise you entertained yourself. What you do next always matters more than what you did last. [▶ 1:07:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=4027s)
- **Volume, not delusion** · To someone who "fumbled their 20s": how many dates? 10, 100, 500? How many girls asked out per day? People radically underestimate how many reps it takes. Extrapolate past success: good at one subject → all → in shape → this job. The transitive property; snowball until you walk in thinking "I am inevitable": I'll either die or figure it out. [▶ 1:10:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=4204s)
- **Under 30, no responsibilities** · Work as many hours as humanly possible; dig the well before you're thirsty. With kids you have trade-offs but more experience to be strategic. Every position has an advantage; nothing to lose = unlimited lottery tickets; your chips refill every day as time. [▶ 1:15:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=4506s)
- **Entrepreneurship as personal development** · The market won't let you hide; 10 out of 10 times the limit is you. Mom says "great job, Timmy"; the market tells the truth. The hard part isn't starting but continuing when the excitement wears off. Potential = uncertainty you can tolerate × how long. Long-term thinking is one of the last alphas (Altman); get your oxygen mask on first (three jobs if needed). [▶ 1:19:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=4742s)
- **Sadness = trades you won't make** · Sadness is a perceived lack of options, usually from absolutes you chose ("I could never…"). Ask: what trade am I unwilling to make? Play it out specifically: the cost of his dream was his parents not texting and holidays elsewhere. [▶ 1:22:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=4923s)
- **Say no to stay good** · The price of wanting to be good at everything is being good at nothing; giving customers everything creates their demise. Decide = cut off. HF0 (beating YC returns) puts founders in windowless rooms with every distraction removed; deep uninterrupted context compounds. You get lucky by staying in the game long enough for luck to find you. The one belief you need: you'll figure it out. [▶ 1:27:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=5225s)
- **Ego keeps you poor** · Zero debt in 12 weeks instead of two years might cost a couple of shameful conversations (moving in with family/friends); that's a great trade. We question every belief except the ones we truly hold (Orson Scott Card). [▶ 1:31:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=5460s)
- **Selling AI** · Nobody buys AI; they buy holes, not drills. "How many sales a month do you lose because the phone isn't picked up fast enough?" → "$5k a month" → "If I fix it for $5k once, worth it?" Train an agent on their recordings; it must beat their front desk. [▶ 1:36:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=5763s)
- **Q&A quick hits** · Ambitious people notice you when you succeed: the size of your action, not your dreams. Two full-time things? Pick one. Fresh grads: 100 interviews, research, manual messages, show up; handwritten cards and physical boxes get noticed in an automated world. Outreach: people call 10 businesses and quit; do 1,000–10,000. He no longer cuts the bottom 10% of reps (culture weeds them out faster); monthly leaderboards and small prizes. Don't build to exit: if you like the game you'll be in it till you die. Make good behaviour easy (5-second breathing prompt before social apps; no ice cream at home; a gym you like). The ultimate thing worth going for: learning. Push vs pivot is yours to decide; most quit too early, before enough iterations. [▶ 1:38:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TmfdhOwIzU&t=5910s)

lessons.t: 2026 · My Take on Elon Musk's First Principles Framework | Content & Personal Branding (live, Aug 2026) · 28 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [My Take on Elon Musk's First Principles Framework | Content & Personal Branding (live, Aug 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA). 28 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Quality volume** · Between "make good stuff" and "make lots of stuff" sits quality volume; content is digital manufacturing [▶ 0:00:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=10s)
- **Algorithm 1: question** · Question the requirements. Compare time on task (e.g. 10h) to delivery time (a week): the gap is waste. His test for each requirement: what does it mean, how do we know, so what? [▶ 0:01:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=70s)
- **Algorithm 2: delete** · Delete so much you have to add some back; process steps are rarely one-way doors (they cut colour grading; his iPhone-on-a-plane video became a top performer) [▶ 0:04:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=240s)
- **Container** · Content is the container; the stuff inside is what matters. Don't major in the minors (lighting, makeup) [▶ 0:05:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=300s)
- **Algorithm 3: simplify** · Most for least: if a step is 40% of the cost for ~5% of the quality, do 1.5 videos at 95% instead of one at 100% [▶ 0:05:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=350s)
- **Algorithm 4: accelerate** · End every meeting with who, what, when; then ask how many hours it really takes and what's more important, often "do it today". Daily instead of weekly updates ~7× team speed; chase vendors hourly if it matters [▶ 0:07:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=420s)
- **Algorithm 5: automate last** · Elimination beats automation; people use AI to automate things that shouldn't exist. Test: are views, leads, money up since you added AI? [▶ 0:09:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=580s)
- **Trust economy** · Show-me times: demonstrate expertise across many real cases and avatars; education is the door to commerce [▶ 0:10:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=640s)
- **Follow-able** · Instructions must be easy to understand (low comprehension cost) and believable (proof). Proof isn't in the pudding, it is the pudding [▶ 0:11:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=710s)
- **Do stuff first** · Best way to build a personal brand: do real things for years; documenting is fine if you state facts and tell the truth [▶ 0:12:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=760s)
- **Impostor = lying** · His workshop story: the guy felt like an impostor because he implied he ran a good agency; the whole truth (including where you look bad) sells most [▶ 0:13:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=810s)
- **Authority** · Only speak where you have proof; he declined to be a happiness authority on Diary of a CEO [▶ 0:15:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=930s)
- **Algorithm = audience** · The algorithm is just nerds quantifying human interest; make what your buyers find interesting [▶ 0:17:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=1050s)
- **Whale content** · Niche content can reach exactly the right buyer: a gym-equipment fabricator with ~6k followers does millions because Alex-type buyers see it [▶ 0:19:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=1140s)
- **Be your customer** · Best case is being your own customer; his meta-frame is being interested in winning and doing the job well, not his mood that day [▶ 0:21:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=1300s)
- **Feedback loop** · Volume only works with feedback: post 100, study the top 10, make the next 100 like them [▶ 0:22:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=1360s)
