- **Organic + paid** · Organic leads the way and warms people up; paid retargets with direct asks. Cold paid can scale bigger but needs a different sales machine [▶ 0:23:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=1410s)
- **Communicate** · Write down what you want to happen in the world as a result, and say only that; his books were compressed 4-5× to only what you can do [▶ 0:28:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=1710s)
- **3 questions** · What problem are we solving? What do you want to have happen? What would it take? [▶ 0:33:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=2000s)
- **Brand first?** · Personal brand first works for consumer niches; for business content you need proof first [▶ 0:34:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=2080s)
- **What business?** · Too many options; add filters (remote/in person, product/service/software, sales motion, capital) until 4 choices remain; confidence is inversely related to number of options [▶ 0:36:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=2160s)
- **Person > company** · People follow people, not companies; Nike rents the GOATs' personal brands [▶ 0:39:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=2350s)
- **Saturation** · Med-spa agencies getting 40 views just means they're bad at YouTube: an opportunity [▶ 0:41:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=2500s)
- **Client privacy** · Show results with the brand blurred or described generally [▶ 0:42:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=2570s)
- **Rule of 100 = RL** · The rule of 100 is reinforcement learning with humans: volume → find what got rewarded → do more [▶ 0:43:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=2620s)
- **Lives findings** · Taking calls and guest talk drop live attendance; engaging chat helps [▶ 0:45:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=2700s)
- **Education vs entertainment** · To get customers, educate; a little adjacent fun (memes, pets) adds likeability. People buy from those like them, so diverse spokespeople widen reach [▶ 0:46:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=2790s)
- **Proof** · Education needs proof because viewers take action and pay a cost; entertainment only needs to be good; reality TV needs believable stakes [▶ 0:51:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X39rITUMEPA&t=3100s)

lessons.t: 2026 · Should He Walk Away From His $1.4M Business To Start Over? (live Q&A, Jul 2026) · 34 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [Should He Walk Away From His $1.4M Business To Start Over? (live Q&A, Jul 2026)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28). 34 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Burn the boats** · Fine with burning the boats; not fine with "two horses, one ass". If you switch, go all in and get the first customer from a reliable channel (outbound, ads or affiliates) [▶ 0:00:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=50s)
- **Remove first** · Make a plan to exit the old work and count the hours freed before adding the new thing; split focus can turn your year 2 into year 4 [▶ 0:04:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=240s)
- **Affirmation** · Asking about a switch you've decided on is asking for affirmation, not solving a problem; risk is personal and the world gives no certainty [▶ 0:06:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=400s)
- **Avatar clarity** · Best: one thing to one person; worse: one thing to many; worst: everything to everyone [▶ 0:08:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=500s)
- **New channel ≠ new business** · Instead of starting a new business, start a new acquisition channel in the one you have [▶ 0:10:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=620s)
- **Ignore naysayers** · Ignore all naysayers, including yourself; none raise your odds [▶ 0:12:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=720s)
- **Sales grads** · Rather than a sales agency, find a low-churn product that benefits from outbound (insurance, M&A, pest control, alarms); agencies cap low because big clients bring sales in-house [▶ 0:12:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=770s)
- **Debt question** · "Crippling debt" is emotion; the true downside is bankruptcy and starting again, not death [▶ 0:14:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=870s)
- **Two businesses** · The new thing grows ~5× faster if you go all in. You can own several companies but rarely CEO two; it's a decisiveness problem. Speed of the company = speed of the boss's decisions [▶ 0:16:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=960s)
- **Burnout definition** · Burnout = the reward for the same work comes later or no longer satisfies; change the variety or intensity of reward [▶ 0:20:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=1210s)
- **Raise the stakes** · A billionaire at the $100 blackjack table feels nothing; once you're successful, bet bigger and shorten timelines so goals change your daily life [▶ 0:23:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=1410s)
- **Hunter in the farm** · If you love winning deals and hate ops, hire a leader people admire (not an "ops person") and go back to hunting. There are no rules in your own business [▶ 0:24:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=1470s)
- **What would it take?** · He took a 5-7 year plan to his team and asked how to do it in 12 months [▶ 0:27:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=1660s)
- **Channels change** · Marketing always changes because attention changes; more businesses die of anxiety than of reality; shift budget gradually [▶ 0:30:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=1800s)
- **Old version** · Don't force users off a version they're happy with just because the founder wants a new one [▶ 0:34:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=2040s)
- **"Trapped"** · The UK isn't a cage; the word "trapped" is the lie. A low wage is easier to replace [▶ 0:35:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=2120s)
- **Price you hope they refuse** · His first $6,000 sale came from naming a price he hoped would be refused; it broke his view of what's chargeable. Biggest barriers are psychological [▶ 0:36:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=2160s)
- **Board games** · Deliver the first promise before building four more; offer past buyers buy-one-get-one on the next game; set a learning budget on ads (70% near the winner, 20% adjacent, 10% wild). Businesses die of indigestion, not starvation [▶ 0:40:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=2430s)
- **Anxiety** · Anxiety comes from many actions and no priorities; cure it by subtraction [▶ 0:44:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=2670s)
- **Heavy words** · "Burned out", "rebuilding": words that chain you. Make a bet that makes you a little nervous [▶ 0:49:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=2960s)
- **Future self** · Look back from your future self: what would he be ashamed of today? Let that move you [▶ 0:51:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=3100s)
- **Confidence generalizes** · Confidence starts domain-specific then generalizes; his first adult speech to 1,200 felt fine because he'd coached groups on a mic for years and was talking about what he'd done. Find what you've already done that's close [▶ 0:53:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=3210s)
- **Webinar ROAS drop** · First check creative and the pixel event before changing the model; train the pixel on the upsell buyers; test a $1,500 upsell; make five ads by hand [▶ 1:00:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=3640s)
- **Content = your life** · Your content should mirror how you spend your time [▶ 1:08:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=4120s)
- **Be less lazy** · You just have to be less lazy than your customer [▶ 1:09:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=4170s)
- **Enterprise sales** · Enterprise is the same pitch repeated to 10 people until you reach the decision maker [▶ 1:10:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=4210s)
- **Shovels vs gold** · Biz-opp is selling shovels: fast money, not the biggest [▶ 1:11:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=4300s)
- **Two zeros ahead** · Think two zeros ahead, not one; pick a business that can reach $10M/month [▶ 1:19:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=4740s)
- **Parents** · To a 19-year-old's immigrant parents: he's now unemployable; support without "I told you so" [▶ 1:21:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=4880s)
- **Cash in 48 hours** · Fast cash, in order: existing customers prepay, past customers via an "I owe you money" credit campaign, then the leads list with an attraction offer [▶ 1:23:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=5010s)
- **Channel demand** · Don't create demand, channel it: sell premium to the rich who want status, or sell abroad [▶ 1:26:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=5160s)
- **Guarantees** · Do the math: a guarantee that triples sales beats the refunds; guarantee traffic, leads, sales or ROI, conditional on paying on time [▶ 1:30:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=5430s)
- **Push or pivot** · Push if demand exists and it's just hard; restaurant owner's real issue is a negative partner. Entrepreneurs are delusional optimists [▶ 1:34:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=5680s)
- **Seasonality** · If you know how to generate demand profitably, you're not seasonal; rerun the giveaway now that the back end works. Nail salons live or die on a tech career path [▶ 1:47:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RjIw9M1j28&t=6420s)

lessons.t: 2026 · We get 34.2M views a month (first live, Sep 2025) · 33 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [We get 34.2M views a month (first live, Sep 2025)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo). 33 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **SPCL influence** · Influence = likelihood someone complies with a request; four stackable parts: Status, Power, Credibility, Likeness [▶ 0:02:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=150s)
- **Status** · Status = controlling scarce things people want in a given setting; the bartender has it inside the bar, not outside [▶ 0:04:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=240s)
- **Power** · Say-do correspondence: you tell them to do X, they do it, something good happens; each cycle raises compliance with the next request. If he could pick only one, this [▶ 0:06:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=360s)
- **Credibility** · Third-party, observable proof (e.g. paying Guinness judges to verify the launch numbers) [▶ 0:08:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=480s)
- **Likeness** · Look like them or share their values; just be you and know why you do what you do [▶ 0:08:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=520s)
- **Parents** · Parents max all four, which is why their requests still pull on you [▶ 0:11:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=700s)
- **Continuums** · Each element is a degree, not yes/no, and mostly domain-specific [▶ 0:12:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=720s)
- **Intro formula** · Open with status/credibility, then promise a framework they can follow (power) [▶ 0:15:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=940s)
- **Exposure time** · Two hours of long form ≈ 480 fifteen-second shorts of reinforcement cycles; crowd applause ran A-listers < shorts < long form < live streamers [▶ 0:19:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=1140s)
- **Internet moves toward truth** · Raw, live, unscripted beats polished; his media 3.0 = live + interactive [▶ 0:24:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=1440s)
- **Volume is linear** · 35,000 pieces/year vs a $1M business's 365: ~100× the volume, ~100× the prospects; Dave Ramsey's consistency [▶ 0:25:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=1520s)
- **Interest media** · Judge content by IRL responses from the buyers you want, not views; the content is the targeting [▶ 0:28:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=1680s)
- **Size your market** · Only ~1.5M US businesses do $1M+; 100k views on a niche video is crushing it; businesses doing $1M+/yr with <5k followers [▶ 0:32:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=1920s)
- **Work in the industry** · Spend 1-3 years working in the industry (he mopped gym floors for minimum wage) before starting [▶ 0:37:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=2260s)
- **TikTok → IG DMs** · Best TikTok CTA for high ticket: "DM me on Instagram" [▶ 0:42:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=2520s)
- **Audience fatigue is a myth** · Audiences have insatiable demand for value; you're fatiguing your editor; rotate lead magnets; keep CTAs under ~3 seconds; lighter asks (cheat sheet + triage question) widen reach [▶ 0:43:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=2580s)
- **Pull forward vs fill** · Sales teams and ads convert a deeper slice of the same audience; only more/better content or true cold traffic grows the pyramid [▶ 0:47:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=2860s)
- **Effort-based proof** · With no results yet, use effort proof ("made 35,000 pieces") and document; then do 10 free clients to earn the next 10 paid [▶ 0:50:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=3000s)
- **Puddle king** · Be king of a tiny puddle; the upstart's advantage is "you get my phone number" [▶ 0:52:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=3160s)
- **Learning budget** · Set a % of income to spend on learning monthly, expecting 9 of 10 to return nothing [▶ 0:57:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=3420s)
- **Control the mouse** · Pay the agency to coach you on calls while you drive the account; he learned national Facebook ads in six weeks this way [▶ 0:59:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=3580s)
- **Story sells commodities** · Tell the story behind the product (the hat); less variety than you think, the variety comes from examples [▶ 1:02:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=3760s)
- **Constraint ≠ media buying** · Ads cap out because hooks only reach most-aware buyers; widen hooks down the awareness levels and lighten the ask [▶ 1:09:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=4140s)
- **Media monetization ladder** · Affiliate → sponsorship → white label → minority/equity deal → own 100% (more risk, more reward) [▶ 1:15:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=4500s)
- **Affiliate ad deal** · Offer to make ads for a brand at half your commission; or ask for a cloned page with your pixel [▶ 1:21:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=4890s)
- **Five YouTube CTA spots** · Bio, pinned comment, first description line, community posts, in-video at one third [▶ 1:26:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=5160s)
- **Clear not clever** · If a stranger can't explain what you do, that's the lead problem [▶ 1:47:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=6420s)
- **Waived-fee offer** · Flex: $25k setup + $5k/mo; or waive the setup with a 12-month commitment and a 90-day out if no result [▶ 1:33:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=5580s)
- **Do it to get better** · Commit to the volume first; the pain of effort pulls you to improve (realtor: 5 live tours a week ≈ 4× business) [▶ 1:40:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=6000s)
- **Protect the core** · Test a new content style as an extra video, never by replacing what works; script intros with proof, promise, plan [▶ 1:54:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=6880s)
- **100× segment** · Switch customer segment only when the value gap is huge (50 vs 5,000 shirts) and delivery is identical; validate reorders fast [▶ 2:13:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=7980s)
- **Price education once** · Bill one-time value up front and consumables (community, calls) as the smaller recurring part [▶ 2:43:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=9780s)
- **Free first** · 10 free clients → testimonials → the next 10 paid; earn your way up to bigger customers [▶ 2:48:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW04CvHKvMo&t=10080s)

lessons.t: 2026 · What really matters at the end of life (life & death discussion) — live, ~Sep 2026 · 36 ideas
lessons.md:
> Watch it: [What really matters at the end of life (life & death discussion) — live, ~Sep 2026](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs). 36 ideas, paraphrased in my words; ▶ jumps to the minute.

- **Happiness gauge** · Happiness is hard to define, so he measures the opposite instead: how much do I want tomorrow? Score it 1–10, then design the job as "install contingencies that make tomorrow worth showing up for": interesting work, people you'd hate to miss, long projects that matter. [▶ 0:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=41s)
- **Meaningful work** · Work gets trashed, but long meaningful projects are one of the strongest levers on that score. [▶ 4:53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=293s)
- **Between the tactics** · Most entrepreneurs struggle not with tactics but with the moments between them: the ceiling at night, the minute in the parked car before going inside. There has to be something worth facing "the onslaught" again for. [▶ 5:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=317s)
- **Kids** · Having a son on the way raised his "want to stay alive" score further. [▶ 6:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=368s)
- **Status games** · Humans compete on whatever can be measured; we play status games, not happiness games. If happiness could be measured, wealth and status would matter far less. [▶ 8:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=487s)
- **Hopelessness = perceived lack of options** · Two things got him through hopeless periods: (1) a conviction that if he only kept doing the task in front of him and didn't stop, he'd get through; (2) understanding that hopelessness means "I don't know what to do". If you don't know what to do, build CAPACITY: sleep, train, save money, make content, prepare. "Dig the well before you're thirsty." [▶ 8:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=536s)
- **Philosophy from practice** · You can't be wise without living in the world; the best economists are investors (Keynes story via Buffett). Wisdom comes from practitioners of reality. [▶ 10:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=622s)
- **Death** · Simple view: nobody knows; he was "not alive" for billions of years before and it was fine, so presumably the same after. Holds it loosely, open to being wrong. [▶ 11:36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=696s)
- **Hard times** · "Hard times don't last, hard people do." The body keeps going with food, water, sleep, air: feeling like you'll die ≠ dying. Moods are weather: they change within minutes, hours, rarely more than a day. Rule: never take drastic action while feeling bad. [▶ 12:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=757s)
- **Alligator perspective** · Alligators eat every month or two and spend the rest of the time basking and cooling, and they've outlived humans by 250M years. When something feels urgent and huge, he remembers the alligator that hasn't eaten in four weeks and is fine. [▶ 15:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=916s)
- **Where beginners begin** · Build capacity: sleep early, train while young (easier to stay in shape than get in shape), and learn second-hand from people who've done it to get a good return on time. Then: do something people don't want to do, don't have time to do, or don't know how to do, for money; repeat until you're out of time; raise prices; hire. [▶ 17:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1067s)
- **Trading time for money** · Everyone trades time for money; don't let anyone shame a cash-flowing service business at the start. Price toward the customer's goal, not hours. [▶ 18:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1136s)
- **Allure of fame** · He rejects the premise: UFC events, parties, celebrities just don't appeal, so avoiding them takes no effort. (Palmer Luckey's point: the kind of person who makes a billion rarely is the kind who stops to enjoy it.) [▶ 19:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1197s)
- **Your obituary** · When you die they split your stuff, summarise you in 500–1,000 words, everyone eats and goes to work the next day. What you're worried about won't be in those words. Dare greatly or not at all, you die either way. [▶ 21:11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1271s)
- **The lonely chapter** · Early entrepreneurship is a rite of passage: certain pain, uncertain time, uncertain payoff. Marry the process so the pain turns into interest; interest → skill → you're out of the lonely chapter. Use whatever fuel you have (anger, shame, frustration), don't judge it. Expect it to take longer and be harder. Measure progress with a map: let people know, get them to pay, deliver. The despair usually comes from being in a rush and comparing to people whose grind you never saw. [▶ 21:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1303s)
- **Logic–Evidence–Utility** · (credited to Dr. Trevor Kashey): "What does that mean? How do you know? Why does it matter?" Ask one at a time; it isn't harsh, it's clarity. Define your own words and you'll speak with clarity; most conversation is noise, high-signal people become friends. [▶ 24:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1465s)
- **Take the shot** · Ask, launch, run the ad, take the risk: at 85 you won't wish for fewer crazy stories. [▶ 26:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1618s)
- **Story frame** · In hard times he imagines telling the story at 80: the harder the period, the bigger the dragon, the better the story. Great stories start with conflict (Taylor Sheridan). [▶ 27:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1626s)
- **Brain differences** · He doesn't think about his ADHD-type traits: brains vary like height does; different ≠ worse. Judge a trait by what it actually does to your life. [▶ 28:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1715s)
- **Labels** · His mother saw the same ADD-type brain as a handicap; he sees it as a superpower. Labels and "I am" statements stick, so he says "I express these tendencies" and describes behaviour without a good/bad verdict. Different traits win in different games; find yours by doing a lot. [▶ 29:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1794s)
- **Local vs national** · Local business with limited demand: expand offers and lifetime value (cross-sell). National/online: stay niched. [▶ 31:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1907s)
- **Stress = alive** · Growth is stressful, stagnation is stressful, decline is stressful. The only stress-free people are dead. Hoping for zero stress is hoping for your own demise. [▶ 33:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=1987s)
- **Define reality to navigate it** · "Monster" vs "mother-in-law" vs "abominable snowman afraid of fire": the label decides how you fight it. Concrete words → accurate model → actions that hit. When reality doesn't match the model, look for the variable you misunderstood. [▶ 33:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=2023s)
- **Self-sabotage = misbehaving** · Fix the environment, not your willpower: lubricate the path to the right actions, add friction to the wrong ones (friends, city, roommates, apps, what's in the house). Make the correct choice the easiest choice. [▶ 35:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=2129s)
- **Third marshmallow fallacy** · Once you learn delayed gratification you can delay forever and never collect. Optimise gratification per unit of time across your whole life: hold the tension between consuming now and investing for later. Stories: Cyclops glasses he saved 8 weeks for and never wore; a summer in Paris without a single croissant. [▶ 37:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=2233s)
- **You can change** · Biggest surprise: traits aren't concrete. He used to lead by anger and fear; as he changed and people described him differently, he believed more that he could change. Become who the business needs you to become. [▶ 41:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=2497s)
- **10× better or don't** · A new product needs no cheap "good enough" alternative; disruption needs ~10× better. [▶ 42:53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=2573s)
- **Joy in the process** · The beginning is the most fun part; he loses interest once it just makes money. You get used to stress: what stressed you at 5, 10, 15 is nothing now; the five-years-from-now you will see today's stress the same way, so borrow that view now. [▶ 44:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=2687s)
- **Funeral, again** · People argue over your things, talk about the food, summarise you in a few paragraphs and move on in weeks. Do what you want. Be like the alligator. [▶ 46:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=2808s)
- **Legacy** · People aren't narcissists for wanting a legacy; they wish they could live forever and use their work as a proxy. [▶ 47:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=2849s)
- **Choosing a partner** · Does she make you better, do you make her better, same destination, same way of getting there? Everyone has issues. Marriage teaches commitment: getting married/in shape/in business is easy, STAYING is the hard part people clap for. Love the soul, not the veneer. [▶ 48:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=2893s)
- **Time** · He doesn't think "abundant time" or "no time"; he thinks return: do the one thing that moves you furthest forward; anything in the way isn't as important. [▶ 50:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=3019s)
- **Character > intellect** · Getting rich is more courage and perseverance than intelligence: take risks others won't, work while others wait, keep going when they quit. High frustration tolerance. Smart people who found school easy often never formed work ethic. Spend your first 4–6 hours every day moving the ball forward; over months or years you'll have crossed the world. [▶ 51:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=3072s)
- **Money morality** · Zero guilt about making money; the issue is only HOW: don't misrepresent or deceive. "State the facts and tell the truth." Decide the most compelling story, make it true, then tell it. Money = society's IOU for a surplus you created through voluntary exchange. [▶ 52:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=3174s)
- **Volume first** · The Beatles played tiny bars nightly for years; Seinfeld too. "Post and ghost" comes AFTER an audience; before that, volume. While you're bad nobody's watching anyway, so you'll still seem to appear from nowhere. [▶ 54:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=3294s)
- **His struggles** · Physical pain, wanting to be a better husband, unsure he'll be a good father, legal noise, hard conversations with staff, working on being more upbeat. One blood family member. Thinks little is solved by introspection. Takes it one day at a time. [▶ 56:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uj5XKwW0Vbs&t=3378s)

lessons.t: Situation → what he would tell you (44 cases)
lessons.md:
Paraphrased from his videos, each with its source. Applied to Caregiver Bench where it fits.


| # | Situation | What he'd tell you (paraphrase) | Sources |
| 1 | I'm not making my calls / procrastinating | Many productivity systems are guilt-free procrastination. Do only the task you set out to do. Real work starts when motivation runs out. Today: dial, nothing else, until the block ends. | [▶ 46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDK4g5na4Jw) [▶ 75](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XwzU4RikbGs) [▶ 168](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bkPwFqa89gE) [▶ 249](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=evNrefJmM_I) |
| 2 | I don't feel motivated | You don't need passion to start; waiting for it is procrastination. Pain and disgust with your situation are valid fuel. | [▶ 215](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDDFezF7OTA) [▶ 231](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3e73Qn6NOo) |
| 3 | First call fear | Rejection tolerance is a learnable skill. A no costs you nothing; it is the price of a yes. Survive the first three months of high-volume calling and you are fine. | [▶ 15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDBkiBnMrHs) [▶ 98](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CaiLcj6tzBQ) [▶ 231](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3e73Qn6NOo) |
| 4 | I keep changing the offer | That is the shiny object. Switching restarts you at uninformed optimism. Stay in the pain long enough to learn the variables. Full conviction in a sensible plan beats hunting the perfect one. | [▶ 74](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-UzJOk85OZI) [▶ 109](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QTZsh3BgOwY) [▶ 230](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kl-I7sUcAOY) [▶ 243](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gEF67-G9MO0) |
| 5 | I want to rework the script / site / deck before calling | Most people already know what to do and hide behind planning. Your first 100 cold calls teach more than 100 videos. | [▶ 7](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aFoMYz_jWcs) [▶ 18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6KqndZuN_Yk) |
| 6 | Owner says "send me info" | Treat "just wanted info" as an obstacle and clear it before you ask. Decisions need information, not time, and you are the source. Always book the next meeting before the call ends. | [▶ 33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NcD2t9qt-fM) [▶ 153](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cy2k1GdA-9o) |
| 7 | Owner says "I need to think about it" | That is avoidance, the core objection. Ask what the main concern is. Confirm the three real yeses: it works, they trust you, they can fund it. | [▶ 33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NcD2t9qt-fM) [▶ 37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RVbvhPGFi6E) [▶ 178](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q32-l3Yoqg4) |
| 8 | Price objection on the monthly plan | "Can't afford it" means they don't see the value. Rebuild the value: bigger result, more certain, faster, less effort. Never discount to close. | [▶ 58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oi7bnS8uyJM) [▶ 81](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yEKu6q0W3gs) [▶ 102](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HsQeQM1jUeg) |
| 9 | "I have to ask my partner" | Ask what happens if the partner says no; about 1 in 3 just go ahead. Ask what the partner's concern would be, then handle that. Ask for support, not permission. | [▶ 33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NcD2t9qt-fM) [▶ 39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=StVqS0jD7Ls) [▶ 58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oi7bnS8uyJM) |
| 10 | "We already have a recruiter / we do it in-house" | Every position has a sellable edge. Small vs big: with the big firm you get a junior rep; with you, the founder's phone. Ask: if ours were the same as theirs, which would you pick, and why? | [▶ 39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=StVqS0jD7Ls) [▶ 65](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=prj1bnTAM8A) |
| 11 | No-shows on demo / follow-up calls | Ask a small preference question before the call. Remind at 24 hours, the morning of, and 1 hour before, in a personal way. Pull later bookings into today; same-day shows better. | [▶ 35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JE2_7elAcxM) [▶ 39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=StVqS0jD7Ls) |
| 12 | Show rate is low and I blame lead quality | Benchmark is about 70% for appointment businesses. Fixing just that one number can beat everything else combined. Check targeting and list quality first. | [▶ 17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HxEQCHpZzHk) [▶ 54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TFxT3G5jwtU) [▶ 182](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c_6BrF7jOGk) |
| 13 | My list is bad / not enough pickups | Cold outreach has three problems: contacts, what to say, too few replies. Hand-built lists are freshest. Track leading numbers: list quality, pickup rate, hook, offer, show rate. | [▶ 17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HxEQCHpZzHk) [▶ 98](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CaiLcj6tzBQ) [▶ 107](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=okA9Yt2KZuk) |
| 14 | What does a good call day look like | His BDRs did about 100 dials a day, ~20 pickups, ~2 shown appointments, in 4-hour shifts, because nobody cold calls well for 8. | [▶ 107](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=okA9Yt2KZuk) |
| 15 | How many calls do I need | Work backwards from the goal: revenue -> clients -> appointments -> outreaches per day. Example in the KB: ~200 outreaches a day for ~$1M at a $2K/mo service. | [▶ 34](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AN2KpRBsmRY) [▶ 121](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WeH2E1fGgaw) |
| 16 | First 5 customers | Make the first offer free in exchange for three things: they use it, give feedback, and leave a review if it's earned. Cap it at about five case studies. The 30-Day Bench Trial fits this. | [▶ 28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w7g08dVTwaE) [▶ 36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=reisEL_D7xc) [▶ 243](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gEF67-G9MO0) |
| 17 | How to get testimonials | Free clients pay in testimonials, referrals and later paid work. Ask for them contingent on doing a great job. Proof only has to look similar enough to the prospect. | [▶ 6](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oRMG_HpOAN4) [▶ 36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=reisEL_D7xc) [▶ 102](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HsQeQM1jUeg) |
| 18 | When to raise prices | After the first 10-20 case studies, raise 20% every five sales until price times conversion starts to fall. Judge a new price on enough pitches, not the first few noes. | [▶ 6](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oRMG_HpOAN4) [▶ 36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=reisEL_D7xc) [▶ 108](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cnbHgYYHzyE) |
| 19 | My price feels too low / am I underpriced | If nobody pushes back, it's too low. Too cheap kills belief: he called ~$13K for 16 weeks small-time for clients with big contracts. Test the new price on new customers first. | [▶ 109](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QTZsh3BgOwY) [▶ 138](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I82d3jxg_Aw) |
| 20 | Scared to charge $1,500–3,000 a month | Doubling price can still win even if close rate drops (30% to 20%). Price is the biggest single lever on profit. | [▶ 25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k-3PoOT4vOM) [▶ 109](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QTZsh3BgOwY) [▶ 129](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ArQlwPvGUA) |
| 21 | Should I offer a discount to get a yes | No. Full or free, never discounted. Free work can still be paid in testimonials, feedback and referrals. | [▶ 102](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HsQeQM1jUeg) |
| 22 | Should I add a guarantee | Risk reversal sells. Unconditional guarantees are good when starting out. A service guarantee: keep working free until they get the result. A guarantee needs a clear "or else". | [▶ 96](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-7VjocC76M) [▶ 119](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s7QA1TJKlbQ) [▶ 146](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=unshZobTt6Q) |
| 23 | How do I make the $15K offer stronger | List every obstacle the owner hits, turn each into a named solution, stack it. Do what others do in half the time at double the price; rich buyers pay for speed and certainty. | [▶ 3](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KhFlD54nQrY) [▶ 65](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=prj1bnTAM8A) [▶ 144](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eq1bnI0JoXU) |
| 24 | Should I run ads | Pick one channel and master it first. A new channel can take 3-12 months to pay back. Founders learn sales personally first. lessons.t: Work = volume × leverage · 106 ideas
lessons.md:
- Redefines work as output, and output as volume (how many times you do something) multiplied by leverage (how much each repetition yields). Working "faster" means more output per unit of time, not more hours or more effort. [▶ 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RdAKXJlMIZM)
- Make activities the goal, not outcomes: "rule of 100" means 100 primary actions a day for 100 days (100 reach-outs, 100 minutes of content, or $100/day in ads). Set company goals scientifically: problem, if-then hypothesis, how to measure, did we do it and did it work. [▶ 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VBoRLJimVzc)
- Let small fires burn: almost nothing kills a business within hours except payment processing going down. Protect the first 4-6 hours of each day for the highest-leverage work, push meetings to one day or the end of the day (book backward from your finish time), and use a far-off milestone as a polite reason to decline meetings. [▶ 3](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KhFlD54nQrY)
- Treat feelings of hopelessness as ignorance, which is fixable. Pick one skill and study it with a cheap timer for four focused hours a day (pause the timer whenever you look away); about 20 hours gets you the basics. [▶ 4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YFA8AS5Cu2w)
- "Volume negates luck": assume you will get no lucky breaks and make up for it with reps (e.g. 10 tailored applications and 40 personal messages a day). Once hired, outwork the top performer by doing what they do and then more, for one to two years, not a week. [▶ 4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YFA8AS5Cu2w)
- Skill = volume of reps times improvement between reps. Review your top 10 and bottom 10 outputs (ads, calls, videos), keep doing what the winners share, drop what the losers share, and build a checklist; inexperience is not stupidity, so make mistakes fast without self-judgment. [▶ 7](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aFoMYz_jWcs)
- Definitions: learning = same situation, new behavior; intelligence = how fast you change behavior; confidence = domain-specific proof built from many reps in the actual situation (practice until bored). If a plan relies on luck, it is a bad plan. [▶ 8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MNll1BaskLA)
- Every business is capped by the founder's weakest of three: skills, character traits, or beliefs (like a ladder missing a rail). His examples: running ~10 businesses at once was a focus (trait) problem; not realizing he could teach gyms instead of running them was a belief problem; "no good salespeople exist" is a skill gap in hiring and managing reps. Turn complaints into solvable "how do I" questions. [▶ 9](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qxQIcDrre1E)
- If it is worth doing, it is worth doing well: first filter out what is not worth doing, then invest the 5-10x effort that separates great from good (he spends about a year writing a book because it can sell for decades). [▶ 16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cq8GyLrEuAk)
- A single meeting can wreck a maker's block: you cannot settle into flow when a meeting is coming, and open loops (the Zeigarnik effect) eat attention. With about 10 blocks a week, one stray meeting costs roughly 10% of weekly output; a 2pm performance review can ruin a whole day. [▶ 20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GIRkQQHzsxI)
- Buying a course only gives you permission to start solving the problem; you still have to put in the effort. To catch up to people who are better than you, do roughly twice the work of the top performer (the Kobe "two-a-days" idea). Aim to become #1 in any group you join, and earn status by giving value first, repeatedly, before you ask for anything. [▶ 22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nh8Oc7ERdIU)
- Productivity comes from what you choose not to do. Commitment means eliminating alternatives, and focus is measured by how many things you say no to, including distractions in your environment (notifications, open doors). Splitting effort across four projects is like building four short ladders; stack every rung on one ladder to get over the wall. [▶ 24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MzAIP_WJ-jE)
- Redirect the energy you spend on envy into your own effort. Nobody is doing as well as you think. Competitors tend to copy whoever ignores them and focuses on the customer. [▶ 24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MzAIP_WJ-jE)
- The hard way is the easy way: real shortcuts get adopted by everyone and stop being shortcuts. Hardship comes in several kinds (sacrifice, effort, risk, uncertainty), and each new level brings a new one. Whatever you blame has power over you, so take that power back. [▶ 24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MzAIP_WJ-jE)
- Learning from your own data: do lots of volume, isolate the top 10% of outcomes (calls, posts, resolutions), compare them with the other 90%, test the differences one at a time to find what actually matters, drop the 90%'s mistakes, and repeat in batches of about 100. [▶ 27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jfW6gL6hKhk)
- His 60-second summary: decide what you want, ignore others' opinions, and do so much volume that failing would be unreasonable. [▶ 29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ub1D6RQocRU)
- Count effort in hundreds: hundreds of hours, days or reps on one goal. The pottery-class parable, where the quantity group ended up with better pots, gives you permission to make lots of rough drafts. For self-employed people, a day only counts as work if it produced a clear output. [▶ 31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ln24y0FPJHo)
- Sales mindset: whoever cares most about the prospect wins, so turn away bad fits. Volume negates luck; do double the top rep's volume, because income lags skill and most rewards come near mastery. "Don't be cute": the great reps just never skip fundamentals. New reps should "be the trash man" and take weak leads as practice. Be kind, not nice, and avoid "commission breath." [▶ 39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=StVqS0jD7Ls)
- Minimum effective doses elsewhere: worked out about twice a week just to maintain; fasted one or two days a week (caffeine and bone broth) to avoid food prep interruptions; deleted social apps from his phone and posted from a computer at scheduled times, which reclaims the 3-5 hours a day many people lose to scrolling. [▶ 41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lRyGIzW9d9k)
- Doing more of what already works is the highest risk-adjusted move available: finding something that works took many failed attempts, so swapping it for a new untested idea is statistically unlikely to beat simply pouring more volume into the proven machine. [▶ 42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0lMn_-EXyhQ)
- Example of sheer volume: ACQ's president grew a company from $200M to $1.2B in about 30 months, partly by speaking at 260 events in a single year. [▶ 42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0lMn_-EXyhQ)
- The 12x30 challenge: work 12 hours a day for 30 days straight with no weekends. It shows you that you aren't fragile, how much more you can do, and that you have that gear when you need it later. Working is itself a skill that improves with reps, including the ability to pull yourself back after a lapse in focus. [▶ 46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDK4g5na4Jw)
- Define work as volume x leverage: high volume early on builds skill, which then raises leverage. Anything that isn't a prerequisite for your one focus (sleep and food are) counts as a distraction, and "real work begins once motivation runs out." [▶ 46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDK4g5na4Jw)
- Masters have more ways to measure progress (more small wins) than beginners, who only see the final output. Building more progress markers increases expertise and makes the work itself rewarding. [▶ 46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDK4g5na4Jw)
- Results need every condition met, like valves in a pipe. Every trait has a price (privacy for fame, loneliness for ambition, pleasure for discipline); keep "bidding" higher effort until you pay what it costs, and at the top level your own standard becomes the source. The person with the highest standards should make the decision on that area, regardless of seniority. [▶ 46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDK4g5na4Jw)
- Define work as output, not hours or effort: output = volume (how many times you do something) x leverage (what you get each time), and speed = output per unit of time. Most owners overestimate how much real volume they do. [▶ 57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gD0X-PLax5I)
- Balancing ambition and marriage: nobody does effective work 24 hours a day. Know your output rate (pages edited, slides made); when it drops off, stop and spend the time on something with higher return, such as an hour with your spouse. Find the minimum effective dose for each goal. [▶ 60](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCgr7jT7JLA)
- His daily routine: decide on one highest-leverage project and give it the first six hours of every day, a habit he has kept for over a decade. [▶ 60](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCgr7jT7JLA)
- People obsessed with morning routines earn less than people obsessed with making money. A follower replaced a 3-hour routine (grounding walk, journal, ice plunge) with 3 hours of work and got far more done. Keep a routine only if it measurably raises your output. [▶ 61](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DiQ3N8F1Hl8)
- Wealth is an output and getting better is the input. Owners who chase the revenue number spread their attention thin, while improving what you deliver is what produces wealth. [▶ 63](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uki3IUkUu7Q)
- Compare inputs, not outputs. Look at a top performer's calls, practice hours, start time and weekend work, not their commission check. When you're behind, do two or three times their inputs, because simply matching them keeps you behind. [▶ 66](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pt50QF6al8g)
- Track leading metrics you control (calls made, calories eaten) rather than lagging outcomes (sales, scale weight). Define winning as giving maximum effort each day, so you can win every day. [▶ 66](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pt50QF6al8g)
- Buffett-style exercise: list your top 25 goals in order, circle the top 5 and drop the rest. Put full effort into the single most important goal and define the minimum upkeep for the other four so they don't slip, much like a bodybuilder working one weak point at a time. [▶ 69](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ueJg14gQLuc)
- The hard part isn't effort, it's not knowing what to do next. People quit at the first unfamiliar obstacle and change strategy, when working out the unknown is the strategy. Endure about 100 days of being bad at something, or stick with it a year, and you'll beat most people. [▶ 74](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-UzJOk85OZI)
- Being busy and broke usually comes from working on too many things, not from too little effort. He worked every waking hour and stayed stuck around $3M/year until he concentrated his effort. [▶ 75](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XwzU4RikbGs)
- Volume beats talent and circumstances. Do so many reps that failing becomes unlikely (no partner? count the dates and the asks). Build confidence by applying past wins to new areas: if hard work paid off in school or the gym, it will pay off in a new job or skill. [▶ 86](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XGm2ERU9qtA)
- If you're under 30 with no responsibilities, work as many hours as you can, because you'll never have fewer obligations. Starting later with a family means trade-offs, but your experience lets you aim the effort better. Having nothing to lose means a capped downside and an open upside, which is the setup for opportunity. [▶ 86](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XGm2ERU9qtA)
- Find the input-output equation for your skill, the repeated action that produces improvement (for example, rehearsing a talk 100 times over 30 days, or a set number of sales calls a day), then pour in as much input as you can. A teammate tripled his prep from 10 to 30 hours, lost his nerves, and realized he hadn't been bad at speaking, just underprepared. [▶ 89](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4evdxF5G0s)
- Young people have to earn respect through visible effort. Hustle is respected across age, gender and culture, but people want the respect before doing the work. The future high performers in their 20s look hungry to learn, not flashy. A track record of proof makes pretending unnecessary. [▶ 90](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-wnnwCqGeNc)
- Advice to beginners: follow instructions; Google before asking; post what you figure out; do the Rule of 100 every day because inconsistent inputs produce inconsistent outputs; real work begins when excitement fades; everything is unscalable at first and the pain of repetition drives skill. [▶ 102](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HsQeQM1jUeg)
- Your standards show in how many angles you attack a problem with, not how many times you repeat one approach. For hiring reps: offer a big referral bounty to your network, acquire a company with a large SDR team, hire several recruiters, fly hires in for a 3-day in-person ramp instead of 30 days, or use senior staff with spare capacity. "I tried it and it didn't work" usually means you weren't skilled enough yet. [▶ 122](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A248pGXTSoY)
- Being consistent at things you enjoy (workouts, boxing) is not discipline; discipline is "frustration tolerance", doing unrewarding things for a long time. It is a trainable skill: e.g., 10 outreaches, then 20, 30, 50, building to the rule of 100 for 100 straight days. [▶ 130](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=spXH1kJ6q-Q)
- Self-awareness means choosing advice that fits your current resources and constraint, then attacking that constraint from every angle at once (many books, videos, a coach reviewing your work) until it stops being the bottleneck. Commitment is the elimination of alternatives; consistency and volume required are far larger than people expect. [▶ 130](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=spXH1kJ6q-Q)
- Fear lives in vagueness: write out, step by step, exactly what happens if you fail (e.g., moving back home); it usually turns out survivable. Commit fully to effort you control and detach from the outcome; nobody faults you for aiming big and missing (his public $100M launch goal ended at $106M). [▶ 132](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YONIUpk-kAs)
- Record outcomes require record work no one sees: the launch took about four years of prep, 400 pages of email copy, six video sales letters, and roughly 1,700 hand-built slides. Expect no applause; you have to be the one who credits your own effort. [▶ 132](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YONIUpk-kAs)
- Public stakes and external incentives drive exceptional effort; his fitness business saw record results when clients could earn their money back as service credit by hitting goals. [▶ 145](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uaLNfijnp-8)
- Boasting that "no one can outwork me" is false and beside the point: everyone has the same hours, so beyond a baseline of effort, results come from volume times leverage (e.g., Buffett reads for hours and needs only a couple of great decisions a year). [▶ 150](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PTgGfV8Tf00)
- Activity counts (emails sent, waking at 4am) are a beginner's metric; once you've maxed out your hours, the only lever left is swapping low-leverage activities for higher-leverage ones. Don't be superstitious about habits like early rising. [▶ 150](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PTgGfV8Tf00)
- The meta-skill is sustained consistency and enthusiasm; the best reps treat poor-quality leads as free practice (kill for sport) and never blame lead quality or comp plans, raising feedback privately with data instead. [▶ 153](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cy2k1GdA-9o)
- Treat entrepreneurship as skill stacking: your work shapes you more than you shape it, failures become lessons, and progress speed depends on deliberate volume; pay mentors to acquire valuable skills faster. [▶ 159](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s9fSDCRPQNA)
- Learning is defined as producing a new behavior under the same condition, and intelligence is the speed of learning; you can beat smarter people by compressing your iterations in time (he outworked Vanderbilt peers by studying 9am-9pm daily). [▶ 162](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q9qBqnhdWKw)
- Ignore the black box of psychology and motives; focus on inputs and observable outputs, and judge teachers by whether they tell you exactly what to do with your words or body (a tennis coach just fixes your grip without analyzing why it was wrong). [▶ 162](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q9qBqnhdWKw)
- Learn first by modeling what the top 1-10% do (not what they say they do, since great performers often can't explain their success), then shift to first-party data: produce high volume, compare your top 10% of outputs to the rest, find differences, and repeat in layers. [▶ 162](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q9qBqnhdWKw)
- Extreme goals require extreme, unbalanced effort: earning $1M a year puts you far beyond the top 1% (about $600k in the US), so you can't act like everyone else and expect that result; obsessing over work-life balance tends to produce mediocrity in both. [▶ 174](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqjGxVW-Ae0)
- Feedback loops speed learning: effort plus feedback in a practice setting lets you run far more reps (he did 20+ in-person sales consults a day for years) than waiting for real-world results. [▶ 179](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BQ3whjWG3M)
- Because real mastery takes so much work, you can only get great at a few things; identify the single lever that would make you win (traffic, referrals, paid ads) and pour effort there. [▶ 183](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m5ordaa7NN4)
- Treat nervousness as a signal of underpreparation, not anxiety or impostor syndrome; habituate to the stressor through reps so your bandwidth is free for surprises. [▶ 183](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m5ordaa7NN4)
- Turn forced downtime into output: a flight without Wi-Fi became a recording session that produced a viral clip. [▶ 184](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y7O-iTWwTW8)
- Work double time: do today's job and, early mornings or late nights, build for tomorrow's (he worked 4-10am on his own projects before running the business, and spent ~6 hours a day for nearly two years writing a book). [▶ 188](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5JLqmQlGG0U)
- Skills acquired young also compound because you accumulate the reps sooner (e.g. Bill Gates coding early) and keep a lasting head start. [▶ 191](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aRVv5NLVRwE)
- Young people have more energy for reps and fewer obligations (no kids or spouse, low living costs, no geographic ties), so they can reinvest aggressively and move to where the action is: DC for politics, New York for finance, LA for media. [▶ 191](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aRVv5NLVRwE)
- Price the wall: picture the payoff of solving the hard constraint (e.g. an extra $250M of enterprise value) so the multi-year effort feels worth it and you allocate resources properly. [▶ 206](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=07jC6ooRIHw)
- Every successful entrepreneur has a "Rocky montage" phase of 2-6 unglamorous years of repetitive reps that builds mastery, after which they apply the skill to a new vehicle and seem to blow up overnight (e.g. a sales leader who did hundreds of daily dials to ignored opt-in lists; a marketer who cold-called for years first). [▶ 208](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tw6kJkVcTL0)
- Define productivity as output per unit of time; adding non-work rituals (walks, red light, cold plunge, journaling until 11 a.m.) lowers it. That person would get more done by prospecting for those three hours. [▶ 214](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PFKGHL1MqkU)
- The productivity equation: volume of work times the leverage on that work. Order your day from the highest-leverage tasks to the lowest. [▶ 214](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PFKGHL1MqkU)
- If you think you need a brain warm-up, treat it as trainable: drop one ritual at a time and see whether output holds, shrinking the routine while hours of real work grow. [▶ 214](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PFKGHL1MqkU)
- His routine: wake up, have coffee, start working without checking the phone, in order of leverage. [▶ 214](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PFKGHL1MqkU)
- Purpose often emerges after you push through enough reps to get good and see compounding results; his own mission for years was simply not being poor. [▶ 215](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDDFezF7OTA)
- Do what is required, not your "best": your true best is what you'd do if lives depended on it (e.g. rewriting his book through 11 drafts so he'd know he exhausted every option). People judge the output, not your reasons. [▶ 215](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDDFezF7OTA)
- You'll suck at first; skill comes from sucking less over hundreds or thousands of reps. Periodically ask whether you've learned what this path can teach you before pivoting. [▶ 226](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5RiR6cBLkFg)
- The highest-leverage act is making good decisions: deciding a project isn't a priority frees more of your team than automating that project ever could. [▶ 227](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WttZ6b-KUP4)
- Learn skills via volume: do 100 reps, study the top 10%, carry their traits into the next 100, repeat (Chris Rock refining sets club by club). Decide the number of reps after which it would be unreasonable to still be bad, then commit. [▶ 230](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kl-I7sUcAOY)
- Build confidence with "unreasonable to fail" input-output statements: e.g. collect 5,000 no's and you'll be a good salesman; post multiple times daily on every platform and reach grows. He raised his GMAT to the 99th percentile by doing four hours of practice problems daily for three months, after reading that score tracks problems practiced. [▶ 231](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3e73Qn6NOo)
- Output = volume x leverage (reps x how much each rep yields); skill is leverage, and skill only comes from more reps, so working hard and smart reinforce each other. When stuck, the answer is usually the highest-pain task you've postponed longest. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- Work-life balance can be measured over seasons, not days (e.g. three intense years, then a calmer one; weekly not daily calorie budgets). Maintaining a skill costs about a tenth of growing it, so maintain most areas and pour effort into one at a time instead of 4/10 effort on ten things. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- Consuming information isn't learning; ~99% of what he learned came from doing. People wildly underestimate the volume needed (400 podcast episodes before reaching the top 10; now 100+ content pieces a week). Expecting to be good on the first try is asking the universe to be unreasonable. [▶ 233](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRPChBZ0Rjo)
- Name the price of what you want and pay it (he gave up fantasy leagues, football, nights out). North Star filter: does having X in my life raise the odds I hit my goal? He prepped for the GMAT four hours a day for four months because practice volume correlated with scores. [▶ 236](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gT2bk52F9bg)
- Output = volume x leverage. Do 100 reps (reels, calls, dates), run a common-factors analysis on the top performers, repeat what they share, and keep doing this for years. [▶ 236](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gT2bk52F9bg)
- Eliminate distractions by eliminating them: no outside light, earplugs plus headphones, a full phone block that he has to walk across the building to undo, a kitchen timer per task. Productivity is output per unit of time, and short breaks count as productive if they raise total output. [▶ 240](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q-_hwD1jNK4)
- People wildly underestimate volume: a mentor tested flyers 5,000 per batch and ran 5,000 a day, versus Alex's 300. His team produces about 450 content pieces a week, and a top closer may have 4,000 closes. Much of the early delay is the time it takes to accept there's no easy way. [▶ 240](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q-_hwD1jNK4)
- The biggest problem is overthinking as a stand-in for action, rooted in fear of others seeing you fail. Beginners should act far more than think; that ratio flips as leverage grows (Buffett makes few moves). Output = volume x leverage; skill creates leverage, and skill comes from volume, so you work hard before you can work smart. [▶ 241](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZKhApFCWO8)
- Optimizers seek the most output for the least input; maximizers know diminishing returns are still returns (Olympic gold vs silver is a tenth of a second but worlds apart in reward). He was rewarded for out-working people and got hooked on that cycle. [▶ 245](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9urSNqHrCFM)
- Real effort requires focus: doing something truly well takes far more work than people think, so cut most things. Most things are not hard if you really try; most people lack the skill of trying hard. Example: about 90% of podcasters quit after one episode and most of the rest before 20, so 20 uploads puts you in the top 1%. [▶ 247](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WK-d4H7xtvQ)
- Reframe hard things by asking in what context they'd be normal (e.g., teachers present all day, every day). Stamina for long mental work (12-16 hour consulting or writing days) is a skill built through volume plus a feedback loop, until your stress response gets used to it. [▶ 251](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f_UL-z1xgI)
- To learn a skill fast, use volume times feedback loops. Ranked by speed: an expert tutor, then a small group, then joining a community of people who already have the skill, which lets you separate the few core truths from the mysticism. Watching top performers beats asking them, since many don't know what they do. [▶ 251](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f_UL-z1xgI)
- Reduce any goal to an input-output equation (calls, emails, DMs, posts, ad spend per day) and grind it out, since action relieves anxiety. Sadness is not knowing your options and is cured by knowledge; anxiety is too many options without priorities and is cured by deciding. [▶ 252](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KepgJld9O2w)
- Think of dating like a sales pipeline in reverse: you need volume (he suggests something like 100 dates rather than 10) and you only need one match, so very high standards are fine as long as the standards you hold yourself to are even higher. [▶ 23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jiCGLDhUCHY)
- How much you need date nights depends on how much you work. Since they eat out almost nightly (often for business), a "date" is set apart by the effort (dressing up, going incognito) or by watching a movie together at home that both actually want to see. [▶ 60](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCgr7jT7JLA)
- He trains his whole body every day, working body parts from weakest to strongest (calves first, as they have been for over 10 years), and supersets so cardio isn't needed. Doubling the volume on a weak area and training it every session is what finally made it grow. Starting with an easy, low-effort exercise makes it hard to skip the workout. [▶ 84](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ABOd589OyTM)
- Effort earns respect in every culture, but most people don't know what hard work looks like (a law partner once told him he didn't even know how to work). The bar is low, so learning how to try is the real edge. Count your hours too: beyond a standard work year there are weekends, holidays and evenings available for reps. Expect lots of junk volume early, since earlier drafts set up later ones. [▶ 89](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4evdxF5G0s)
- Identity works like a running tally of votes cast by your actions; the root idea is repeated "being." Affirmations without evidence don't convince a sane mind, so build the evidence by doing. Once behaviors become part of who you are, they take little effort. [▶ 99](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YaNX49ygr0I)
- Plot where you are and where you want to be on a 2x2 of body fat versus muscle. The direction tells you whether to raise or lower calories and whether to raise or lower training volume. [▶ 100](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RpqSy5V1fFQ)
- Pain fades while achievements stay; complaining just asks for pity and spends effort for nothing. [▶ 102](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HsQeQM1jUeg)
- Bezos's final shareholder letter, citing Richard Dawkins: living things must expend energy to stay distinct from their surroundings, and in death they reach equilibrium with them. The world constantly pulls you toward typical; being distinctive is worth it but requires continuous effort and is never free. [▶ 122](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A248pGXTSoY)
- Rank your 10 areas, then check where your effort doesn't match the rank; he concluded he should spend more time with his wife and friends, trading some career hours for a higher overall life return. [▶ 143](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OHu1FY1R-x0)
- Caring about anything can be framed as cringe (bodybuilding, chess, YouTube, writing a book); the only truly cringe stance is being afraid to look cringe, and people who mock effort usually have never committed to anything. [▶ 155](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yb2cLMMuMdQ)
- Join a "championship team": being around people with higher standards (as in the book Grit's swimming example) recalibrates what normal effort looks like. [▶ 183](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m5ordaa7NN4)
- You impress less successful people by outspending them and successful people by outworking them; flashy spending beyond your means reads as insecure. [▶ 183](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m5ordaa7NN4)
- Train with a partner (more sets, reps and accountability) and ideally with someone stronger, which breaks limiting beliefs about what weight is possible, similar to business. [▶ 184](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y7O-iTWwTW8)
- Munger's warning about the three things that ruin most people: liquor, leverage (excessive debt) and ladies (philandering); he and Buffett never took on debt beyond what they could easily cover. [▶ 187](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-NLqtk4F4oY)
- After the gym sale year (~$40M in distributions before the exit) left him idle and miserable, he found his best days were workout plus producing something with people he liked; his thesis became hard work as the goal itself. He works until output drops, takes a day off when empty, and treats responsibility as absolute: whoever you blame holds power over your life. [▶ 230](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kl-I7sUcAOY)
- Highest-leverage single behaviors for 20-35 year olds: go to bed on time (set an alarm for bedtime, not wake-up), which avoids DUIs, hangovers at work and more; eat your body weight in grams of protein; optimize the 3-5 meals you eat 90% of the time. He's against getting a dog for ambitious people because of time and freedom costs. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- He tells young men to work 6 days a week, 12 hours a day if they want big goals on short timelines; be clear on trade-offs (he traded his 20s). Most could hit their goals by extending the timeline. Spectators watch only a marathon's start and finish; the "mundane middle" is the work. Key trait: resilience, defined as how fast you return to baseline after a setback. [▶ 235](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rRI0J8a4I9g)
- Fitness basics: six-pack is just body fat percentage (calorie deficit); muscle is progressive overload, hitting each group three times a week, plus protein, sustained over ~18 months. Once built, maintenance takes little effort. Everyone has the same 24 "dollars" a day; decide if the price is worth it, or accept you do not want it. [▶ 244](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sdd4BST87ks)
- Being jacked is functional because it pays off in the situations you are most exposed to (e.g., being on camera), so put effort where your exposure is highest. [▶ 245](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9urSNqHrCFM)
- Marriage: manage closeness by deliberately creating space to be missed, and make "I need alone time" carry no negative meaning. Choosing a spouse is like taking on behaviors you want; Leila made him more patient and kind, and he made her more direct. Parting advice: figure out what you want, ignore others' opinions, and do so much volume that failure becomes unreasonable. [▶ 251](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f_UL-z1xgI)

lessons.t: Discipline, patience & the boring middle · 116 ideas
lessons.md:
- Shiny opportunities get more tempting as you grow, so the discipline to say no must be re-learned at each income level. Patience is a behavior (not acting on distraction), not a feeling. [▶ 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RdAKXJlMIZM)
- Patience simply means having something else to do in the meantime. Traits are continuums, not binaries, so you can move along them by repeated actions. [▶ 8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MNll1BaskLA)
- Start when you are busiest so the habit survives busy seasons; audit your phone screen time to find hours; you cannot be smart, busy and broke at once, so if you are working hard without progress, cut the wrong activities first. Measure yourself on whether you did the committed actions, accept that this is what hard feels like, and aim to outlast rather than "win." [▶ 8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MNll1BaskLA)
- Apparent speed comes from fewer wrong strategic decisions, not frantic activity: "micro slow, macro fast" beats constant direction changes. Most success is doing the obvious thing consistently for an unusually long time. [▶ 9](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qxQIcDrre1E)
- Skills stack and compound: math to bookkeeping to accounting to tax, insurance, deal structure and capital markets turns a bookkeeper into a rainmaker. His stack (fitness, nutrition, sales, local marketing, operations, sales teams, national B2B marketing) took Gym Launch from zero to $28M/year in 20 months; he had logged about 4,000 one-on-one sales in 3.5 years first. [▶ 9](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qxQIcDrre1E)
- Skills stack exponentially (video, then editing, social media, messaging, copywriting, branding, management and leadership turns a videographer into a CMO and then a founder); invest in yourself because that compounds far faster than market returns. [▶ 10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dZ7xeVCYC5M)
- People quit when work gets boring, not just hard. He has recorded ads every week for 14 years and made around 5,000 ads in one year, reusing proven hooks and body copy. [▶ 15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDBkiBnMrHs)
- Things always take longer, cost more and are harder than expected; reframe complaints as wrong expectations about the price. Drop limiting "I'm not a math person" labels; he trained mental math for years by refusing a calculator. Identity is defined by what you do. [▶ 18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6KqndZuN_Yk)
- Action habits: start today rather than tomorrow; read one book and apply it instead of collecting 52; do not wait for perfect conditions (start in bad conditions so success survives the next downturn); talk less and do more instead of performing elaborate prep routines. [▶ 19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ySuYdJ0H4s)
- Ramsey's advice to his younger self: play incremental long ball, not home runs; run many survivable experiments, never bet the farm on one horse, and accept that it never becomes easy. Ramsey's failures outnumber its successes, but debt-free survival let the iterations compound. [▶ 21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jvXOOddDg_s)
- Consistency beats talent: you can get competent at most skills in about 20 hours and beat most people at almost anything by sticking with it for a year. Overcome self-doubt through repetition and habituation (he got comfortable on stage after years of coaching fitness classes on a microphone), not affirmations. [▶ 24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MzAIP_WJ-jE)
- Separate maker time from manager time. A maker's ideal day is an empty calendar; a manager's is many short touchpoints. Keeping the first 4-6 hours of the day for maker work is his most impactful habit. Avoid task switching, and batch manager work into one day (his is Monday). [▶ 27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jfW6gL6hKhk)
- Obsession is the price of entry, and from inside it looks like simply trying when others don't. Most hate amounts to someone preferring you lived differently. "Work smart, not hard" only wins against people who aren't smart, so work hard and smart, compressing 40 years of work into 4 if you can. [▶ 29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ub1D6RQocRU)
- Accept boredom and sacrifice. Crowds gather at the start and finish lines, but the race is won alone in the unglamorous middle, and consistency only looks impressive at the end. Whatever you spend hours on instead of your goal is what you've actually prioritized. You either live up your 20s and end up under-skilled, or work them and end up under-lived. [▶ 29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ub1D6RQocRU)
- Weekends are 104 days a year. If you lose ground on them (no lead follow-up, partying), you may net only about three productive days a week, while someone who keeps going is moving several times faster. Aim for work you don't need a weekend from, and think of balance over seasons of years. [▶ 31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ln24y0FPJHo)
- When all you have is time, it comes down to brute force: live a normal day (job, chores) and then start a second workday. Think of it as pulling future pain into today so the later years get easier. Moving somewhere he knew nobody freed up his weekends for learning to market and sell. [▶ 32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oys_fv25SYM)
- Poor habits flip delayed gratification into delayed pain ("I'll start Monday"). Today is yesterday's tomorrow, so the current pain is the bill coming due. Master basics like showing up on time before chasing advanced tactics; understanding a concept is not the same as being able to do it. [▶ 32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oys_fv25SYM)
- Focus on actions, not feelings. Patience is knowing what to do in the meantime; courage is acting as if you weren't afraid. Vividly picture the pain of staying the same so it outweighs the comfort, because change happens when that pain exceeds the pain of changing. [▶ 32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oys_fv25SYM)
- Don't interrupt compounding. Focus is measured by what you say no to; shiny new opportunities ("the woman in the red dress") restart you through uninformed optimism, informed pessimism and the valley of despair. Compare year 5 of your current thing with year 2 of the new one. Diversify only after you're rich (Gates versus Ballmer). Learn through a common-factors analysis of your top and bottom 10% (content, ads, customers, calls). [▶ 34](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AN2KpRBsmRY)
- Champions usually don't have a secret habit you lack; they lack things you have (like an "off switch"). So the most productive "routine" is an anti-routine: stop doing things until only the work remains. He credits this with going from nearly bankrupt to taking home over $1M/month within about 18 months, at 27. [▶ 41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lRyGIzW9d9k)
- Three foundations for getting out of being broke: (1) accept that it's your fault, because whatever you blame holds power over you (a parent, politics, your past); (2) use what you have, even anger or shame, since passion isn't required to start; (3) live below your means and pour the surplus into skills and experiments. Failed bets count as "experience points," not a return to zero, and the first $100K took him five years. [▶ 56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vhOV_Od0A3M)
- His maker habits: pick one key project; work 4am-9am; notifications off, windowless room, earplugs; treat nothing as an emergency except a 911 call; keep a fixed bedtime (an alarm for going to bed, not waking); treat weekends like weekdays (104 extra days a year); and remember drinking costs two days. [▶ 57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gD0X-PLax5I)
- Copy what successful people did on the way up, not their habits at the top (Buffett isn't rich because he drinks Coke). Check correlations by asking how many people share the trait without the result, e.g. many people with hard childhoods never succeed. [▶ 61](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DiQ3N8F1Hl8)
- Tolerance wipes out the benefit of a habit over time (e.g., coffee ends up only bringing you back to normal). If you want the boost, rotate inputs so they stay novel rather than becoming dependent on them. [▶ 64](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ErWpi_91b70)
- Health, marriage and business are infinite games: the aim is to keep playing, so you win by not quitting. Take quitting off the menu and just try the next idea. The montage that lasts seconds on screen may take years in real life. [▶ 66](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pt50QF6al8g)
- A "season of no" is a set stretch (from 3 months to 3 years) where you turn down almost everything except your main goal. His longest lasted 3 years: no alcohol, no social events, and he skipped a mastermind he paid about $35k a year for. Gym Launch was built during it. [▶ 69](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ueJg14gQLuc)
- Top business owners are paid so much because they made it through the brutal early years. Growth is the painful gap between where you are and where you need to be, so wishing for fast growth means wishing for a lot of pain. [▶ 71](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WOZGZK7K-Jo)
- Most people already roughly know what to do (e.g., to get fit: eat better, move more, lift and add progressive load). The gap is execution. Commit to one plan for about three years and you'll beat most people. [▶ 74](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-UzJOk85OZI)
- Patience means having something to do in the meantime. Park ideas in a big "ridiculous ideas" list (his has 200+ items across AI, traffic, conversion, LTV, ascension and renewal) and pull very few; he took 3 in 18 months. Buffett-style punch card: allow yourself one major optimization bet per year. [▶ 75](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XwzU4RikbGs)
- Training with a partner makes him push harder, rest less (the partner's set becomes the rest timer, roughly 2 parts rest to 1 part work), do more sets, and keep better form. Many "disciplined" people have simply found a hard activity they enjoy. About 90 minutes of pickleball burns roughly 1,000 calories without feeling like cardio. [▶ 84](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ABOd589OyTM)
- The one belief you need is that you can figure it out. Entrepreneurs who stay on an unusual path longer than seems reasonable, turn down imagined opportunities, and make trades others won't are the few who earn outsized returns. Study people who consistently get what they want, to copy how they weigh decisions. [▶ 86](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XGm2ERU9qtA)
- Resilience is how long it takes to return to baseline, measured in time (five minutes vs five years). You can drop hard and still recover fast. He calls this the most trainable part and the one to work on first. [▶ 88](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SE9_1PYsaP0)
- He reviewed three to four years of good and bad days, found what the good days had in common, and maximized those things. For him that meant long workouts (about two hours with people he likes) and four to six hours of writing. The formula is doing things you like with people you like, and minimizing or outsourcing the rest. [▶ 89](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4evdxF5G0s)
- His "Solomon" method: in a dated Google Doc, write a back-and-forth conversation with your wiser future self, who has all the context and the same incentives as you. People give better advice than they follow, so this gets around that. The usual advice is to be patient, keep doing what works, and wait for enough data. [▶ 89](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4evdxF5G0s)
- Every goal has three layers: the outcome (money, a six-pack), the behaviors that produce it, and the identity of someone who naturally does those behaviors (be, then do, then have). Change the identity and the habits follow. [▶ 99](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YaNX49ygr0I)
