- Keystone habit: at every decision point, ask "what would [the person I want to become] do?" Examples include a wise man, a billionaire, someone 10x smarter, the best husband, or role models such as King Solomon, Buffett or Munger. One repeated question is easier to apply than a 50-item checklist, and it covers situations you didn't plan for (as "What would Jesus do?" does). [▶ 99](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YaNX49ygr0I)
- Extraordinary results come from doing the obvious thing consistently for an unusually long time. People who act from identity keep going indefinitely, while people chasing an external outcome ease off once they hit it. As you level up you'll keep finding new people to compare yourself to, so measure yourself by your activities instead. [▶ 99](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YaNX49ygr0I)
- If you copy what others did and fail, assume you missed a variable rather than that it doesn't work. Write down all your reasons (including what you're running from) and keep them visible; business is simple but hard because of consistency; the ability to work long without reward beats the need for instant reward. [▶ 102](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HsQeQM1jUeg)
- Long time horizons justify moves that look irrational on a one-year view. What sustained him through two years of hard writing and editing was imagining a struggling teenager relying on the book to change his situation, and seeing passed-on skills as the only lasting legacy. [▶ 111](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qel9bf653Es)
- Discipline: design the environment so the right choice is the easiest; willpower fades through the day. Delete distracting apps, block sites, work in airplane mode, use a visible timer on tasks (he says it can triple his pace), or work alongside a "work buddy." Make life boring during work seasons so the work becomes interesting. Moderate caffeine is fine if sleep isn't affected; sleep, exercise and diet are the 80/20. [▶ 121](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WeH2E1fGgaw)
- Live without regret by believing you had to go through past experiences to know what you know now; staying in "decision purgatory" trades years of life for nothing. [▶ 139](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MZPVPCIeUpg)
- 1) Meals first: the average American spends about 13.5 hours a week on groceries, planning, cooking, cleaning and portioning. Two prepared meals a day plus a morning shake costs about $750/month (offset by no grocery spending) and can help you get leaner; eating out works too (he ate Chipotle twice a day for years). [▶ 147](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3SVksBB3_YY)
- Stick with one vehicle: switching to new opportunities every few years forfeits the compounding of years five and beyond, so a mediocre opportunity pursued for a long time beats a string of new ones. [▶ 154](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fD-sxKiB30M)
- To get what you want you have to deserve it, which means becoming good, and the only path there is being willing to be bad for a long time: start, take feedback, improve, never stop. [▶ 155](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yb2cLMMuMdQ)
- Go slow to go fast: sticking with one thing unlocks compounding, while frequent changes reset you to zero and always carry a guaranteed cost with an uncertain payoff. [▶ 157](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ULGT0Qpglek)
- For about eight years he woke around 4am, giving roughly six uninterrupted hours before anyone needed him at 10am, and started working immediately after coffee. [▶ 168](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bkPwFqa89gE)
- If you're on a productive streak building new habits, don't break it for eggnog and political arguments; the main reason people go is fear of what others will say. [▶ 176](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OvEfWrDOfNk)
- Simple scales, fancy fails: repeat successful actions and do the boring work others skip. [▶ 189](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3P1XjUvo1b4)
- Habits: get 20-30 minutes of morning sunlight and about an hour total daily (walk after lunch and dinner), no workouts within 2 hours of bed, screens off 2 hours before, use a bedtime alarm instead of a wake-up alarm (aim for 9-11pm), keep naps under 30 minutes and before 2pm, keep the bedroom only for sleep and sex, and wind down after dinner instead of working until bed. [▶ 192](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=55H71isO_Bo)
- Refusing help is usually ego, especially among people who identify as smart; humility to say "I don't know, please help" speeds learning, and being willing to look dumb for a long time is an underrated money-making habit. [▶ 193](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IYuiV4YuGB4)
- At 19, a year feels huge, but good things take years; treat your late teens and twenties as a season of learning, not earning, and work below your worth to raise it. He told a 16-year-old neighbor he could be a millionaire by 30 if he committed to 10 hard years. [▶ 198](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6ySRKgXBcO0)
- If you're 18 months into a business and not making money, the blunt reason is usually that you aren't skilled yet; expecting top-1% income against people with 20 years in the game is unrealistic. [▶ 208](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tw6kJkVcTL0)
- Playing an infinite game (he'd keep making videos with no money) gives him the most underrated lever, time: a decade of experience by his mid-20s with decades left to compound. [▶ 210](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VPre_XMgKjs)
- Rituals like making your bed only matter because of the meaning attached (keeping commitments); the discipline is the point, so the ritual is replaceable or unnecessary. [▶ 214](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PFKGHL1MqkU)
- Identity is fluid and should change with what the business needs: become patient (fast on the micro, patient on the macro), act with integrity even at short-term cost, and build the focus to say no; strategy is choosing what not to pursue even when it looks good on paper. [▶ 217](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4vLgOX1Ykjg)
- He defines patience operationally as deciding what you'll do in the meantime, not just waiting. [▶ 223](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5cOwh-8scu8)
- Weigh decisions by reversibility and long-term impact: lunch choices don't matter, but committing four years and $50-200K plus lost earnings is a big, hard-to-reverse bet that deserves real analysis. [▶ 226](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5RiR6cBLkFg)
- For big decisions, keep thinking until you can reduce it to one sentence, e.g. given the cost, which path gives me the most potential four years from now? [▶ 226](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5RiR6cBLkFg)
- What beginners need is less a tactic than the courage to be wrong and to fail publicly in front of people whose opinion matters. He left a consulting career (and a path to top business school, banking, PE) because he didn't want the lives of people 20 years ahead; he had to accept his father might never speak to him again. [▶ 230](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kl-I7sUcAOY)
- Delay discounting runs both ways: we postpone the pain of quitting "until tomorrow" for 20 years and massively underweight a lifetime of misery. Embarrassments become funny eventually, so pull that time horizon forward. [▶ 230](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kl-I7sUcAOY)
- Entrepreneur cycle: uninformed optimism, informed pessimism, valley of despair, then either restart with a new shiny idea (the "woman in the red dress") and repeat the same 6 months for 20 years, or persist into informed optimism and success. His CFO's line: other businesses' grass is fertilized with manure too. [▶ 230](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kl-I7sUcAOY)
- Desirable traits (patience, toughness) each carry a price paid in time spent in hard periods; reframe hardship as the purchase price. Pain motivates faster and harder than passion; use anger and sadness or they use you. Aim to be directionally correct, not right first try. [▶ 231](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3e73Qn6NOo)
- Bad things don't come in threes; they cascade only when one bad event changes your behavior. After a setback, ask what action lowers the odds of the next bad thing. The more space between how you feel and what you do, the more consistent your results; giving in to "not feeling it" breeds superstition. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- Most people never get feedback fast enough on big goals, since winner-behavior precedes winning by years. Making yourself the goal lets you stretch the horizon indefinitely; results come slower than expected, then faster than imagined, and people misapply intensity to too short a timeline. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- Consistency, not intensity, is what's hard; the required intensity is lower than people expect. Make decisions with incomplete data and be directionally correct, since starting produces the information to improve the decision (each step lights the next). With nothing to lose, you can take unlimited shots. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- After five years of owning six gyms but being asset-rich and cash-poor, then losing everything, he realized he hadn't lost the years: skills, experiences and character traits are the real assets you keep. [▶ 233](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRPChBZ0Rjo)
- His early drive was beating his father's standards (income targets that kept rising) until he realized he was playing someone else's game; the habits remained, fueled by something else. [▶ 233](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRPChBZ0Rjo)
- Three shared traits of ultra-successful people he cites from research: a superiority complex (believing they deserve and can achieve more), crippling insecurity (never enough), and impulse control (focus on one thing for a long time). These are matters of degree, not yes/no. [▶ 233](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRPChBZ0Rjo)
- Control the environment to control behavior (Skinner's horse): "starve" bad habits by changing surroundings. Vietnam veterans mostly dropped heroin once home, while ~90% of US rehab patients relapse on returning to the same setting; even moving across town adds friction to bad habits. [▶ 234](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tigt75AcLLA)
- Confidence without evidence is delusion; confidence is your predicted likelihood you'll do what you say. Mine your past for proof (he told a woman who hadn't trained in seven years that she was already very consistent) and count losses that didn't happen. [▶ 234](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tigt75AcLLA)
- Definitions: patience = knowing what to do in the meantime; sadness = perceived lack of options, solved by knowledge; anxiety = many options without priorities, solved by deciding; learning = same condition, new behavior; intelligence = rate of learning. [▶ 234](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tigt75AcLLA)
- He doesn't think analyzing feelings or past trauma helps much; stimulus and response is what matters. People keep doing what was rewarded before, so pair new behaviors with small immediate rewards (he buys a shake after each gym session). Experts aren't more disciplined; they've found more ways to win while working. [▶ 234](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tigt75AcLLA)
- Traits like "charismatic" or "patient" are bundles of small behaviors (nodding, repeating back, smiling, vocal variety, firm handshake, eye contact); do the behaviors and others will label you with the trait. He rejects "be-do-have": doing creates both the having and the being, so focus only on doing. [▶ 236](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gT2bk52F9bg)
- Skill and income compound late: the gains from six months to three years look small, but almost all income comes at the top. An expert has made the most mistakes in a narrow field. [▶ 236](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gT2bk52F9bg)
- Shrink the time between decision and action. Ask "will I get more information to make this decision?"; if not, decide now. Fast sequential decisions compound into operating many times faster than others. [▶ 240](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q-_hwD1jNK4)
- Stress frames: "veteran frame" (imagine it happening the 1,000th time; you'd be used to it, so feel that now), reset expectations (a cat that lived 18 months seems long if cats lived six), and zoom out until Earth disappears. Add life to years, not just years to life. [▶ 241](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZKhApFCWO8)
- Criticism is a fixed cost whether you act or not. It takes about 20 hours to get proficient at most things, but people take years to log those hours; he favors full shutdown days (he built his first web page in a locked-in weekend, done by noon). Take feedback from people closest to your goals, not closest to you. [▶ 243](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gEF67-G9MO0)
- His definition of discipline: how many times in a row you can do a punishing behavior (or forgo a reward) without being rewarded. Trainers who love the gym at 5am are not showing discipline, because they enjoy it. [▶ 245](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9urSNqHrCFM)
- Common traits of the ultra-successful: an inflated sense of self, a feeling of never being good enough, and impulse control. He told his YouTube lead to judge results in five years. [▶ 246](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTAXjVgK-1o)
- Five stages: uninformed optimism, informed pessimism, valley of despair, informed optimism, success. Most loop from stage 3 back to a new stage 1. The work shapes you more than you shape it: when he lost everything five years in, he kept every skill and reapplied them. [▶ 247](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WK-d4H7xtvQ)
- His imagined 85-year-old self pushes patience, focus, sticking to commitments, and controlling inputs while staying detached from outcomes. Judge yourself by whether you truly gave everything, not by wins you may not have deserved; that internal standard keeps his inner state separate from external events. [▶ 247](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WK-d4H7xtvQ)
- Successful people's habits vary wildly, so copying rules is a trap. Model the rise, not the plateau: post-exit health routines are not what built the wealth, and the rise usually involved imbalance. Every choice is a trade with a price; pay it or do not, without labeling it good or bad. [▶ 248](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPV7Sn-POlM)
- "Solomon time": the Solomon paradox says we advise others better than ourselves, so every Monday his first meeting is a written chat with his imagined 85-year-old self, who has full context, aligned incentives and a long time horizon. Typical prompts: what problem are we solving, and are you sure it is a problem? [▶ 248](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPV7Sn-POlM)
- After losing $15M on a deal in a day (his worst day in five years), the reframe that freed him was that his future self knew everything he did and approved, and that approval was enough. He hunts for the one frame shift that ends a mental loop. [▶ 248](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPV7Sn-POlM)
- Judge yourself on actions, not feelings or outcomes: you can feel impatient yet act patiently, and become known as patient. He would rather someone think unkind thoughts but act kindly than the reverse. [▶ 248](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPV7Sn-POlM)
- His drive started from insecurity and a need for approval, then became conditioned habit through positive feedback. He shares uncomfortable numbers publicly because the things he fears saying are usually the ones he should say. [▶ 250](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4KfuQwB5rIs)
- He thinks in entrepreneurial "seasons" of about five years: roughly three to see a thing through and two to transition out of it. [▶ 250](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4KfuQwB5rIs)
- Make the path itself the goal: if you judge success by how closely each day matches the process you want to follow, you win daily instead of once every few years when a destination is reached. [▶ 251](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f_UL-z1xgI)
- For negative thoughts, flip through a set of reframes: why am I judging this? Is there a version where it's good? Would it still feel bad the thousandth time (habituation)? Cosmic irrelevance. Anxiety comes from many options and unclear priorities, and commitment (cutting alternatives) reduces it. [▶ 251](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f_UL-z1xgI)
- His highest-ROI habit is spending the first six hours of every day on the work that moves the business forward, with no calls or meetings. His team books meetings from the end of the day backward (e.g., last at 4:30, then 4:00, 3:30), so he is free until mid-afternoon. [▶ 252](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KepgJld9O2w)
- Compounding rewards boring persistence; patience means having productive things to do while you wait. Price out your actual dream lifestyle (it is often far less than imagined) and treat business as an infinite game whose point is to keep playing. [▶ 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VBoRLJimVzc)
- Get in shape and protect your energy: set an alarm to go to bed, avoid stupidity rather than chase brilliance, and consider dropping alcohol during intense growth seasons (he quit for two years while scaling to $4.4M/month). Fitness costs time, which is cheapest when you are young. [▶ 7](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aFoMYz_jWcs)
- Test each friend: do they raise or lower your odds of hitting your goal? Several draining friends compound like a slow spell in a video game. There are no social obligations, only social consequences; if the "punishment" for skipping events is fewer invitations, that saves you time. [▶ 32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oys_fv25SYM)
- His approach: about 100 g of protein per meal from no-prep, very lean foods with almost no fat or carbs, then deliberately add carbs (dessert, cereal) when he wants them. He tends to eat the same meal for years to remove decisions. [▶ 38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hGX_z5rXRlU)
- If you skip college, stay a professional learner: treat your first four years of work as being paid to learn, spend that money on courses or books, and pay skilled people by the hour (e.g. one hour a week) to teach you; accept starting at minimum wage. [▶ 43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nxL4ZfVqKLI)
- Judge every friend, habit and belief by one test: does it make my goal more or less likely? Five friend questions: would you be flattered to be compared to them; are you fulfilled or just less lonely; can you be yourself; do you like who they are or who they might become; would you want your child to be friends with them? Cut friends who only reminisce about the past, and expect a lonely in-between period while you change groups. [▶ 56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vhOV_Od0A3M)
- You can predict how wealthy people will become by the units they think in: weeks and paychecks versus years, decades and $100k investments. Most of his big deals came within one or two degrees of people he had met. Relationships beat hacks. [▶ 70](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Day0yToqeco)
- When injured, keep training the movement at the lightest weight that doesn't hurt and add a little each week (he added 10 lbs weekly) instead of stopping completely. He also tests products systematically against a written list of criteria (he has tried 30-40 tank tops and about 50 shoes), which shows his habit of standardizing daily decisions. [▶ 84](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ABOd589OyTM)
- Sleep and food raise all four capacities. Eulogies mostly skip accomplishments and focus on service and character, meaning how someone treated others. Behaving well consistently earns a reputation for being unshakable, and people reinforcing that identity creates a virtuous cycle. Many people chase new tactics but can't execute consistently because of low mental toughness. [▶ 88](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SE9_1PYsaP0)
- Context: he has eaten dessert almost every night for 20 years and kept a six-pack, after trying keto, high-carb, low-carb, intermittent fasting, carnivore and more. He has eaten the same way for about 10 years, and it fits around business dinners and drinks. He presents it as what works for him, not as settled science. [▶ 92](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fxyhIXZ6Yog)
- Context: at a mastermind of founders whose businesses totaled about $500M in revenue, others followed keto, fasting and biohacking while he ate candy and ice cream daily and was in the best shape of anyone there. He says he has stayed lean for about 17-20 years this way, and several attendees later got in shape using it. He considers most entrepreneur biohacking marketing fluff. [▶ 100](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RpqSy5V1fFQ)
- Trust runs on zero punishment: years of reinforcement can be erased by a single betrayal. To be trustworthy, respond well at the moment of disclosure (thank them, treat it as theirs to control) and never use it against them later, including indirectly by passing it on. [▶ 104](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k5-57282taI)
- Relationships are exchanges that are either reinforced or punished; a long positive history buys patience during hard times, but without ongoing reinforcement even decade-long friendships fade. [▶ 163](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vVssypj7nYw)
- Play foolish games and you win foolish prizes: a tragic outcome is sacrificing for years to reach a podium only to realize you didn't want the trophy and played to impress people you don't care about. [▶ 165](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P14HA83uNJE)
- Accept hard tradeoffs consciously: in your 20s you either live it up and become underskilled or work it up and become under-lived, and skills compound while most of the living it up won't matter later; he gave up football and TV to expand from 6 to 10 gyms. [▶ 174](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqjGxVW-Ae0)
- Intake tactics: keep supplements by the bed or toothbrush so you remember them; to avoid night urination take salt tabs with an electrolyte drink, front-load fluids in the morning and stop liquids ~3 hours before bed; eat meals at consistent times and finish the last meal ~2 hours before bed; stop alcohol ~4 hours before bed. [▶ 192](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=55H71isO_Bo)
- Breathing: nasal strips helped him most (after years of poor nasal breathing and eventually surgery); saline sprays help some people; avoid relying on sleep-disrupting medications (not medical advice). [▶ 192](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=55H71isO_Bo)
- If college is about socializing, there are far cheaper ways: work all day and go out at night and you'll end four years debt-free with savings and stories. [▶ 226](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5RiR6cBLkFg)
- Quitting consulting at 22 (despite a paid-off condo and his father's approval) was by far the hardest decision of his life, harder than any later crisis; he felt he had to let his father's dream die for his own to live, accepting he would "die" in his father's eyes. Years later he had to make peace that his father did his best as a single immigrant dad. [▶ 231](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3e73Qn6NOo)
- Remembering that even the Queen is rarely thought about months after death frees him to take big shots. Grief and disappointment come from expectations ("should"); reframing expectations (e.g. a cat that lived two years) reduces suffering. [▶ 231](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3e73Qn6NOo)
- He left a consulting job his father had set up, deciding he'd rather "die to his father" than to himself. He judged that putting the ~$100k an MBA would cost into a business for two years would teach more and could match a job's income. [▶ 237](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3iPYrHhkEc)
- Punishment fades but reward sticks, so the hardest habits to break are ones that rewarded you; replace them with something more rewarding. Early entrepreneurs get rewarded for big risky jumps and must unlearn that to stick with one thing. 2024 was his first year with no FOMO. [▶ 240](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q-_hwD1jNK4)
- Swap "chemistry" for "shared mission" as a pillar: chemistry fades in about two years, so look for shared mission (where you're going), values (how you get there) and interests (what you do along the way). Hollywood gets it backward: the partner who makes sense on paper is the one who lasts. [▶ 242](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NI22-qg2Hio)
- Three truths: give first without expectation; if you cannot do it forever, do not do it for a day; if nothing matters, you get to decide what matters. Greatness is when reality beats expectations. Lessons he expects at 40: patience works, define your terms, and enjoy the present. [▶ 246](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTAXjVgK-1o)
- Muscle built over 16+ years is like passive income that needs only light upkeep (training 1-2x per week). His diet is fixed: protein shake and bar, then meat and sweet potato for lunch to hit about 150g of protein early, and a free dinner out. [▶ 249](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=evNrefJmM_I)
- Happiness defined in practical terms: live as many days in a row as you can like your ideal day. His current ideal day is working out with someone he likes, eating with people he likes, and building something. Pain shows up during growth, plateaus and decline alike, so suffering is feedback, not a sign something is wrong. Force-ranking his past years showed that even his worst recent year beat older ones. [▶ 251](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f_UL-z1xgI)

lessons.t: Fear, rejection & confidence · 54 ideas
lessons.md:
- Rejection from strangers costs nothing: each no leaves you where you were plus experience, and one yes can change your life, so either you learn or you win. [▶ 4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YFA8AS5Cu2w)
- Reread one great book several times until you can teach it rather than skimming many; drop mediocre books quickly, favor older books written to pass on knowledge, and judge reading by whether your behavior changes. [▶ 16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cq8GyLrEuAk)
- Treat failure as learning: fail once and try again; seek out discomfort since the pain of being new is mostly self-judgment; and stop repeating the same mistake (same bad partner, same failed tactic). [▶ 19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ySuYdJ0H4s)
- Your fear of regret has to outweigh your fear of rejection. Fear lives in vagueness, so write out the worst-case plan B in concrete steps (for him: couch surfing, then getting another job with a good story). One measure of personal power is how short the gap is between making a decision and acting on it. Responsibilities only grow, so the easiest time to jump is now. [▶ 24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MzAIP_WJ-jE)
- Confidence follows evidence: act first and confidence comes after. Swap "fake it till you make it" for proving it to yourself through action. Confidence without a track record is self-deception. [▶ 66](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pt50QF6al8g)
- Confidence is a prediction that what you expect will happen, and it is domain-specific. To get good at something, do that exact thing. Time spent rehearsing the sales script builds more confidence than hyping yourself in the mirror. He failed his first ever sales consult (let the prospect leave to "get her card"). [▶ 66](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pt50QF6al8g)
- Comparing yourself is useful for spotting gaps ("he's better at ads, what is he doing?"). Turning it into a judgment about your worth is not. Remember others have felt the same pain and learn from them. [▶ 71](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WOZGZK7K-Jo)
- You can outperform 99% of people by learning to handle three things: the shame of rejection, the boredom of repetition, and the sting of feedback. About 20 hours of real practice in a skill like sales teaches more than any number of books, because doing it gives you feedback. [▶ 86](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XGm2ERU9qtA)
- Confidence comes from a pile of proof that you've done the thing, not from affirmations. Do it until you're bored and the outcome no longer moves you emotionally. Mastery is when the work becomes rewarding in itself, so masters enjoy it more than novices do. [▶ 89](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4evdxF5G0s)
- Don't reject the first step because you fear the extreme outcome (like the gym client afraid of getting "too bulky" on day one). You can't be busy and broke at once: if you're broke, fill your time with the hands-on work that makes money. [▶ 110](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H_ZLs1-jOKQ)
- Reject "industry standard" as a target: it literally means average, with half your competitors better than you, and the average business makes almost no money. Claims that "our industry is different" (HVAC, SEO, trucking) usually excuse low standards; you get what you tolerate. [▶ 122](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A248pGXTSoY)
- Distinguish breaking laws (real, written consequences) from breaking unspoken social rules, whose consequences are far smaller than feared; critics have only a couple of sentences of context on your life, and you're the one with full context. [▶ 143](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OHu1FY1R-x0)
- Don't judge your early chapter against someone else's late one; his first ads and videos were rough, yet he now produces about 450 content pieces a week and runs a portfolio above $250M in annual revenue. [▶ 155](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yb2cLMMuMdQ)
- Example: a friend who lost a physique competition realized the winning look would require sacrifices too costly for the rest of her life; judges signal what they want after the fact through who they pick. [▶ 165](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P14HA83uNJE)
- If you compete, control the controllables and judge yourself by your own standard of performance, not the trophy; and if the goal is money, choose a game that actually produces money. [▶ 165](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P14HA83uNJE)
- Courage is scarcer than intelligence; fear lives in the vague, so define the worst case concretely (in developed countries it's rarely catastrophic) and keep trying, since you're not a failure while still trying. [▶ 174](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqjGxVW-Ae0)
- Push or pivot: when stagnating (as in his consulting job), either push for more challenge or change paths; coasting and doing neither cost him time and self-confidence. [▶ 196](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tdLLGKoBojo)
- Arguments instead of affirmations: rather than repeating "I am wealthy," say "I am [trait] because..." and list real past examples of showing that trait, until the self-story becomes automatic. He works on wisdom this way, seeing good judgment as the top trait. [▶ 217](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4vLgOX1Ykjg)
- Fear is not cowardice; letting fear steer your behavior away from what you want is. He would rather be labeled a failure than a coward. [▶ 230](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kl-I7sUcAOY)
- "Guaranteed bad vs. chance at good": staying put guarantees an outcome you don't want. Fear lives in vagueness, so play the worst case out specifically (a good story, can get another job, couch-surf) and the amygdala loses its grip; the same works for hard conversations. [▶ 230](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kl-I7sUcAOY)
- Early on he led purely by fear, which works short-term but not long-term; his wife Leila showed him influence. Her loyalty when he was broke (willing to sleep under a bridge with him) and her record-setting solo launch were defining. [▶ 231](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3e73Qn6NOo)
- Reframe anxiety as excitement before a presentation, but real anxiety mostly means you haven't practiced enough; rehearse until you're bored of the material. Confidence = the probability your prediction of what happens is right, built by repeated attempts (e.g. 1/10, then 2/10, then 8/10 approaches going well). [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- Most people fail from fear of judgment by an imaginary inner critic, not lack of know-how; everyone finds a way to pay a surprise bill, but won't use that resourcefulness for themselves. Behaviorally it shows as refusing short-term discomfort for long-term achievement. [▶ 233](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRPChBZ0Rjo)
- People don't fear failure, they fear others' judgment of it (losing a video game level in private isn't embarrassing). Make your future self your only judge. [▶ 234](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tigt75AcLLA)
- Model people by observable behavior only. From Elon he copies big concentrated bets, trading equity for speed, tying companies to a mission, and the process: question requirements, delete, optimize, speed up feedback loops, automate. Courage is the trait everything else follows from, and is a matter of degree. [▶ 235](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rRI0J8a4I9g)
- Higher stakes mean bigger losses: to make $1B you must be willing to lose $100M. Judge a decision on the information available then; checking everything is impossible without micromanaging. [▶ 241](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZKhApFCWO8)
- Past failure doesn't change the work required to succeed now. Build confidence by generalizing small past wins and adding weight to goals gradually (get out of bed, then a 10-minute walk), raising your own standards as you go. [▶ 241](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZKhApFCWO8)
- He drops labels and "because" stories: you don't know why you do things, so stick to what you can observe. Telling someone "you're right, you'll never succeed" often provokes them to fight back. Doing produces results regardless of mood or self-image; don't wait to feel confident. [▶ 241](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZKhApFCWO8)
- Fear of sucking is really fear of judgment, usually by one or two specific people. Name them: he nearly held off selling his company at $46.2M because of imagined disapproval from one acquaintance. If you cannot explain why you believe something, it is someone else's belief. [▶ 243](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gEF67-G9MO0)
- People are not afraid of failing; they are afraid of being seen failing and losing status. Starting anything new usually means a step back in status (he went from consultant to living in his gym as a trainer, where his Vanderbilt degree meant nothing). [▶ 248](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPV7Sn-POlM)
- Confidence comes from a stack of undeniable proof, not affirmations; confidence without evidence is delusion. He defines confidence as the likelihood you will do what you say. He rehearsed his launch presentation three times a day for 30 days (in his head, out loud recorded, then reviewing and editing slides), so he was calm in front of hundreds of thousands. [▶ 248](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPV7Sn-POlM)
- Why people do not act: fear of punishment (really fear of judgment), lack of the right reward, and environment. Fix it by rewarding yourself for controllable activities rather than outcomes, reframing judgment, and changing your surroundings. [▶ 248](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPV7Sn-POlM)
- Don't analyze your fuel: if revenge, shame, fear or anger gets you moving, use it, then gradually let the rewards of the work itself take over. Success as revenge only works when you win so big that the people no longer matter to you. [▶ 251](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f_UL-z1xgI)
- The "good old days" were always times of pursuit, not achievement. Aim for joy and meaning rather than happiness, which is circumstantial. Separate outcome from winning: judge yourself by how hard you worked, like praising a kid who loses 10-0 but gave everything, so self-respect stays in your control. [▶ 252](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KepgJld9O2w)
- Beginners look awkward; name the few specific people whose opinions you fear and ask whether they deserve to steer your life. Use the gap between you now and the person you want to become as the reason to keep enduring; nostalgia is memory with the pain removed. [▶ 15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDBkiBnMrHs)
- Your "type" is a warning sign: if dating that type had worked, you'd be married to one. Dating outside your type, and having plenty of bad dates, builds the pattern recognition to judge people accurately. Assessing people is a valuable skill; what you avoid is labeling them good or bad. [▶ 23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jiCGLDhUCHY)
- Pick someone who judges you by the same metrics you judge yourself on, and who sees your work toward your goals as a contribution to the household, not as something taken from them. Mismatched scorecards produce constant "you could do more" conflict. [▶ 23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jiCGLDhUCHY)
- Judge a partnership the way you'd judge a business partnership: same goals and values, complementary skills, and success measured by how much better the two of you are together than apart. A good spouse never asks you to leave the game when it's on the line. [▶ 23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jiCGLDhUCHY)
- Two tests for friendship: do they genuinely root for your wins, and do they make you better? Peers cheer when you quit your job because it lowers your status, then resent you as you rise. Envy is wanting what someone has; jealousy is fearing you'll lose what you have. Treat hate as data, nothing more. [▶ 31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ln24y0FPJHo)
- Sadness comes from feeling you have no options, usually because of self-imposed "nevers." Ask which trade you are refusing to make, then play the feared outcome out in concrete detail (for example, disappointing your parents means fewer texts and a different holiday). Fear lives in vagueness and shrinks once the details are specific. [▶ 86](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XGm2ERU9qtA)
- Every choice has a price and a payoff; judging others' trades (e.g., $500 shoes) without their context is pointless. The worst trades are unconscious ones, such as losing the fun of your 20s without building the skills or savings that would set up your 30s. A 1% outcome requires 1% trade-offs. [▶ 139](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MZPVPCIeUpg)
- Criticism almost never comes from people ahead of you in that domain. His childhood germaphobia ended after five days camping without washing his hands and nothing bad happening; others' opinions are similar, feared but harmless. Even a billionaire investor on TikTok gets called a fake guru, so you'll never seem legitimate to the ignorant; being hated by bad people is a compliment. [▶ 139](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MZPVPCIeUpg)
- He once feared winning a huge lottery because it would rob him of proving he could earn it; the point of the game is who you become. [▶ 162](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q9qBqnhdWKw)
- Others' judgments about how you spend your time only reveal how they would spend theirs; you can't do what everyone does and expect a different result. [▶ 163](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vVssypj7nYw)
- Judge sub-markets, not cities: opinions of a city rest on a handful of people and places, and affluent neighborhoods everywhere have the same chains, so living quality differs little; when there is no real difference, pick the zero-income-tax option. [▶ 212](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RBR4BwOVNvs)
- Borrow belief: his wife believed he could succeed before he did, and he trusted her judgment until his own belief caught up. [▶ 217](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4vLgOX1Ykjg)
- Most people go to college (like marrying, having kids or buying a house) because it's the expected next step, not a conscious decision. Fear of disappointing parents or looking like the "troubled kid" is a bad reason. [▶ 226](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5RiR6cBLkFg)
- You once wanted the life you have; he was about as content poor as rich, and wellbeing returns to baseline after both windfalls and tragedies (e.g. paralysis, after 3-6 months), so neither future wants nor fears deserve much weight today. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- The relationship worked because Leila never tried to change him; he rejects compromising on who you are. They tested a six-week breakup early to see whether they could still be good business partners apart; she set a sales record launching a gym in Hawaii, which earned his respect and made her a real partner. [▶ 242](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NI22-qg2Hio)
- Make who you become the goal so you can win daily; milestones feel smaller as you approach them. Work-life balance should be judged over a lifetime: being unbalanced for a season can buy more balance later. People want the benefits of other paths without their costs, and the "perfect pick" with no trade-offs does not exist. [▶ 243](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gEF67-G9MO0)
- Quitting consulting was emotional, not mathematical: his father strongly disapproved and they stopped talking for a while. He chose rejection by his father over rejecting himself, and only phoned after driving halfway across the country. [▶ 244](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sdd4BST87ks)
- All criticism reduces to he lives his life in a way I would not prefer. Haters are a fixed cost, so judge the quality of your haters; even revered religious figures were hated, so no one is above it. [▶ 245](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9urSNqHrCFM)
- Ego gives unearned confidence; he estimates he has cut his ego about 40% since 19 by linking success to having less ego, viewing everyone as distant family, and keeping the message above the messenger. [▶ 246](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTAXjVgK-1o)
- He rejects "should" frames about how life must be lived (e.g., relax like Europeans); preferences are personal, so do what you love rather than seek legitimacy from people you do not care about. [▶ 247](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WK-d4H7xtvQ)

lessons.t: Focus: one thing, say no · 70 ideas
lessons.md:
- Growth, stagnation and decline are all stressful, so stress is not a sign something is wrong. The hardest work is the priority you do not yet know how to solve; quantify what solving it is worth (e.g. a feature worth $150M) and learn by doing, since learning means new behavior under the same conditions. [▶ 6](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oRMG_HpOAN4)
- Champions usually lack distractions you still have; with equal hours, their edge is ruthless elimination and singular focus, not saying yes to everything. [▶ 16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cq8GyLrEuAk)
- Four steps for the year: eliminate distractions, get started, get better, never stop. Your calendar and card statements predict next year's results; budget time and money toward the identity you want (commitment means eliminating alternatives). [▶ 18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6KqndZuN_Yk)
- Focus is what remains after removing everything else (like a writer locked in a bare room with only a notepad). Tactics: time-block tasks with a visible timer and pause it when distracted, set the phone to grayscale (about 30% less usage), turn off all notifications, use a do-not-disturb mode, and drop whole channels (he does not use email). [▶ 18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6KqndZuN_Yk)
- Start now, not on January 1; about 20 focused hours makes you decent at most skills. Failure increases your odds of success because it reflects action and gives feedback; build a "failure resume" (he lists losing deals, bad hires, six failed businesses, nine failed partnerships). His father failed medical school entry twice in a foreign language before succeeding. [▶ 18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6KqndZuN_Yk)
- Declarative knowledge (knowing about) is not procedural (knowing how); your first 100 cold calls teach more than 100 videos. Saying no without remorse and hearing no without losing enthusiasm gets harder as better opportunities appear. [▶ 18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6KqndZuN_Yk)
- Persistence creates timing: if you never stop, you will be ready whenever opportunities show up. Opportunities multiply as your skills grow, so build as many skills as you can. [▶ 24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MzAIP_WJ-jE)
- Step 2, reclaim time. A 9-to-5 leaves two roughly 4-hour blocks (5-9am and 5-9pm) that most people waste. Without a job, use a 4/4/4 split: 4 hours promoting (do it first, because nobody can pay you if they don't know you exist), 4 hours delivering, 4 hours building (finding opportunities and ranking them). [▶ 27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jfW6gL6hKhk)
- Winners focus on customers; losers focus on winners. Reacting to a competitor once cost him about $25M. Being copied means you've already won; worry when nobody copies you. Markets are far bigger than they feel (45 client gyms in a city with about 1,500). [▶ 31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ln24y0FPJHo)
- Sadness comes from feeling you have no options, so solve it with knowledge. Anxiety comes from many options and no priorities, so solve it with a decision. Disappointment is an unmet expectation: change the expectation or change reality. Making "being" a certain kind of person your goal keeps it fully in your control. Ask your future self for advice. [▶ 31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ln24y0FPJHo)
- Priorities mean two things can't be equally important. Splitting time evenly between two tasks quietly makes neither a priority. Prioritizing means saying no to everything else, a temporary "season of no." [▶ 41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lRyGIzW9d9k)
- Tactics: he changed his phone number (gave the old one to his EA and only reached out himself to people he needed), took no meetings from 4am to noon (8 uninterrupted hours of priority work), and kept the same bedtime and wake time on weekends. [▶ 41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lRyGIzW9d9k)
- Sadness comes from a perceived lack of options (fix it with knowledge); anxiety comes from too many options with no priorities (fix it with a decision). If you don't know what to do, learn; if you know, do it; if you are doing it, never stop, regardless of how you feel. [▶ 45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFElGv5ZmRM)
- His focus stack: earplugs plus earmuffs or headphones, nicotine gum, caffeine, and a visible timer set to his estimate of how long a task should take. He blocks meetings until about noon or 1pm and values empty calendar days for deep work. [▶ 53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lJF__n_34ew)
- Decide fast: unmade decisions weigh the most, and if a wrong choice can be fixed quickly, choosing now and correcting later beats deliberating. Move deadlines from week to day to hour, try for 20 focused hours before calling something hard, and use phone hygiene (grayscale, all notifications off, do-not-disturb, no email) to remove distractions so focus is what's left. [▶ 56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vhOV_Od0A3M)
- Watch for "I have to / I must / I need to" language about conditions you don't control, and for self-imposed punishments ("I can't focus without X"). Aim to perform just as well on a cot in a closet as in an ideal setup. He uses Rocky versus Drago to illustrate. [▶ 64](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ErWpi_91b70)
- Write a "not-to-do" list of what you'll give up (he dropped football and Netflix while working 80-100 hour weeks). People ahead of you have the same hours; they just say no to more. [▶ 69](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ueJg14gQLuc)
- The best productivity hack is to do nothing but the task you set out to do. Many productivity systems are just guilt-free procrastination. Focus, commitment and "decide" (which shares a root with cutting off) all mean removing alternatives. [▶ 75](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XwzU4RikbGs)
- He writes from waking until about noon and takes no meetings before noon or 1pm. That first block always goes to his current top priority. Writing has three phases: work out what to say (the longest), draft it (the easiest), then compress repeatedly. If two sentences mean the same as one, cut one. His book shrank from 1,000+ pages to about 270. [▶ 84](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ABOd589OyTM)
- When you don't know what to do next, build capacity: rest, fitness, savings, skills. Opportunities come to everyone, but only people with spare capacity notice them and can act. In the Princeton "Good Samaritan" study, whether seminary students stopped to help depended on how rushed they were, not on their moral views. There was about a 6x difference between those running early and those running late. [▶ 85](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EonibwnAEME)
- Problems are finite; missed opportunities are infinite and are the gateway to mediocrity. Solve the problems you know you must before chasing new ideas, park ideas on a "big money ideas" list to cool off, and remember that feeling rushed comes from who you compare yourself to, which you choose. [▶ 108](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cnbHgYYHzyE)
- Match the size of change to your situation. His self-described second-biggest weakness after lack of focus is "killing a mosquito with a cannon": wanting to rebuild everything whenever something feels uncomfortable. [▶ 118](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bpIW-dfKFoE)
- Diagnose your emotions: anxiety usually means you have too many options and cannot choose (a prioritization problem); sadness or hopelessness means you see no options (an information problem you can solve by learning). [▶ 127](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I64gYLBrics)
- The longest realistic time horizon wins, but if you have bills to pay, focus first on a near-term step like going from $100k to $1M a year; each level gives you resources and a clearer view of reality. [▶ 130](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=spXH1kJ6q-Q)
- The cost of failure has never been lower (shots on goal for the price of a software subscription); the real competition is distraction. Separate failing from being a failure; most big founders had many failed ventures first, and business is an infinite game you lose only by quitting. [▶ 137](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YUXLJauT4eY)
- Humans overestimate downside and underestimate upside (an evolutionary bias), so the opportunity lies in what is uncertain and delayed, the two costs most people won't pay. Apart from death, failure is psychological: if it doesn't work, try again, because failure changes little while success can change everything. [▶ 139](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MZPVPCIeUpg)
- Problem 4, focus: the leap that made you an entrepreneur trains you to jump again whenever things get hard, and every new opportunity looks different. Commitment is eliminating alternatives (the chicken is involved in breakfast, the pig is committed); measure focus by the number and quality of things you turn down, and give yourself a mental point for each "no". [▶ 142](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F84olnKkseM)
- Finish what you start regardless of cost or time; being seen as cringe is the price of caring more about your goals than appearances, and goals get easier as you become harder to distract. [▶ 143](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OHu1FY1R-x0)
- If you earn more per hour than a service costs, outsourcing "humaning" chores buys back time; he lists seven investments in priority order that together can reclaim roughly a week every month, as long as the freed hours go into building skills or income. [▶ 147](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3SVksBB3_YY)
- "Zero" priority, sleep: optimize the place you spend a third of your life with blackout curtains (dark enough that open and closed eyes look the same), earplugs, electrical tape over small lights, an eye mask, no screens before bed, and optionally a cooling mattress (about $2k) that can cut cooling bills. It raises the productivity of every waking hour. [▶ 147](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3SVksBB3_YY)
- Shiny new opportunities are like the distracting figure in The Matrix training scene: they reappear at every level of growth and get more tempting as you get bigger, so you must relearn how to decline them each time. [▶ 156](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yflKMUffctE)
- Personal beliefs: attention is your most valuable asset, focus on making rather than saving, never count what you could have saved on roads not taken, and since everyone is effectively taxed 100% at death, money should buy options rather than cost you them. [▶ 161](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w5g0JiO7OdE)
- Focus and energy are finite: he declined a past mentor's request for a two-hour weekly call (about 100 hours a year) while protecting a weekly one-hour meeting with his closest friend. [▶ 163](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vVssypj7nYw)
- Plan the night before: pick one to three priorities for tomorrow (no fixed rule on the number) so you can sleep and begin the moment you wake. [▶ 168](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bkPwFqa89gE)
- Speed is not rushing or doing many things; it is refusing to be distracted by low-priority work and acting on what matters. [▶ 180](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oW6JkqL6sdM)
- Attention, not time, is the entrepreneur's scarcest resource: hours are useless if your focus is scattered, leaving you "everywhere and nowhere." A billionaire friend's phone only rings for whitelisted contacts. [▶ 199](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6ZEZWuVC8-8)
- Picture attention as a small bowl of marbles spread across trauma, marriage, health, spirituality and business; consolidating the small piles gives more to the one thing you want to grow, and abundant attention makes hard problems look easy (like solving a problem after sleep). [▶ 199](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6ZEZWuVC8-8)
- Clarity focuses attention: define the single number you need (e.g. members needed for your desired lifestyle), then filter every opportunity by whether it moves that number. [▶ 199](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6ZEZWuVC8-8)
- Simplicity takes more work than complexity; listing every feature or benefit is usually lazy thinking from failing to prioritize, and the right business moves often run against natural instinct. [▶ 202](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-JLN1d1ZKUU)
- The moment you hit the hard problem is exactly when shiny new opportunities look most tempting, and they get more attractive the better you become; resist them. [▶ 206](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=07jC6ooRIHw)
- Commit to the business like a marriage: being married freed up a big share of his attention that used to go to "what if" options, and dropping side projects and distracting partnerships does the same for a business. [▶ 206](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=07jC6ooRIHw)
- You only get four or five big runs in a career, like Buffett's 20-punch card, so choose few opportunities and give up shiny ones. [▶ 222](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jqo0lVveh98)
- Don't straddle two models; commitment means eliminating alternatives, and focus is measured by how many things you say no to. Even a small side business consumes far more than its share of mental bandwidth when problems hit. [▶ 224](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rm4zRdLAyjw)
- The trap: extra AI capacity gets spent on lower-priority tasks you'd never have bothered with, done faster and automated, which doesn't matter. Scarcity used to force prioritization. [▶ 227](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WttZ6b-KUP4)
- Focus is measured by what you say no to; commitment is eliminating alternatives. Running three businesses at once is arrogance, since your competitor does one. Compare year 0 of a new venture to year 3-to-4 of your current one, not year 0 to year 0. His biggest mistakes all came from splitting attention. [▶ 230](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kl-I7sUcAOY)
- When broke and with his mother in hospital after a DUI, he coped by ignoring the bleak big picture and focusing only on controllable actions (100 reachouts, $100/day of ads, kill bad ads). Lead generation in any industry became his "get out of jail free card". [▶ 233](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRPChBZ0Rjo)
- No half measures: decide if something is for you or for the audience (or a dream house vs. an investment) rather than blending two priorities into a mediocre result. [▶ 239](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2IoKsGLpGys)
- Success has never been easier, but distraction and comfort have never been easier either. The safety net (you won't starve or be homeless) means you can take bigger shots. He believes in conditional "shoulds" (if you want X, do Y), not absolute ones. [▶ 240](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q-_hwD1jNK4)
- Most people never start (a belief problem); those who start often fail from lack of focus, splitting limited resources across several businesses. Knowledge is declarative (knowing it's possible) and procedural (knowing how); the second only comes from doing. [▶ 240](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q-_hwD1jNK4)
- During his worst 90-120 days (lost savings to a partner, his mother's accident, a DUI and head-on crash, spread across agencies, gyms and launches), the fix was having the hard conversations he'd avoided: he ended three partnerships, cut back drinking and focused on Gym Launch alone. The life you want is often on the other side of a few hard conversations. [▶ 242](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NI22-qg2Hio)
- Five stages new entrepreneurs go through: uninformed optimism, informed pessimism, the valley of despair, informed optimism, achievement. Most people bail at stage 3 and restart on a new shiny thing; staying in the pain is what forces you to learn the variables and break through. [▶ 243](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gEF67-G9MO0)
- Ignorance tax: not knowing how to earn more is an opportunity cost every year, so pay to get into any room where you can learn. Definitions: learning is same condition, new behavior; intelligence is rate of learning; resilience is how long a bad event affects you. [▶ 245](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9urSNqHrCFM)
- Obsessing over competitors makes you emotionally reactive and adds no value; competitors do not put you out of business, obsessing over them does. Focus on customers. [▶ 246](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTAXjVgK-1o)
- Handling money, sticking with things, and focus are trainable skills. People who hop between ventures have not been rewarded for sticking, or burned enough by restarting. [▶ 247](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WK-d4H7xtvQ)
- Daily structure: wake up around 4:30-5:30, start working within about 45 minutes, and no meetings before about 12:30, which gives a full uninterrupted workday every morning. Work that isn't finished rolls to the next day; prioritizing well matters more than doing more. [▶ 249](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=evNrefJmM_I)
- When smart people argue hard on both sides (morning routines, plan B, manifesting), the variable probably doesn't matter. Be a deleter: improve life by removing things rather than adding. A plan B (his was driving Uber and dancing on stage to save money for another shot) can be a short-term speed bump rather than a distraction. [▶ 251](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f_UL-z1xgI)
- Find the big domino. Most dating hacks are about how you come across, and they fall apart over time. The one thing that makes the rest unnecessary is becoming someone genuinely worth being with. [▶ 23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jiCGLDhUCHY)
- Rank your priorities in a partner. If they deliver your #1 but miss your #3, that's the trade you chose, so don't resent what it costs. State the costs of your goals plainly and check that your partner is willing to pay them too. [▶ 23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jiCGLDhUCHY)
- Live with people who share your goals: bad roommates distract you, and responsible roommates with smaller goals project their limiting beliefs onto you. Never take advice from people with smaller goals for your life than you have. Having several roommates also cuts costs (he paid $400/month in a 7-person house). [▶ 51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q6SdmgIji30)
- If you want an ambitious spouse, the price is less time and flexibility in their busy seasons. Don't hold two expectations that conflict; adjust expectations to reality, talk openly rather than complain or be passive-aggressive, and support each other's goals instead of being a distraction. [▶ 60](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCgr7jT7JLA)
- Conflicting priorities (a partner, family who disapprove, leaving medical school) require ranking your reinforcers. Spell out the rules of engagement with a partner (e.g. focused work hours, full presence outside them). With family who don't share your vision, stay respectful, talk about the other topics, and if needed reduce contact. Generational labels matter little; reliable people exist in every age group. [▶ 121](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WeH2E1fGgaw)
- You get to pick your regrets or they'll be picked for you. Looking back, we wish for the benefits of trades we didn't make while already enjoying those we did; if you like your priorities, you've already won. The danger is passively letting options expire. [▶ 143](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OHu1FY1R-x0)
- Focus on observable behavior instead of feelings or intentions; in conflicts ask what do you want to have happen and choose responses by their second-order effect on future behavior rather than retaliating. [▶ 158](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s6tkRztZwYc)
- Don't invert priorities: moving away from people and places you love to grow net worth so you can later live where you want with those people defeats the purpose; also your enough number keeps moving (his went from $4M to $10M, $14M, $20M, $30M, $100M). [▶ 161](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w5g0JiO7OdE)
- Friendship is a spectrum, not yes/no; its opposite is someone who works against you by making you emotional, distracting you, or undermining your goals. [▶ 185](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1taVrxMFjaY)
- High-level operators keep their surroundings, devices and schedules quiet and clean, have low tolerance for distractions and negativity, and sit behind layers of protection (for him: Leila, the CEO, a team of four executive assistants); nobody has direct access to him. [▶ 199](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6ZEZWuVC8-8)
- Authenticity operationally is how you'd act if punishment were impossible: alignment of thought, word and deed, starting by saying what you actually think. Say no honestly instead of "I'm busy" (he showed someone his empty calendar). There are no social obligations, only social consequences. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- His working definitions: love = what you'd give up to keep something (he realized he loves his goals most, and Leila's goal is helping him reach them); learning = same condition, new behavior; intelligence = rate of learning; motivation = the flip side of deprivation, relative to your reference group; sadness = perceived lack of options; anxiety = many options, no priorities. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- Final five: best advice is do so much work that failure would be unreasonable; worst is follow your passion; wished-sooner is find people better than you and help them first; hardest lesson is focus on one thing. His law: everyone gives away all wealth at death so top capital-makers become top allocators and everyone starts closer to zero. [▶ 243](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gEF67-G9MO0)
- People root for you until you pass them, because you remind them of dreams they gave up; hate comes from below, since winners focus on goals and losers focus on winners. Strangers online often become bigger fans than your hometown, because your success does not implicate them. [▶ 248](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPV7Sn-POlM)

lessons.t: Learning & skill · 105 ideas
lessons.md:
- Learning means the same situation produces different behavior. If you attend a training and act the same afterward, you learned nothing. [▶ 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RdAKXJlMIZM)
- Ask "If I were coaching me, what would I tell me to do?" You already know more about your situation than any coach and usually aren't following your own advice. [▶ 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RdAKXJlMIZM)

- What he learned from nomad life: he missed familiar social circles (a month somewhere is too short for real relationships) and having his own things set up; rentals can't be customized. The answer is a middle path of 2-3 stocked homes in different climates as home bases. [▶ 212](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RBR4BwOVNvs)
- Think "models, not mentors": copy behaviors from people ahead of you. He drove across the country to a gym guru and paid to join his mastermind; in one day gym owners corrected his pricing, equipment, square footage and rent (never over $1.50/ft). Value a skill as the gap between your income and what the skill would earn. [▶ 230](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kl-I7sUcAOY)
- "Should" is the root of pain; drop unconditional shoulds about yourself and others. He stopped demanding that life be happy or meaningful and found contentment by doing the work he wanted. Happiness, operationally: string together as many good days in a row as possible. Meaning of life to him: learning. [▶ 230](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kl-I7sUcAOY)
- His happiness definition: do what you like with people you like as much as possible; autonomy is his core need. He feels most connected to himself while writing, which always matches difficulty to skill. [▶ 231](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3e73Qn6NOo)
- His contrarian core belief: meaning is self-ascribed, so suffering can be reframed; distress comes largely from beliefs about emotions (thinking sadness is wrong), and you can't have joy without sadness. A great mentor question: "What do I believe to be true that isn't?" [▶ 233](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRPChBZ0Rjo)
- They took courses meant for at-risk and divorcing marriages early on to learn communication and expectation-setting. A mentor told him to "look at your stats": if fitness, business and headspace all improved since meeting someone, that's the signal. Choose a partner who raises your standards, because as you grow, your alternatives improve too. [▶ 242](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NI22-qg2Hio)
- Achieving the external checklist (body, money, partner) showed him circumstances do not fix internal problems. Realizing everything eventually turns to dust quieted his ego and made him a better leader and husband; his main mentor is his imagined 85-year-old self, who would trade all the money to be young again. [▶ 246](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTAXjVgK-1o)
- The mission (documenting and sharing best practices for building companies) pulls him more than the billion-dollar goal; planning runs on 36-month, 12-month and quarterly horizons. He sees most biohacks as placebo that turns into superstition and dependency; the big basics (progressive overload, protein, sleep, time) matter most. [▶ 249](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=evNrefJmM_I)

lessons.t: Identity, ego & self-talk · 48 ideas
lessons.md:
- Proficiency carries you further than passion: like farmers who took pride in providing, aim to be passionate about excellence and your values rather than the product (a friend built a high-end cookie bakery without loving cookies). [▶ 15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDBkiBnMrHs)
- Assume the world is unfair and act accordingly; complaining and blaming circumstances produce nothing, while hard seasons build character ("your mess is your message"). Nobody, including the government, is coming to save you. [▶ 19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ySuYdJ0H4s)
- Treat business as an infinite game. The goal is to keep playing, not to "win," so separate your identity from any single business. People often quit an industry when they really only disliked one function in it; consider switching roles within the industry instead. [▶ 22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nh8Oc7ERdIU)
- Put yourself where you have no choice but to become the person you want to be. He signed a $5,000/month gym lease with $5,000 in the bank. Excuses may be valid, but the problem is still yours to solve. Do what's required, not just "your best." [▶ 24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MzAIP_WJ-jE)
- Get over your past. Losers define themselves by what happened to them; winners by what they make happen despite it, turning a hardship into an origin story. Treat today as a fresh spawn point. [▶ 29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ub1D6RQocRU)
- Events, masterminds and coaching programs often serve social needs more than real problems. He attended one mastermind, took what he needed, skipped it for 18 months to execute, and returned as a success story. Ask whether you need more information or more execution. [▶ 41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lRyGIzW9d9k)
- Most criticism boils down to "he lives his life in a way I would not prefer," which is true and fine. You do not have to catch what people throw at you, and hardship reveals your character rather than defining it, giving "memory dividends" you can draw on later. [▶ 45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFElGv5ZmRM)
- You become more productive by eliminating drains (you have one battery shared by family, chores and staff) rather than adding hacks. Someone doing about 96 productive hours versus about 3 in the same period moves roughly 30x faster. [▶ 57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gD0X-PLax5I)
- Be careful with "I am" statements (e.g., "I'm a high-anxiety person", "I'm all-or-nothing"). They lock a trait into your identity. Ask whether the label helps your goals, and if it doesn't, stop saying it. [▶ 64](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ErWpi_91b70)
- Say "I have a tendency toward..." or "I struggle with..." instead of "I am...". Your identity should be whatever this stage of growth demands. He believed he was bad at math until 26. [▶ 64](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ErWpi_91b70)
- Be the source of your results rather than a reaction to your environment: hold beliefs that serve you and succeed regardless of circumstances. [▶ 64](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ErWpi_91b70)
- Decision rule: pick the option that makes the more epic story. Treat disadvantages as what will make the eventual win more inspiring, and use your pain the way a hero would, not a villain. [▶ 66](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pt50QF6al8g)
- The many-sided die parable (from his Leads book): every player has a die with one green side, but you can't see how many sides it has (20 or 200). Each green roll turns another side green. Keep rolling and greens become the norm. People who complain about other people's luck stop rolling and lose. [▶ 71](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WOZGZK7K-Jo)
- At 27, taking home about $17M a year, he wanted to stay "rich and unknown" and explained celebrity wins away (family advantages and so on) to protect his ego. Seeing case after case forced him to drop a false belief. Wrong beliefs build a false reality you then make decisions in. [▶ 80](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6DCDGSnRDtM)
- Things that held portfolio businesses back: founders easing off once money was "enough," and unsupportive spouses or partners. Neutral support tends to become negative over time, so he suggests gauging a key hire's spouse's support. [▶ 108](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cnbHgYYHzyE)
- Turn complaints into "I don't know how" questions: "No one can sell like me" becomes I don't know how to get anyone to sell like me; "there are no good plumbers" becomes I don't know how to recruit, hire and train good plumbers. Questions have answers; complaints just push blame outward. Calling something "not scalable" usually means "I don't know how to scale it yet." [▶ 126](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q9OmYf_IlQ0)
- Avoid ritual dependence: elaborate routines become superstitions and crutches, while resilience means being able to work in any conditions. [▶ 168](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bkPwFqa89gE)
- Raise your standards by questioning inherited beliefs about what's possible; top performers he knows refuse to accept impossible unless someone can break it down to physical limits, then dismantle each obstacle. [▶ 174](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqjGxVW-Ae0)
- Be willing to look foolish and low-status short-term for long-term status; asymmetric returns come from being right when conventional wisdom bets against you, and you know yourself better than doubters do. You also become successful the moment you decide you are. [▶ 174](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqjGxVW-Ae0)
- Don't say I'm working on it when called by an old trait like a temper, since that accepts the frame; respond as the person you've become, e.g., you might have once, but not now. [▶ 176](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OvEfWrDOfNk)
- Memory compresses suffering into brief moments, and winners can rewrite their own story; consciously mark good moments to remember and let bad stretches compress. [▶ 193](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IYuiV4YuGB4)
- Progress beats pride: as you get successful it gets harder to ask for help, but he still pays in time, money or favors for it. Determination is rewarded more than intelligence, and it looks like a long string of failures until it works. [▶ 193](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IYuiV4YuGB4)
- Invisible limiting beliefs (e.g. that help must be one-on-one) can trap a business; look for evidence from other industries that the alternative works. [▶ 220](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N5MExtki_VI)
- Founders need an overarching worldview to frame setbacks. His is "cosmic irrelevance" (in a few generations nobody will remember him), which lowers anxiety about both upside and downside; a religious "this happens for me" frame works just as well. Without one, you become the center of the universe and slip into victimhood. [▶ 229](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6Ait5R-3-lI)
- Time horizon separates poor, middle class, rich and truly wealthy; you can gauge wealth by the horizon someone speaks in (today, month, decade). Building from belief in the problem (not need for cash this week) lengthens it; most failure comes from trading global benefit for local benefit (cake vs six-pack, salespeople skipping CRM notes). [▶ 246](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTAXjVgK-1o)
- Burnout isn't about hours worked. It happens when you've gotten used to the reward or the reward comes less often. Work ethic is mostly doing what you've been rewarded for before, cutting what you dislike, and building a history of being rewarded for delaying gratification. [▶ 251](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f_UL-z1xgI)
- Identity is just a description of repeated actions, so skip "be, do, have" and simply do what the person you want to become does; the work changes you more than you change it. [▶ 8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MNll1BaskLA)
- Five questions to vet a friend: would being compared to them be a compliment; are you fulfilled or just less lonely; can you be yourself; do you like who they are now or who they might become; would you want your child to be friends with them. Look for friends with goals of similar scale and similar dedication; expect lonely transition seasons, and take advice from people closest to your goals, not to you. [▶ 18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6KqndZuN_Yk)
- A spouse should love both who you are and who you're becoming, wanting you to grow (more of what you are) rather than change (become someone else). Treat a partner like an asset that appreciates: choose someone who keeps improving. [▶ 23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jiCGLDhUCHY)
- First marriages divorce at roughly 30%; repeat marriages pull the overall average up. Big goals plus big work is ambition; big goals plus laziness is entitlement, so become the person who deserves the partner you want. [▶ 23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jiCGLDhUCHY)
- The "Solomon" technique: people give better advice to others than to themselves, so write a message to your wise 85-year-old self and answer as him. It gives objectivity with full context and privacy; he finds it more useful than therapy. Also use whatever motivation you have (shame or aspiration), since the action matters more than the story behind it, and in some seasons simply maintaining counts as winning. [▶ 45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFElGv5ZmRM)
- Build the relationship on respect for character rather than on feelings of love, which come and go. Loyalty shown in a partner's darkest moments (losses, crises) is a strong signal. [▶ 60](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCgr7jT7JLA)
- Treat your non-negotiables as mutual agreements that only change if both agree. Putting the business before the marriage made both of them miserable by year three; putting the marriage first made their lives much better. [▶ 60](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCgr7jT7JLA)
- Drop the "because" explanations that tie your behavior to past trauma you can't change. Say "I have struggled with X" and work on present behavior you can change. "Potential plus trauma" is ego padding. [▶ 66](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pt50QF6al8g)
- Document the hard times (sleeping on the floor, lost sales, an empty bank account). Those are the photos and stories you'll actually use later, and they become proof of who you are. [▶ 66](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pt50QF6al8g)
- To improve adaptability, ask how this setback could serve you. Picture yourself as the protagonist of a movie with a happy ending and do what that character would do next. Guilt (breaking your own rules) and shame (breaking others') are only useful if they change your behavior. How long you grieve isn't a measure of how much you loved. [▶ 88](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SE9_1PYsaP0)
- "Marriage is compromise" is a belief, not a fact. Rigid schedules (finishing at 5pm to please a partner) can leave a driven person anxious and not themselves. [▶ 91](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-TydwZMX8wM)
- Being open about weaknesses is an asset. Harley stepped back from COO because someone else was better suited, which freed him for storytelling. Admit your flaws up front and hire people with complementary strengths. Choosing a life partner may be the most important decision you make; Hormozi cites a strong correlation between relationship quality and well-being. [▶ 95](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YZdE8U5eD_s)
- "Death creates clarity": write your own eulogy (500-1,000 words); accomplishments get a sentence, while service and character dominate, so pick causes worth serving and the traits needed to serve them. [▶ 130](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=spXH1kJ6q-Q)
- Think for yourself instead of adopting a pre-packaged identity; for every choice ask what do I want, and does this help me get it? Unusual combinations of reasoned choices make you interesting and form the base of a distinctive personal brand. [▶ 132](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YONIUpk-kAs)
- People from your past keep reinforcing your old identity and labels; growth looks like change to them, and you want people around you who don't believe the old stories you told about yourself. [▶ 163](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vVssypj7nYw)
- Build an anti-fragile identity rooted in your behaviors (who you are is what you do, especially when things go badly) rather than in what others think of you, so external swings stop driving your emotions and you can take necessary risks. [▶ 193](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IYuiV4YuGB4)
- Even if the hardship is real, winning despite it is a better story; when torn between two choices, pick the one that makes the better story at 85, which is usually the harder one. [▶ 207](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hnmBXTyMFKI)
- Childhood trauma is a convenient story for current behavior; almost everyone perceives some trauma as a child. You can choose to stop giving it power instead of letting it keep shaping you. [▶ 217](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4vLgOX1Ykjg)
- A borrower who could have kept a $50k invoice error paid the right amount anyway, earning Alex's goodwill. Lesson: you only get one name, and it becomes either an asset or a liability. [▶ 237](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3iPYrHhkEc)
- A desire is a contract to be unhappy until you get it; saying "I just want to be happy" creates a gap. Watch the belief statements you speak over yourself, and question beliefs you never thought to question.
