Life is a casino where death pushes every chip back to the middle, so build what you find cool and drop others' expectations. [▶ 239](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2IoKsGLpGys)
- He and Leila run on explicit agreements and see love as conditional on shared mission, values and interests. They create space to be missed and do a nightly 45-minute walk to go through both calendars. Don't expect a hookup to become a life partner. [▶ 241](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZKhApFCWO8)
- He calls ego his weakest trait: it's effective fuel but "burns dirty." Tools: humility as raising your regard for others or thinking of yourself less; the "grandfather frame" (an 85-year-old reborn in this moment is simply grateful); you can't feel entitled and grateful at once, so avoid "deserve," which is a contract to be unhappy. He follows Albert Ellis's three distortions: demands on the universe, demands on others, and avoidance. [▶ 242](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NI22-qg2Hio)

lessons.t: Emotions, stress & hard times · 73 ideas
lessons.md:
- Five-stage cycle of any new venture: uninformed optimism, informed pessimism, the valley of despair (where most quit and hop to a new idea), informed optimism, then achievement. Push through the valley rather than restarting elsewhere. [▶ 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VBoRLJimVzc)
- Inversion: since brains are better at spotting threats than solutions, list everything the worst version of you would do to guarantee failure (show up late, be unprepared, never follow up, never advertise, never ask for referrals), then flip each item. The shorter the list, the more powerful each item; e.g. a rep doubled the top performer just by always asking new buyers to bring someone else. [▶ 8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MNll1BaskLA)
- Winners and losers share the same goals (e.g. about half of high-school seniors expect to be millionaires by 25); what differs is commitment to activities. Separating self-worth from outcomes keeps your emotions steady. [▶ 11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7ITff1fIbSc)
- Interests get you started, proficiency keeps you going, pain tolerance gets you to the finish. All failure short of death is psychological; you are not out of business until someone physically stops you. [▶ 15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDBkiBnMrHs)
- Ignore critics. People who chose not to take a risk often want you to fail because it justifies their choice. Listen to the people closest to your goals, not the people closest to you. [▶ 24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MzAIP_WJ-jE)
- Much of entrepreneurship is buying the next week, month or payroll. Take positive-expected-value bets, but remember that most founders can only afford to play a couple of hands. Someone who refuses to quit rarely loses for good; they may just change vehicles. [▶ 26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xRxVpjeHmeA)
- Take asymmetric bets while your downside is close to zero (under 30, few obligations). Each failed attempt still leaves you with experience, so you never truly restart from scratch. Success is built brick by brick like a bridge: the result looks binary, but the building is linear. He had nine failed businesses before one worked. [▶ 29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ub1D6RQocRU)
- Reframing: ask in what world this setback is good, or how you will tell it as a turning point decades from now. After an unexpected multi-eight-figure bill due in 72 hours, he asked what it actually changed in his daily life (food, home, work) and saw that only his expectations of the future had changed. [▶ 45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFElGv5ZmRM)
- Redefine pain as the price of what you want: any goal costs either boredom or pain, and bigger goals cost more of both. Purpose raises pain tolerance a lot (research subjects took several times more shocks when told it spared their family), and work changes you even if the project fails, since after the first time you never start from scratch, only from experience. [▶ 45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFElGv5ZmRM)
- Endure what others won't: you can beat 99% of people simply by tolerating pain and uncertainty longer. Ask whether you are settling or "moving mountains," and what you would do if a life depended on finding another option, since most people never truly try. [▶ 45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFElGv5ZmRM)
- Much of the pain is mental: feeling incompetent and comparing yourself to others. When someone is ahead, either blame outside factors or accept that you aren't good enough yet, and only the second leads anywhere. [▶ 71](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WOZGZK7K-Jo)
- What keeps you in the game is frustration tolerance, fortitude, resilience and adaptability. Get your early failures out of the way quickly, and avoid any single loss big enough to knock you out. [▶ 71](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WOZGZK7K-Jo)
- "Trying" leaves room to fail. Stop trying to make ads work and make them work. If someone else can sell better than the founder, that person exists and can be found and hired. [▶ 72](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Ju1I37jWUM)
- Suffering is a fixed cost of every path, whether rich or poor, employee or founder, single or married. The only thing you control is what you get for it, so pick a goal big enough to justify the pain. Most people spend that same cost on comfort (Netflix, sleeping in) and get nothing back. [▶ 86](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XGm2ERU9qtA)
- Tolerance is how much hardship you take before your behavior changes (long fuse vs short fuse). Fortitude is how much your behavior changes once you snap (a five-minute walk vs quitting your job and wrecking your life). [▶ 88](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SE9_1PYsaP0)
- To improve tolerance, be more upset about letting something control your behavior than about the thing itself, and act as you normally would even in a bad mood. To improve fortitude and resilience, notice quickly when you've slipped, then deliberately turn back to normal. A feeling doesn't have to dictate an action. [▶ 88](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SE9_1PYsaP0)
- Writing down goals isn't what separates winners from losers, since both have the same goals. The difference is the activities they commit to. Make the activity itself the goal; a big-revenue month achieves nothing if the activities stop. [▶ 99](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YaNX49ygr0I)
- Design a system you can follow for life rather than an 8-week sprint. Since nothing is forbidden, you can't "fall off" or cheat. Restriction drives bingeing, and having dessert daily makes it unremarkable. Everyone loses weight in a calorie deficit, just at different speeds. [▶ 100](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RpqSy5V1fFQ)
- Making the trust calculus explicit isn't cold; it lets you name exactly why you don't trust someone (specific times something you shared was used against you) instead of a vague feeling. [▶ 104](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k5-57282taI)
- Like his "baby steps," a clear path lowers anxiety and analysis paralysis. Six drivers repeat at each stage, starting with personal growth (the owner is both the problem and the solution) plus purpose, people and culture, profit and planning; Ramsey estimates cycling through them 10-15 times. [▶ 114](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HJg4TYBgtI)
- People avoid bets because the cost feels certain and the upside uncertain. Play out the real worst case: for most socially functional people it's crashing on someone's couch for a while, not ruin. [▶ 139](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MZPVPCIeUpg)
- Baseline happiness is largely inherited and fairly stable, and the brain evolved to scan for threats, so achieving a goal won't make you permanently happier and failing won't make you permanently miserable; both the downside and upside are smaller emotionally than imagined. [▶ 139](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MZPVPCIeUpg)
- Test claims with three questions: what does this mean (define bundled terms), how do you know (evidence), and so what (utility); e.g., unpack stressed because lonely into observable events and check whether they actually correlate. [▶ 158](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s6tkRztZwYc)
- You can't be both busy and broke: if you're busy you should be earning, and if broke you have time to trade; if you feel both, you're wasting time. [▶ 159](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s9fSDCRPQNA)
- Drop luck as an explanation: assume anyone ahead of you did something you didn't and figure out what; it's better to fail and know why than succeed without knowing. [▶ 162](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q9qBqnhdWKw)
- Winners and losers share the same goals; what separates them is willingness to pay the price, just as you don't buy everything you like at the mall. [▶ 163](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vVssypj7nYw)
- Pain and uncertainty are prerequisites to progress; growth periods are often the most miserable, and you adapt to steady pain but not to pain that changes in kind or intensity, which is why entrepreneurship feels so hard. [▶ 174](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqjGxVW-Ae0)
- For one-time high-stakes events, expand prep (10-20 hours per hour presented), scale it with audience size and stakes, and rehearse in conditions as close as possible to the real thing (e.g. going live to simulate an audience; facing away from the mirror when squatting). [▶ 183](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m5ordaa7NN4)
- Mindset first: avoid "must/have to" superstitions about sleep and treat it 80/20; believe you do not need much sleep and can sleep anywhere, which reduces the anxiety that keeps people awake. Improving even 10-20% of your nights is a win. [▶ 192](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=55H71isO_Bo)
- Lying in a dark room with eyes closed delivers most of the rest benefit, so do not panic about falling asleep. Working hard and being active all day creates high daytime peaks and deep nighttime troughs. [▶ 192](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=55H71isO_Bo)
- He stopped using sleep trackers because his competitiveness turned scores into stress; he also keeps weekends on the same sleep schedule as weekdays, since weekends are his most productive work days. [▶ 192](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=55H71isO_Bo)
- Risk is unavoidable: every good thing (ideas, love, intimacy) carries its downside, and risking nothing gets you nothing. Beginners' biggest perceived losses are often in their heads, like status among friends or family image. [▶ 193](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IYuiV4YuGB4)
- When something bad happens, ask what it actually changes about your daily life (job, food, home, spouse); usually nothing, so the suffering is optional. Also ask how this event could make you stronger. [▶ 193](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IYuiV4YuGB4)
- Once you commit to the big bet, let small fires burn and sit with the pain of an unbuilt bridge rather than launching a second or third solution after 30 days, which steals resources from the sure but slower one. [▶ 202](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-JLN1d1ZKUU)
- Hedonic adaptation means new luxuries stop feeling special within weeks; a car subscription that allowed swaps went unused because swapping was a hassle. [▶ 212](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RBR4BwOVNvs)
- Fewer possessions can raise quality of life: giving away about 90% of his clothes made him feel lighter. Changing your surroundings is often easier than changing yourself. [▶ 212](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RBR4BwOVNvs)
- You don't need passion or purpose to start; waiting to find it is procrastination. Negative emotions such as anger, pain and disgust with your circumstances are valid fuel. [▶ 215](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDDFezF7OTA)
- Pain usually motivates harder than vision: picture a big dream on one side and your family's safety at stake on the other, and the threat moves you faster. [▶ 215](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDDFezF7OTA)
- Elite performers often run on loss aversion: he cites research that top Olympic medalists hate losing more than they love winning and feel relief on winning; some greats invented imagined slights to fuel themselves. [▶ 215](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDDFezF7OTA)
- Much of the work is unpleasant overhead; you keep going as long as the pain of moving forward is smaller than the pain of going back or of regret. [▶ 215](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDDFezF7OTA)
- Novelty fades: helping business owners will feel just as routine as your current work after hundreds of testimonials, as happened to him with weight-loss results. [▶ 224](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rm4zRdLAyjw)
- Emotional stability broken into three measurable behaviors: toughness (how many bad events in a row you absorb before your behavior changes), fortitude (how sharply your behavior drops once that threshold is crossed), and resilience (how fast you return to baseline). You can still feel upset; the goal is that behavior stays or quickly returns to normal. [▶ 229](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6Ait5R-3-lI)
- Growth, plateau and decline are all painful, so pain is just the signal of being alive. In training, feeling bad doesn't correlate with performance; the end state is not even consulting your feelings before acting. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- Feelings don't require action: create space between feeling and acting (be like an insulated tumbler); if an angry idea still seems good in the morning, do it. Nothing is good or bad until the end (the farmer's horse parable); ask "what would make this the best thing that ever happened?" [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- Most people fail because they spend time on everything that isn't revenue-generating; if you aren't doing outreach, content, ads or partnerships right now, nothing else matters. [▶ 235](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rRI0J8a4I9g)
- Motivation mirrors perceived deprivation; he feels more deprived relative to a $1B goal than someone chasing $10k/month. The fastest way to change behavior is to change your environment (join a great team in what you want to get good at). [▶ 241](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZKhApFCWO8)
- "Solomon" method: a weekly written chat (first hour of Monday) with his imagined 85-year-old self, the one advisor with full context, aligned incentives and equal competence. Good advisors need all three. After a vendor failure cost ~$15M, the takeaway was that the person he's becoming is the real asset; compare yourself to future you, who knows how hard you could have tried. [▶ 241](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZKhApFCWO8)
- Filter questions by whether the answer would change his behavior (simulation theory and UAPs get zero attention). For stressors, use logic, evidence, utility: what does it mean, how do you know, and why should I care. [▶ 245](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9urSNqHrCFM)
- Some problems (e.g., Leila's health issues this year) are "kick in the nuts" problems with no fix; you simply have to suffer well. These, like criticism, are life overhead and a fixed cost. [▶ 245](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9urSNqHrCFM)
- When all tasks are high-ROI, he does whichever one he feels like that day (writing vs. content), since order doesn't matter. Needing stimulants to grind is a sign he should delegate rather than push harder. Elaborate three-hour morning routines are just procrastination with a nicer name. [▶ 249](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=evNrefJmM_I)
- Before a hard conversation, ask what you want to happen and what makes that more likely, not what would make you feel better. Often the best move is to do nothing. Only play games you have a strong chance of winning; if you can't see an edge, you don't understand the game yet. [▶ 251](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f_UL-z1xgI)
- Power follows blame: whoever you blame (parents, government, employer) you've handed control of your life to. It may not be your fault, but it is your problem, so solve it. Actions work no matter how you feel about yourself; 100 calls or 500 lb are the same for everyone, which he finds freeing. [▶ 252](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KepgJld9O2w)
- Behavior follows reinforcement, not just reward: a painful act can be reinforcing if it protects someone you love, so frame hard work as duty to the people who depend on you (family, then employees). [▶ 15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDBkiBnMrHs)
- Cut friends who only talk about the past and keep those who talk about the future. Other people, even parents, want the version of you that serves them (parents tend to play not to lose); only your future self is fully aligned with your interests. [▶ 61](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DiQ3N8F1Hl8)
- Ignore other people's prescriptions for your life. They tend to want the version of you that serves them, and those closest to you can feel threatened by your success. Building your life around proving critics wrong hands them control. [▶ 66](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pt50QF6al8g)
- Networking rules: accept the first invite (turning it down kills momentum), spend about 30 minutes researching the person beforehand, and bring value. If you do a favor, over-deliver at full project scope so they feel awkward about how much you did. A half-finished free patio breeds resentment. [▶ 70](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Day0yToqeco)
- Drawing on Esther Perel: desire depends on balancing mystery and familiarity, which is a tension to manage rather than a problem to solve. Founder-plus-homemaker couples tend to drift apart and need more closeness. Couples who work together (who he says earn about 5x more) risk becoming like siblings and need more space, so he and his wife work in separate parts of the house and attend different meetings. Couples with separate careers but shared goals and values tend to sit in the middle. [▶ 91](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-TydwZMX8wM)
- Step 1, calorie target: multiply bodyweight in pounds by a factor from 7 to 21, in bands of three. The bands run from extreme cut, moderate cut (about 10-12), maintenance (about 13-15), moderate gain, up to extreme gain. Example: 200 lb at 10 is about 2,000 calories for a cut. If you lose too fast, move up a factor (e.g., to 11). [▶ 92](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fxyhIXZ6Yog)
- Every diet works the same way: keto removes carbs, low-fat removes fat, portion control shrinks everything, and intermittent fasting drops a meal. Each one just cuts calories. Keto "fails" when people add so much butter and fatty meat that total calories go up. [▶ 100](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RpqSy5V1fFQ)
- Two numbers cover about 99% of what most people need. Calories equal bodyweight in pounds times a factor from about 7 (aggressive loss) to 21 (aggressive gain); about 10-11 for weight loss and 13-15 for maintenance. Example: 200 lb at 11 is 2,200 kcal. Protein equals about 1 g per pound, so 200 g, which is roughly 2 lb of lean meat (100 g of protein per pound of lean meat). Adjust calories down if progress is too slow. [▶ 100](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RpqSy5V1fFQ)
- There are four types of trust, defined by two variables, who is at risk (you or them) and who punishes (the other person or the environment): you share a secret and they could hurt you; they share one with you; you rely on someone's word or advice and reality punishes you if they fail (e.g. not picking up your kid, bad advice); or they rely on yours. [▶ 104](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k5-57282taI)
- To end a relationship, reduce frequency and accept fewer invitations so it fades naturally; if it's close enough to need a talk, be honest and say to their face what you'd say behind their back. [▶ 163](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vVssypj7nYw)
- Nearly all criticism reduces to you don't live the way I'd prefer, which is irrelevant because it's your life; people often want you to fail to confirm their own safer path. Missing acquaintances' weddings rarely affects real friendships. [▶ 174](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqjGxVW-Ae0)
- He openly calls his view transactional: the benefits of the relationship should outweigh the costs, and the best relationships are "abundant exchanges" where both sides feel they are getting the better deal. Rules get stricter as demands on your time rise (rare lives warrant rare rules). [▶ 185](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1taVrxMFjaY)
- For hard conversations with close people, keep the other person's humanity ahead of being right, and take responsibility for being the one who changed. [▶ 185](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1taVrxMFjaY)
- Know when enough is enough: Munger aimed for independence rather than maximum wealth, spending his life doing what he was great at with his closest friend; avoid the endless race for more. [▶ 187](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-NLqtk4F4oY)
- He quit drinking because evening drinks masked unresolved anxieties; sobriety made them "loud," forcing him to resolve them, and after about six months the desire to drink faded. [▶ 199](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6ZEZWuVC8-8)
- If you're comfortable-but-mildly-miserable, either agitate the pain (he thinks about death constantly) or accept and enjoy your current life; there is honor in all work and you can choose to do any job excellently. Business, health and marriage are infinite games: the goal is to keep playing, not to "win". [▶ 231](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3e73Qn6NOo)
- Change your surroundings to change behavior (Skinner: salt the horse's mouth and it drinks). The strongest correlate of outcomes is your reference group - who you compare yourself to - so get around fitter or richer people to feel deprived and motivated. Before reacting, think two moves ahead about what your reply makes more likely. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- Mental frames he uses: the "veteran frame" (how would I feel the 1,000th time this happened? choose that now) and the "grandfather frame" (wake up as your 85-year-old self who traded everything to be young again) for gratitude and perspective. He gave up chasing happiness ("forget happiness, just do stuff") and found joy arrived later. [▶ 233](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRPChBZ0Rjo)
- Rules: if you don't both agree, don't move forward. Leave a discussion when emotionally charged and argue by text to add delay. Most fights are miscommunication, so break down what was said versus what was heard. Leila defuses his anger with warmth and he comforts her stress. His proposal was simply "it makes sense if we married"; they wed in six days, worked the next day and he tore up the prenup. [▶ 242](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NI22-qg2Hio)
- Respect lasts longer than love because it rests on facts (Leila crushed a launch right after they broke up, and stayed when he lost everything again); when emotions fade, logic remains. Create variety by deliberately being apart (separate work spaces, separate meetings). [▶ 246](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTAXjVgK-1o)
- Marriage: align on mission (where you're going), values (how you get there) and lifestyle, and accept each other fully without trying to change the other person. A coach had him check his "stats" since meeting Leila (money, fitness, energy, progress on goals); all were up. Working together means facing the same stressors, so you grow in parallel. [▶ 252](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KepgJld9O2w)

lessons.t: Decisions, risk & thinking · 66 ideas
lessons.md:
- Motivation comes from perceived deprivation, the gap between where you are and where you want to be. For money that gap is psychological, so widen it by changing who you compare yourself to (people 10x ahead, or the future you); environment shapes behavior more than willpower. [▶ 8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MNll1BaskLA)
- Money loves speed. If a wrong decision is cheap to fix, decide immediately. Moving decision deadlines from end of week to end of day can multiply your pace; unmade decisions are the heaviest load you carry, and very few decisions are truly irreversible. [▶ 29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ub1D6RQocRU)
- Think 100x, not 2x: a public CEO who grew market cap from $200M to $1.2B attended 66 in-person events in a quarter, and Hormozi was publishing about 450 content pieces a week against a peer's 7. Every result has a price tag; you can't get someone's outcome while keeping your own lifestyle. [▶ 46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDK4g5na4Jw)
- Treat each no as a yes to the thing that matters most. The people you decline usually come back once you've succeeded, and new doors open. Think of yeses as withdrawals from your energy and nos as deposits toward your goal. [▶ 69](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ueJg14gQLuc)
- Casual "quick call" and catch-up requests cost much more than their length: prep, rumination afterward, and the cost of switching tasks. He cites research that switching between tasks takes roughly four times longer than doing them one after another. [▶ 69](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ueJg14gQLuc)
- (3) Neutral-passive: "let's see if it works for me". Most people are here and make mediocre customers. (4) Negative-passive: "it probably won't work for me", which leads to half-hearted execution. (5) Negative-active: actively tries to prove it can't work because they're "special" (e.g., "calories don't affect my body"). [▶ 72](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Ju1I37jWUM)
- There are many viable routes up the mountain, but switching between them means climbing back down and starting over. Full conviction in a sensible plan beats searching for the perfect one, a trap he calls "the fallacy of the perfect pick". [▶ 74](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-UzJOk85OZI)
- Work-life balance is a personal choice, not a universal rule. If work energizes you more than time off, work more, and adjust only when you notice you've given up something you actually care about. He chose to work on his birthday because that's what he wanted. [▶ 91](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-TydwZMX8wM)
- He eats the same breakfast and lunch every day to cut decisions: a roughly 200-kcal protein bar plus a shake (about 360 kcal and 50 g protein), then a pound of turkey with half a cup of rice. That makes dinner the flexible meal, at about 3,000 kcal for maintenance. Eating extra protein keeps him full, and he takes a multivitamin instead of worrying about greens. [▶ 92](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fxyhIXZ6Yog)
- His content rules: anything works better than nothing, some things work better than others, and nothing works forever. Start, find what works best, do as much of it as you can until returns fall, then find the next thing. [▶ 97](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HVOubeXUcx0)
- The gap between knowing what you need to do and doing it is what delays your growth; the best entrepreneurs act almost the moment they know. [▶ 103](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H8QfAfCbOXs)
- Unless physics or the law prevents it, treat constraints as mental handicaps your competitors choose to live by. Reason from first principles (like Jobs demanding a device fit a given size, or Musk asking why a part needs so many bolts): what physical law stops us from hiring 100 people a day if a company 20x our size can? [▶ 122](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A248pGXTSoY)
- Be less reasonable: setting out to beat book-sales records held by presidents and royalty, he planned for redundancy (backup generators and internet, enough printed inventory, hundreds of fulfillment staff) so several things could go wrong and the goal would still be hit. Then you only need enough eyeballs and a compelling offer. Never apologize for big goals; outsized returns require betting against conventional wisdom, where you're either wrong or right and early. [▶ 122](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A248pGXTSoY)
- When choosing between paths (e.g. franchise vs private ownership), identify each path's big hairy problem and ask which you'd rather have and which you're better equipped to solve today. Every goal implies a timeline. Entrepreneurship funnels you the hardest problems nobody else wants; that's what you're paid for. [▶ 126](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q9OmYf_IlQ0)
- Tactical tip: choose activities that check several boxes at once; he lifts weights with coworkers who are friends, which covers recreation, friendship, career and health in one time block. [▶ 143](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OHu1FY1R-x0)
- 2) Laundry: about 4 hours a week (sorting, washing, folding); drop-off service at about $1.50-2 per pound, roughly $60-80/month. Wearing the same outfit daily removes decision time. [▶ 147](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3SVksBB3_YY)
- 6) Frequent travelers: semi-private flights skip security for about 3x commercial fares but a fraction of private jet costs (e.g., about $300 vs $15-20k for a short hop). All in, about $2-3k/month can reclaim about 45 hours a week; he calls it a better return than the S&P 500 because it lets you grow active income. [▶ 147](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3SVksBB3_YY)
- Tax-chasing breeds incremental thinking (saving 30%) instead of order-of-magnitude thinking (making 10-30x more); fortunes are made by taking big risks with small money and kept by taking small risks with big money. [▶ 161](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w5g0JiO7OdE)
- Reduce repeated low-stakes decisions, e.g., eating the same breakfast, lunch and dinner daily, to save mental bandwidth. [▶ 168](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bkPwFqa89gE)
- Set an alarm for bedtime rather than wake-up: go to sleep earlier and wake naturally, since you make better decisions well rested even if you can function on four hours. [▶ 168](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bkPwFqa89gE)
- Successful people keep very different schedules (one billionaire friend works 10pm-4am); find the hours you work best and protect time to think, because at higher levels decisions matter more than actions. [▶ 168](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bkPwFqa89gE)
- He defines power as how short the gap is between deciding something and it becoming real; the smaller that gap, the more effective you are as an entrepreneur. [▶ 180](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oW6JkqL6sdM)
- The trait he sees most in top-1% operators is how fast they act after making a decision, which he treats as a cause of success rather than a side effect. [▶ 180](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oW6JkqL6sdM)
- Inversion: instead of asking how to grow the business, list the fastest ways to destroy it (no one hears about you, terrible product, bad reviews), then do the opposite; humans spot threats far more easily than positives, so this surfaces better answers. [▶ 187](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-NLqtk4F4oY)
- Model the rule, not the exceptions: late-bloomer stories like Colonel Sanders exist, but most of the richest people got rich young because they decided to. [▶ 191](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aRVv5NLVRwE)
- Unifying spending rule, function over form: pay up when something works better (well-fitting flannels), go cheap when cheap works better (bulk cotton tanks). Keep the wardrobe a fixed size by tossing the lowest-utility item whenever you add one; buy favorites in multiple colors. [▶ 212](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RBR4BwOVNvs)
- Build decision algorithms (if this, then that) for recurring choices so you stop re-deciding old questions and keep mental bandwidth for new ones. [▶ 212](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RBR4BwOVNvs)
- Regret comes from imagining the upside you missed without the cost you'd have paid. Work-life balance is a preference trade-off (cookies vs a six-pack); dissatisfaction comes from wanting both, so want less or trade more. [▶ 222](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jqo0lVveh98)
- Separate preparation (work directly tied to the task, like researching an audience) from rituals and morning routines that don't move the needle; start working right after waking and between tasks without warm-up ceremonies. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- His life thesis, formed during the idle year of the gym-business sale: hard work itself is the goal, not "work hard so that X". Aim to empty the tank (Jesse Itzler's zero sign); only you know whether you held back. Marry it with direction: choose the input most correlated with your outcome, then put blinders on. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- Your calendar predicts your future better than your bank account; giving free time to anyone who asks surrenders your only currency. Today's results reflect work from 6-12 months ago. [▶ 232](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WO5m-roVzjg)
- The difference between self-made winners and others who started with nothing is resourcefulness, not resources; giving power to circumstances or other people casts power outside yourself. Selling is helping people reclaim that power. [▶ 233](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRPChBZ0Rjo)
- Make bets with incomplete information: check reversibility and recovery time, and place smaller directional bets before big ones. [▶ 235](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rRI0J8a4I9g)
- Model what successful people did at your stage, not what they do now (billionaires fly private as an effect, not a cause). He regrets not recording any of his 4,000+ in-person sales. [▶ 236](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gT2bk52F9bg)
- Each time his monthly income gained a zero, it came from giving up something everyone praised (a good job, his gyms) for something better that didn't exist yet. [▶ 239](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2IoKsGLpGys)
- Marriage removed the mental bandwidth he'd spent on dating, and income went from a few hundred thousand to a few million a month within about 12 months. He opposes side hustles: shower and drive time go to the main thing, and it's arrogant to think you can split attention and beat people who are all-in. [▶ 242](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NI22-qg2Hio)
- Best morning routine for ambitious financial goals: minimize the time between waking and starting work. [▶ 248](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPV7Sn-POlM)
- Your reference group shapes your outcomes; ask of every person and activity whether it makes hitting your goal more or less likely. Expect a lonely chapter between old and new friend groups; criticism is often a leading indicator of progress. [▶ 7](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aFoMYz_jWcs)
- Choose a spouse who supports your ambitions even if they do not fully agree; asking a partner for permission rather than support breeds resentment. Take advice on getting rich only from people who are rich, and value your own opinion over others'. [▶ 19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ySuYdJ0H4s)
- Choosing a partner is probably the biggest decision you'll make, because over your life your spouse ends up taking most of your time. He cites a roughly 0.71 correlation between well-being and relationship strength, yet people put more thought into buying a car. [▶ 23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jiCGLDhUCHY)
- His good-day formula: eat with people he likes, lift with people he likes, write something. The upgrade was removing time pressure (fewer hard stops in the schedule), which he decided was worth giving up some money for. [▶ 45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFElGv5ZmRM)
- When you want time together but your partner is in a busy season, accept that you can want something without getting it and make your own plans. Trading off intense seasons builds space to miss each other, which makes the time together better. [▶ 60](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCgr7jT7JLA)
- Parents have huge influence because they max out all four: they control resources, have countless reinforcement cycles with you, often have credibility, and look and think like you. [▶ 68](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dMZ-n2KSlxE)
- "Family obligations" are actually choices and trade-offs. Others, family included, often want the version of you that serves them. Trying to satisfy both their goals and yours tends to achieve neither, so pursue yours fully in the short term for the long-term win. [▶ 69](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ueJg14gQLuc)
- Stop chasing happiness. Like hunger or sleep, it never stays satisfied, and making it a goal places it outside you. The people most fixated on it tend to be the least content and spend all day thinking about themselves. Aim to be useful to others instead; that combines service and self-improvement, and he argues it fits men especially, since usefulness earns respect and status. [▶ 89](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4evdxF5G0s)
- Two relationship models he has seen work long term for entrepreneurs: partners building together, and "cheerleader and quarterback" with fully shared goals. A real cheerleader doesn't ask the quarterback to leave the game when it's on the line. Many couples who think they're in the second model are actually undermining each other. [▶ 91](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-TydwZMX8wM)
- Behavioral definition: trusting someone means making yourself punishable by them, betting that they won't use what you gave them (a secret, information, your word) against you. [▶ 104](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k5-57282taI)
- Before extending material trust, ask two questions: do they have a track record of protecting what they've been given, and does betraying you cost them more than protecting you? Proceed only if both are yes. [▶ 104](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k5-57282taI)
- Why trust at all: a relationship's ceiling depends on how much context each person has about the other; you can't help someone you know nothing about. But more context also means more ability to hurt you, and short-term incentives (like winning an argument) can tempt people to betray long-term relationships. [▶ 104](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k5-57282taI)
- Fame's biggest pro is being able to recruit anyone; the cost is privacy and being treated as permanently on the record. It's irreversible like a tattoo, so choose it deliberately; if you don't want it, grow the business by other means. He estimates his social presence could be worth around a billion dollars if monetized, e.g. by letting his audience invest. [▶ 123](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lEIqyLE4iOY)
- Decision tools: protect your reputation (you only get one name), and use the 85-year-old self test, asking whether your older self would care about the extra money versus the life you sacrificed. [▶ 161](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w5g0JiO7OdE)
- Getting rid of accumulated stuff and clutter frees up attention, like the relief of cleaning out a garage, which improves decision quality. [▶ 168](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bkPwFqa89gE)
- Reputation over everything: trust is earned in drops and lost in buckets; he turns down deals adjacent to reputationally risky industries, and is wary of partners who loudly claim to value morals above money. [▶ 169](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-k0_pQJ1fY)
- Curate your reference group: drop friends who aren't happy when you win; motivation scales with the gap between you and your peers, which is partly why married men with kids tend to earn more. [▶ 169](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-k0_pQJ1fY)
- Don't take advice from people with smaller dreams for you than your own; parents usually optimize for you being safe and stable, a different risk tolerance rather than malice. [▶ 174](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqjGxVW-Ae0)
- Test each relationship by whether it makes your long-term goal more likely; if not, decide whether the relationship matters more than the goal. He chose the goal and found a new tier of friends appeared as he leveled up. [▶ 185](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1taVrxMFjaY)
- Having tried everything: flying private is nice but very expensive; exotic cars are not worth it (the enjoyment fades within a couple of weeks; he regrets buying after being told he was too cheap); fancy restaurants are mainly worth it for dressing up on date night; designer clothes add nothing. [▶ 200](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vKnAWYqMJ10)
- Mass-market products are often better because they are heavily tested; a rented Chevy Suburban's interface beat his far pricier Bentley's. [▶ 200](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vKnAWYqMJ10)
- Network arbitrage: a founder who lived beyond his means in Alex's luxury building pitched him in the elevator and funded his software company through neighbors; risky, but access to wealthy people paid off. [▶ 203](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ovL6Z5z0jxQ)
- After selling his companies, two exotic cars and a $4M Austin house, he lived from one bag for about 9 months, renting high-end homes ($50-100K/month) to reset and decide where to live. He frames life in 3-5 year seasons. [▶ 212](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RBR4BwOVNvs)
- Mortality is his main decision tool: most choices don't matter in the long run, and remembering death frees you from others' expectations. Life satisfaction is lowest from 20s to mid-40s and rises when people accept life is short. Even his great-great-grandfather with 400 children left no legacy he can name, so he doesn't chase legacy. [▶ 237](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3iPYrHhkEc)
- Who you marry is the most important decision you make: time with spouse and coworkers rises through life while time with family and friends falls, and relationship quality correlates about 0.71 with subjective well-being. Pick a partner like he picks gear, obsessively. [▶ 242](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NI22-qg2Hio)
- People without values need rules (date nights, no work talk); led by values, you allocate attention naturally. Problems come from mismatched expectations between partners, not from others' norms; never compare your relationship to anyone else's. Buffett's tip for marriage was low expectations; two whole people who choose each other beat two halves. [▶ 242](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NI22-qg2Hio)
- Working with his wife Leila: they split decisions by domain (she owns people/talent calls, he owns marketing/brand angles) and talk through big strategic calls until they agree. When the relationship needs attention, whoever notices says so and the other corrects, without keeping score. [▶ 245](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9urSNqHrCFM)
- Marriage made him more money: attention no longer goes to chasing partners, and a higher exit barrier gave the security to take big risks; you trade novelty for loyalty. He measures love by how much you will endure to keep it. Pick a partner on aligned mission, values and interests. [▶ 246](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTAXjVgK-1o)
- After selling his companies he took most of a year off, with fine dining and travel, and felt empty. His conclusion: passive income is overrated, and what you actually want is the option to choose engaging work. He accepts that he simply loves working and ignores other people's ideas of balance. [▶ 250](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4KfuQwB5rIs)

lessons.t: Time, energy & health · 45 ideas
lessons.md:
- For young men (roughly 16-28) he argues for normalizing six 12-hour workdays a week: when young you have little utility but lots of energy, so trade energy for experience. Resourcefulness beats resources; use what you have. [▶ 7](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aFoMYz_jWcs)
- Passion is often an excuse that hides low tolerance for difficulty; business funnels the hardest problems to the owner. Putting yourself in no-exit situations helps (a signed lease holding all his savings forced him to make the gym work). [▶ 15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDBkiBnMrHs)
- Extraordinary results come from ordinary actions repeated for extraordinary lengths of time; commitment to the action, not the action, is what is remarkable. [▶ 16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cq8GyLrEuAk)
- Productivity is money out per unit of time in. Building on Paul Graham's essay, there are two schedules: managers split the day into 20+ small slots (15-90 minutes) where an empty slot is wasted, and makers (coders, editors, writers, founders building assets) need a few 4-6 hour blocks where an empty calendar is the most productive day. [▶ 20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GIRkQQHzsxI)
- Makers should explain how they work, set fixed meeting windows (e.g. two afternoons a week), batch as many meetings as possible into any block that gets broken anyway, tell people when they will be slow to reply, and genuinely produce during protected time so trust is earned. [▶ 20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GIRkQQHzsxI)
- You can beat most people simply by working without needing an immediate reward. Work ethic multiplied by time is the most powerful money-making combination. Going from good to great takes so much work that you can only be great at one or two things. [▶ 31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ln24y0FPJHo)
- Every incoming message carries an implied request for a reply. Having the time to reply doesn't create an obligation; with 500,000 texts you obviously couldn't reply to all, so the obligation never existed. During his build phase he largely stopped replying. [▶ 41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lRyGIzW9d9k)
- Resilience means returning to baseline behavior quickly; toughness is how much it takes before you drop; a third factor is how deep you fall. Don't let one bad event snowball into your marriage, parenting and other projects; the "second arrow" (your reaction) is optional, and worrying about futures that haven't happened is mostly wasted time. [▶ 45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFElGv5ZmRM)
- Contrarian: once you earn more than about $15/hour, buy takeout instead of cooking. Two $10 meals a day costs about $50/week more than groceries, and the time saved on shopping, cooking and cleaning is worth more. [▶ 51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q6SdmgIji30)
- Maker time versus manager time: makers need 4-6 hour uninterrupted blocks (only about 14 a week), and one meeting can ruin a whole block; manager time is 5-15 minute slots best packed back to back. Don't mix the two; he does four maker days and one packed manager day each week. [▶ 57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gD0X-PLax5I)
- Money is bottled time, and its value per hour changes as you get richer ($100 might be 4 hours for one person and 4 minutes for another). Keep reviewing your calendar for trades that buy back low-value hours. [▶ 59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oZ-H_TjSzok)
- Depending on rituals and crutches (alcohol, cannabis or pills to sleep, coffee to function, rigid morning routines) makes you fragile. A competitor only has to disrupt your routine to knock you off for the day. [▶ 64](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ErWpi_91b70)
- Seinfeld-style time blocks: during the block you don't have to produce, but you can't do anything except the work. Make room for nothing else, and change your environment rather than counting on willpower. [▶ 69](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ueJg14gQLuc)
- Business is an infinite game that has run since ancient merchants. Nobody remembers past "number ones", and the players get swapped every century. The only thing that counts as winning is staying in the game. [▶ 71](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WOZGZK7K-Jo)
- Treat time as an asset. The 5-9am and 5-9pm windows outside your job (about 8 hours) are where you get ahead, so stop doom-scrolling in them. Work hours pay for today; those hours build tomorrow. [▶ 85](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EonibwnAEME)
- Buy back time: the average person spends about 96 hours a month on food, cleaning and laundry, which you can outsource for about $1,500 a month (roughly $15/hour); if you earn more than that working on your business, it's worth it, but only if you spend the reclaimed hours on the constraint. [▶ 140](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h6y0nYVZgwE)
- Fat pitches come only a few times in life; when things suddenly get easy, push harder rather than coasting, accepting short-term sacrifice. [▶ 157](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ULGT0Qpglek)
- Many productivity and biohacking routines are really procrastination dressed up as productivity; he keeps routines minimal so more time goes to actual work. [▶ 168](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bkPwFqa89gE)
- Take ownership: it may not be your fault, but it's your problem and nobody is coming to save you; starting is the perfect condition, so use what you have. [▶ 169](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-k0_pQJ1fY)
- Determination beats intelligence (citing Paul Graham), and behaviorally it's a long extinction curve: how many times you keep acting without results, trying the door, the window, the back, the phone, until you get in. [▶ 174](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqjGxVW-Ae0)
- For recurring work, use roughly a 1:4 prep-to-event ratio (15 minutes before a 60-minute meeting, 2 hours before an 8-hour day), which can shrink toward 1:10 with experience; review who is attending, background, agenda and the problem to solve. [▶ 183](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m5ordaa7NN4)
- Cramming has high ROI in business: prep right before the event (reverse Parkinson's law) because proximity makes it most useful for one-off meetings and presentations. [▶ 183](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m5ordaa7NN4)
- Game-theory view: in any new system the most adaptable player wins, and youth brings the most neuroplasticity, energy and flexibility. Leaving a default path only gets harder with time. [▶ 191](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aRVv5NLVRwE)
- Invert the problem: the worst morning routine would be long, multi-step, mentally draining and something you can't work without, which describes many guru routines. [▶ 214](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PFKGHL1MqkU)
- Delay of gratification scales outcomes: if you can wait a year you can avoid financial need; a decade puts you above the 1%; a lifetime can change the world. You can tell how successful someone will be by the time horizon and money amounts they talk in. [▶ 233](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRPChBZ0Rjo)
- He avoids rigid rules and routine superstition; a three-hour morning routine could be three more hours of work. The result only cares whether you did the work (100 calls or posts), regardless of other vices. Routines among the wealthy vary so much that they can't be what matters. [▶ 234](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tigt75AcLLA)
- Schedule: wakes at 4-5am without an alarm, sleeps 9-10pm, deep work until ~11am, meetings until 3-4pm. [▶ 239](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2IoKsGLpGys)
- Avoid crutches and superstitions (sleep scores, rituals you can't function without), since any crutch you depend on can be knocked out. He doesn't use an alarm and chews nicotine gum only while working, pairing a stimulant with work. [▶ 241](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZKhApFCWO8)
- Schedule: wakes without an alarm, solo creative work (books, content, portfolio fixes) in the first half of the day, meetings in the second half, then a 45-minute walk to debrief with Leila. [▶ 242](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NI22-qg2Hio)
- Daily routine then: 5am-1pm on his own work, meetings 1-4:30pm, then gym and done. Goal: $10B portfolio; mission: make real business knowledge available to everyone, documenting the path as he grows. [▶ 244](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sdd4BST87ks)
- Energy tactics: he does not sacrifice sleep, but about six hours (10pm-4am) works for him; he averaged about five hours for six weeks before the launch. He trains full body most days for two-plus hours because he enjoys it, and enjoys workouts most with no deadline and with partners for accountability. [▶ 245](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9urSNqHrCFM)
- Go on a new information diet and ignore advice from people who do not have bigger dreams for you; skeptics are right about most attempts but wrong about the one that works. Balance can be across a lifetime or within a family unit rather than daily. [▶ 4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YFA8AS5Cu2w)
- Pay a premium for a convenient micro-location (near the gym, the highway and cheap food, ideally walkable); more roommates in a good area beats fewer in a bad one. [▶ 51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q6SdmgIji30)
- "There are no social obligations, only social consequences." If people stop inviting you because you skip events you didn't want to go to, you save time now and later. [▶ 56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vhOV_Od0A3M)
- The "bosses" you face pile up as you grow: yourself, then doubtful friends and family, then recruiting and leading employees, then market shifts and regulators. People often cheer you on until you overtake them, as he found when gym clients turned snarky once he succeeded. Hold on to the friends who really want you to win. [▶ 65](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=prj1bnTAM8A)
- Increase your luck surface by getting out and meeting people (coffee shops, gyms) rather than staying home. The fastest way to change your life is to change who is around you, so move to the hub for your field (finance in NYC, film in Hollywood, politics in DC). [▶ 85](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EonibwnAEME)
- Step 2, protein: eat about 1 g per pound of bodyweight (200 g for 200 lb). A pound of lean meat (turkey, white fish, lean beef, shrimp) gives roughly 100 g of protein, so that's about 2 lb a day if it all came from meat. [▶ 92](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fxyhIXZ6Yog)
- Ten competing life areas: community, romance/partner, parenting, extended family, recreation, friends, career, physical health, spiritual health, personal growth. Time is zero-sum (about 70 minutes a day each if split evenly), so rank them yourself; others will criticize a ranking that differs from theirs. [▶ 143](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OHu1FY1R-x0)
- One-time environment fixes with lasting returns: cool room (they sleep at about 67°F), good ventilation/AC, remove all LED and screen light (ideally phone out of the room), full blackout curtains plus an eye mask, a weighted blanket around 10% of bodyweight, a quality mattress and pillow (buy several and keep the best), white noise or earplugs, and consider separate bedrooms if a partner disrupts sleep. He cites a stat that one extra hour of sleep adds more happiness than an extra $70K a year. [▶ 192](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=55H71isO_Bo)
- Cut caffeine after about 10am: its half-life is ~6 hours, so a large morning dose is still meaningfully present at bedtime; heavy users who "sleep fine" have usually built tolerance. [▶ 192](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=55H71isO_Bo)
- Choosing where to live: most of daily life happens within walking distance, so his must-haves nearby were nature, restaurants, a great gym and a grocery store, plus home features (water or mountain view, fast Wi-Fi, office/studio, 3+ bedrooms, outdoor space). [▶ 212](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RBR4BwOVNvs)
- Marriage rule: if both don't agree, they don't do it. The one time he overrode Leila (ALAN software) it hit $1.7M/month in six months but had flaws she had foreseen. They have fully joint finances. [▶ 237](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3iPYrHhkEc)
- After a year of doing nothing in 2021 he was miserable; he works to create the option to work, not to stop. Couples working together earn far more but must create space (separate meetings) to avoid becoming siblings; cheerleaders who pull the quarterback out mid-game are sabotaging. [▶ 239](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2IoKsGLpGys)
- He doesn't police Leila's spending since it doesn't affect their goals; his own indulgence is gym equipment. He bought the old 36,000 sq ft UFC headquarters for studios and a gym after seeing Dave Ramsey and others put about 20 hours a week into content, versus his half-day. [▶ 241](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZKhApFCWO8)
- Meaning is self-generated: one blunt test is that whatever keeps you living is your meaning, and it can change over time. [▶ 245](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9urSNqHrCFM)

lessons.t: Money, status & happiness · 19 ideas
lessons.md:
- Growth requires stretching past comfort, so the fastest-growing stretches tend to be the most miserable. You can't want progress and also expect an easy life. Be "happy but not satisfied": content with the process, never complacent. His own conclusion after a year off was that the work itself is the goal. [▶ 24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MzAIP_WJ-jE)
- Step one out of poverty is ownership: everything up to now is your fault. Whatever you blame (a parent, politics, your ZIP code) gains power over you, and blaming creates self-confirming evidence. You can't both want to improve and hold onto blame; you can be right or you can be rich. [▶ 32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oys_fv25SYM)
- Turn "no one can sell like me" into the solvable question "How do I find someone who can sell like me?" Be wary of self-imposed rules like "we can't charge more" or "we can't pay that much, it's not industry standard"; the average business owner earns modest money by copying peers. Doing what everyone else does guarantees commoditization (Henry Ford paid above market to get the best workers). [▶ 120](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aUnorufFIq8)
- Every entrepreneur has enough ideas to kill their business. Keep a "big list of ideas" document, write each idea up fully, and revisit only when the team is rested; ideas you forget weren't good, and ones that keep nagging get fleshed out and released at the pace the business can handle. Waiting can be the most profitable move. [▶ 130](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=spXH1kJ6q-Q)
- Useful definitions: shame is breaking other people's rules, guilt is breaking your own, and calling something cringe is usually a defensive status move by someone who senses you are rising relative to them. [▶ 155](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yb2cLMMuMdQ)
- Seeing a disorganized operator stuck at $300-400k/month convinced him and Leila they could do it too; use others' success as fuel, and within six months they hit $1M/month. [▶ 157](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ULGT0Qpglek)
- Keep high minimum standards and larger measuring sticks for money, and wait or take more shots rather than accepting below-standard offers. [▶ 169](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-k0_pQJ1fY)
- Ignore critics who aren't where you want to be: wealthier people don't mock saving and fitter people don't mock dieting, so criticism from people going nowhere is often a sign you're on the right path; take advice only from people whose lives you'd swap for, and consume content from them if none are nearby. [▶ 174](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqjGxVW-Ae0)
- You are broke because you aren't doing the activities that build wealth, not because you lack passion; fuel those activities however works for you. Good outcomes can come from negative motivation. [▶ 215](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDDFezF7OTA)
- People forget you weeks after you die, so give little weight to opinions from anyone without both a stake in your success and the context to advise. [▶ 16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cq8GyLrEuAk)
- In 2021 he lived off company cash flow and did nothing, and it was miserable, especially once he realized he couldn't spend the money anyway. His conclusion: work to create options, including the option to keep working, not to stop working. Returning to building Acquisition.com brought the joy back. [▶ 91](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-TydwZMX8wM)
- Handle obligations by telling the truth (I don't want to come because X drinks too much and we always argue), attend conditionally (I'll come but won't engage with a particular person), or send money for gifts instead; honest answers can't be argued with the way excuses can. [▶ 176](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OvEfWrDOfNk)
- The wealthiest people keep pristine environments and high standards for who's around them; your standards should rise as you grow, and if someone gets upset, stay calm like a rock and don't change your behavior. [▶ 176](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OvEfWrDOfNk)
- In paid rooms, give far more than you take (he would spend hours reviewing peers' sales processes) so others reciprocate with their expertise and point you to the best resources; being around people ahead of you removes the mystique of their success. [▶ 179](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BQ3whjWG3M)
- In competitive peer groups, rising status makes others look worse by comparison, so some will try to pull you down with gossip, guilt or old labels; they are not necessarily bad people, just not helping your goal. [▶ 185](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1taVrxMFjaY)
- People often want the version of you that serves them, not your best version; family and especially a spouse should be most aligned, acting as your strongest ally who never resents your success. [▶ 185](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1taVrxMFjaY)
- Happiness equals what you have divided by what you want; shrinking your wants increases abundance and, by extension, your income-to-expense ratio. [▶ 200](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vKnAWYqMJ10)
- Joy is internal while happiness depends on circumstances. It's easier to fix what you hate (job, city, relationship) than to name what brings joy; use inversion by asking how you'd ruin your life and doing the opposite. [▶ 237](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3iPYrHhkEc)
- At the top, money is mostly about status (you can only eat so much), and he argues men chase money largely because many women value resources in a mate; people would get fit if attraction depended on it. [▶ 248](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPV7Sn-POlM)

lessons.t: Relationships, family & people · 19 ideas
lessons.md:
- Define winning as impressing your future self, not comparing to people around you (you get complacent comparing down and excuses do not help comparing up). [▶ 8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MNll1BaskLA)
- He paid a coach for nine months for 90 minutes a day just to examine where his attention went; this exposed toxic relationships and unresolved "open loops," and closing them freed attention, after which his business took off. [▶ 199](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6ZEZWuVC8-8)
- Disprove "millionaires all do X" by finding one counterexample: plenty don't wake early or have seven income streams, and a friend does ~$70M/year in unglamorous janitorial services. [▶ 214](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PFKGHL1MqkU)
- Low expectations plus high commitment: assume your partner may not change (or might even get worse) and commit anyway, provided core values stay aligned. Don't blow small annoyances out of proportion, and accept the downsides that come with your partner's strengths. [▶ 60](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCgr7jT7JLA)
- The strongest position in a relationship is not needing anything back. Build up goodwill before you need it ("dig the well before you're thirsty") so you have favors to call in when you make your move. [▶ 70](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Day0yToqeco)
- Youth is about keeping options open, adulthood about commitment, i.e., walking through one-way doors (marriage, children). Options are worthless until exercised; hoarding them is another form of endlessly delaying gratification. [▶ 143](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OHu1FY1R-x0)
- Marriage and partnership rule: if you don't agree, don't move forward; almost nothing is truly urgent, and the first question is what information each person is using. [▶ 157](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ULGT0Qpglek)
- He views life in 3-5 year seasons (high school, college, early career) and keeps a very small inner circle, letting relationships go when they no longer fit who he's becoming, which he credits for growing quickly. [▶ 163](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vVssypj7nYw)
- How much you love someone shows in what you'll give up to keep the relationship; ask not whether you love your friends but which ones you'd sacrifice most for. [▶ 163](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vVssypj7nYw)
- Letting go of a misaligned friend frees them to find someone who wants the same things (e.g., drinking and fantasy football), which can be kinder for both. [▶ 163](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vVssypj7nYw)
- View life through game design: you're playing several games at once (business, fitness, relationships); identify who defines the winning criteria, whether it's clearly defined, and whether you'd want the prize if you won. [▶ 165](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P14HA83uNJE)
- He skips going home for the holidays because the old environment pulls him back toward who he used to be; if you love your family and it's a highlight of your year, go, but you're allowed to miss it. [▶ 176](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OvEfWrDOfNk)
- His one-strike rule: anyone who resents your wins, openly or quietly, should be out. Real friends root for you to your face and, especially, behind your back. [▶ 185](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1taVrxMFjaY)
- When told "you've changed," simply agree, and accept that others may not want to change; growth means change, and friendships can come in seasons that end without hostility. [▶ 185](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1taVrxMFjaY)
- Reframe "burning bridges" as pruning a tree so it can grow; most misaligned friendships can simply fade by reducing contact frequency. [▶ 185](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1taVrxMFjaY)
- Friends need not chase greatness themselves if they support yours; he wants to admire something in every friend, like a friend committed to excellence in a completely different craft. [▶ 185](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1taVrxMFjaY)
- Leaving his prestigious consulting job meant disappointing his father; he frames maturity as valuing your own opinion of yourself above family members' opinions. [▶ 198](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6ySRKgXBcO0)
- Don't hunt for passion: you suck at anything new, you like what you're good at, so sucking comes first. A friend left fitness for a cookie shop because his passion was excellence itself. Make daily excellence and repetition the win. [▶ 241](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZKhApFCWO8)
- Behaviorist lens: people repeat what has been rewarded, and a "trigger" is just the situation in which a rewarded behavior shows up again (e.g., his anger got rewarded when his wife's crying stopped). Kids' tantrums persist because a tantrum once worked. Immediate rewards beat delayed ones, which is why apps hook people. [▶ 251](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f_UL-z1xgI)

lessons.t: Purpose & meaning · 4 ideas
lessons.md:
- The best diet, spouse, or business is the one you stick with; persistence matters more than picking the perfect option. Test whether you own a business or it owns you: if your phone rings when something breaks, you're the CEO, not a passive owner, so you can't really run two. [▶ 142](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F84olnKkseM)
- Memory is biased: punishment's sting fades quickly while rewards linger (like vowing never to drink again, then drinking next weekend), so deliberately remind yourself why you left. [▶ 176](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OvEfWrDOfNk)
- His edge is defining vague terms (like "value" or "grow my business") into concrete parts, e.g. growth = get more customers or make each worth more, then pick from the eight ways to get customers. Asking "why can't we?" without knowing the rules drives innovation. [▶ 231](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3e73Qn6NOo)
- On-the-go: original beef jerky (about 60 g protein / 480 kcal per bag) and light string cheese. Benchmark leanness against a protein scoop (about 120 kcal per 24 g protein). Diet staples: thawed pre-cooked shrimp with cocktail sauce (essentially pure protein); lean ground beef with microwave riced cauliflower and a light-mayo/sriracha/sweetener sauce, dipping the utensil to stretch the sauce. [▶ 38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hGX_z5rXRlU)

lessons.t: More · 57 ideas
lessons.md:
- Make the action the goal (did I post, did I do my reach-outs today); if you do them, you succeeded that day regardless of outcome. [▶ 11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7ITff1fIbSc)
- Pull the future forward: replace arbitrary weekly deadlines with actual task durations (a 3-4 hour task due by noon, the next by end of day), then ask how to shorten, automate or delegate each step. [▶ 18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6KqndZuN_Yk)
- Uses Munger-style inversion: list 28 ways to stay poor, then do the opposite; since brains spot threats more easily than solutions, avoiding the obvious mistakes makes you succeed almost by default. [▶ 19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ySuYdJ0H4s)
- Keep promises to yourself and others; self-respect is the hardest reputation to rebuild. Doing "your best" is irrelevant if it falls short of what is required, so improve until your best exceeds the requirement. [▶ 19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ySuYdJ0H4s)
- Impostor syndrome comes from posturing. State the facts and tell the truth; if the truth isn't impressive, work until it is. [▶ 29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ub1D6RQocRU)
- His seven levels for weighing advice, lowest to highest: strangers' comments; acquaintances who don't have what you want; someone who knows someone who got there; someone who has been there; someone who took someone else there; someone who took someone like you to exactly your goal; someone who has done that repeatedly. [▶ 31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ln24y0FPJHo)
- Step two is to use what you have, not what you wish you had. For him that was anger at the thought of proving the people back home right, not passion. You can start from anger, sadness or shame; what matters is taking the next step. [▶ 32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oys_fv25SYM)
- If you do go, maximize it: take 18-21 credits, use summer school, aim to graduate early or with a double degree, and join clubs to increase how many people you meet (your "luck surface area"). [▶ 43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nxL4ZfVqKLI)
- In a hard season, aim for a good day (or even just good moments); stringing good days together turns the season around. Long obstacles that come with big goals need small daily progress that only shows up over 30-90 days. [▶ 45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFElGv5ZmRM)
- Even terrible experiences pay off through inversion: list everything that made it bad and do the opposite. So every experience has a positive return. [▶ 72](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Ju1I37jWUM)
- Mental toughness defined: the likelihood that something bad (anything against your preferences) changes your behavior in a way that works against your goals. That makes it a degree you can measure and improve, not a trait you either have or lack. [▶ 88](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SE9_1PYsaP0)
- Six stages of response: normal baseline, the trigger, how far you drop, how long you stay down, the recovery, and whether you stabilize above or below where you started. These map onto four separate parts of mental toughness. [▶ 88](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SE9_1PYsaP0)
